text.en:
New Guinea lies at the northern edge of the Australian plate. Uplift and faulting formed mountain ranges that divide river basins, while coastal plains, islands and reefs support different ways of obtaining food and moving between places. Western Papua includes the western part of this island and its surrounding islands.

During the Ice Age, lower sea levels joined New Guinea, Australia and the Aru Islands into Sahul. Waigeo and other islands to the northwest remained separated by deep water. Reaching them required sea crossings. These landscapes give the settlement histories below their geographical context.

Mountain ranges, lowland floodplains and island channels created different conditions for travel and settlement. A highland garden, a southern sago forest and a reef fishery depend on different skills and seasonal knowledge. The same geography also helps explain why neighbouring regions developed distinct languages and institutions while remaining connected through exchange. Papua’s history begins with people using these environments, not with a single culture spreading across an empty island. Sources: Tectonics of the New Guinea region Baldwin, Fitzgerald & Webb · 2012 https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-earth-040809-152540; West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea
text.pmy:
Nugini berada di tepi utara lempeng Australia. Pengangkatan dan patahan membentuk pegunungan yang membagi daerah aliran sungai, sementara dataran pesisir, pulau, dan terumbu mendukung cara memperoleh pangan serta berpindah yang berbeda. Papua bagian barat mencakup bagian barat pulau ini beserta pulau-pulau sekitarnya.

Pada Zaman Es, permukaan laut yang lebih rendah menyatukan Nugini, Australia, dan Kepulauan Aru menjadi Sahul. Waigeo dan pulau lain di barat laut tetap terpisah oleh perairan dalam sehingga perlu dicapai melalui penyeberangan laut. Bentang ini menjadi konteks geografis bagi riwayat permukiman berikutnya.

Pegunungan, dataran banjir dan selat antarpulau membentuk kondisi perjalanan serta permukiman yang berbeda. Kebun di pegunungan, hutan sagu di selatan dan perikanan terumbu memerlukan keterampilan serta pengetahuan musim yang berlainan. Bentang ini juga membantu menjelaskan mengapa wilayah bertetangga memiliki bahasa dan lembaga berbeda sambil tetap terhubung melalui pertukaran. Sejarah Papua berawal dari manusia yang menggunakan lingkungan tersebut, bukan satu kebudayaan yang menyebar di pulau kosong. Sumber: Tectonics of the New Guinea region Baldwin, Fitzgerald & Webb · 2012 https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-earth-040809-152540; West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea

text.en:
During periods of lower sea level, New Guinea, Australia and the Aru Islands formed the connected landmass called Sahul. Getting there from the islands to its west still required water crossings. Archaeological sites help investigate these journeys, but do not establish one exclusive route or one founding population.

The modern coastline is a poor guide to every early settlement. Sites once near a shore may now be inland, while others are submerged. Reconstructions depend on the period studied and local land movement as well as global sea level.

The land connection made movement between southern New Guinea and northern Australia possible without crossing today’s Torres Strait. To the west, deep channels still separated Sahul from Wallacea and islands such as Waigeo. People approaching the region therefore needed knowledge of boats, currents and island resources. Evidence from caves on both sides of these channels allows researchers to compare island settlement with occupation on the connected mainland, rather than assume that a modern national border divided those early journeys. Sources: West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea
text.pmy:
Ketika permukaan laut lebih rendah, Nugini, Australia, dan Kepulauan Aru terhubung sebagai daratan Sahul. Perjalanan dari pulau-pulau di sebelah barat tetap memerlukan penyeberangan laut. Situs arkeologi membantu menelusuri perjalanan tersebut, tetapi tidak membuktikan satu-satunya rute atau satu kelompok pendiri.

Garis pantai sekarang tidak selalu menjadi petunjuk yang tepat bagi permukiman awal. Situs yang dahulu dekat pantai bisa berada di pedalaman, sementara situs lain terendam. Rekonstruksi bergantung pada periode, pergerakan daratan setempat, dan perubahan permukaan laut.

Hubungan darat memungkinkan perjalanan antara selatan Nugini dan utara Australia tanpa menyeberangi Selat Torres seperti sekarang. Di sebelah barat, laut dalam tetap memisahkan Sahul dari Wallacea serta pulau seperti Waigeo. Manusia yang mendekati kawasan ini memerlukan pengetahuan tentang perahu, arus dan sumber daya pulau. Temuan gua di kedua sisi perairan memungkinkan perbandingan kehidupan pulau dengan permukiman di daratan yang tersambung. Batas negara sekarang belum membagi perjalanan tersebut. Sumber: West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea

text.en:
A worked piece of tree resin from Mololo Cave on Waigeo was radiocarbon dated to approximately 55,000–50,000 years ago. The find supplies direct evidence of plant use by people living on an island near the northwestern edge of New Guinea. Its manufacture involved collecting and processing resin rather than simply carrying an unmodified natural object into the cave.

Waigeo remained separated from Sahul by deep water even when sea levels were lower. Settlement therefore involved crossings between islands as well as movement over land. The researchers combine the cave evidence with reconstructed coastlines to examine possible journeys into the wider region; the find establishes activity at Mololo, not one definitive migration route.

Resin preserves a form of work that stone tools alone would miss: selecting a useful tree product, gathering it and changing its form. The cave’s long sequence connects this early plant technology with later use of forest and marine resources. Waigeo was consequently more than a stepping stone on a migration map. People stayed, acquired detailed knowledge of its resources and maintained an island way of life while conditions around the coast changed. Sources: Oldest plant artefact found outside Africa reveals Pacific’s role in early human migration University of Oxford · 2024 https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2024-08-15-oldest-plant-artefact-found-outside-africa-reveals-pacifics-role-early-human; Mololo Cave study Antiquity · 2024 https://doi.org/10.15184/aqy.2024.83
text.pmy:
Potongan resin pohon yang diolah dari Gua Mololo, Waigeo, bertanggal radiokarbon sekitar 55.000–50.000 tahun lalu. Temuan ini menjadi bukti langsung pemanfaatan tumbuhan oleh orang yang hidup di pulau dekat tepi barat laut Nugini. Pembuatannya mencakup pengumpulan serta pengolahan resin, bukan sekadar membawa benda alam tanpa perubahan ke dalam gua.

Waigeo tetap terpisah dari Sahul oleh perairan dalam ketika permukaan laut lebih rendah. Permukiman dengan demikian melibatkan penyeberangan antarpulau sekaligus perpindahan darat. Peneliti memadukan bukti gua dengan rekonstruksi garis pantai untuk mengkaji kemungkinan perjalanan ke kawasan lebih luas; temuan ini menetapkan aktivitas di Mololo, bukan satu jalur migrasi yang pasti.

Resin menyimpan jejak pekerjaan yang tidak terlihat dari alat batu saja: memilih hasil pohon yang berguna, mengambilnya dan mengolah bentuknya. Urutan lapisan gua menghubungkan teknologi tumbuhan awal ini dengan penggunaan hutan serta sumber daya laut pada masa berikutnya. Waigeo bukan sekadar persinggahan pada peta migrasi. Manusia tinggal, mengenali sumber daya setempat dan menjalankan kehidupan pulau ketika kondisi pantai terus berubah. Sumber: Oldest plant artefact found outside Africa reveals Pacific’s role in early human migration University of Oxford · 2024 https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2024-08-15-oldest-plant-artefact-found-outside-africa-reveals-pacifics-role-early-human; Mololo Cave study Antiquity · 2024 https://doi.org/10.15184/aqy.2024.83

text.en:
Excavations at Andarewa Cave near Fakfak place its earliest recorded occupation around 26,327–25,900 years ago, during the Last Glacial Maximum. The site lies between the Bird’s Head and the wider Sahul landmass. Stone tools, bone points, shells, charcoal and ochre document activities across several occupation layers. Pottery and jewellery belong to later parts of that sequence.

Local sedimentary stone was worked into small flakes and scrapers. Imported igneous stone raises questions about movement and exchange beyond the immediate area. Together with the inland Toé Kria record, Andarewa shows that early settlement included different environments, from coastal limestone caves to rainforest in the Bird’s Head.

The excavations distinguish a long sequence of occupations rather than one collection left at a single moment. Later bone points and ornaments made from animal remains show additional ways of working available materials; pottery marks a much later part of the cave’s use. Shell and charcoal deposits help connect tools to activities around the shelter. Because excavation did not reach sterile deposits below the occupation layers, the oldest recovered charcoal establishes a minimum depth to the known history, not the first arrival of people in Fakfak. Sources: Last Glacial Maximum to Late Holocene occupation on the Bomberai Peninsula Mene, Setiawan & Gaffney · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch09.pdf
text.pmy:
Penggalian di Gua Andarewa dekat Fakfak menempatkan hunian paling awal yang tercatat sekitar 26.327–25.900 tahun lalu, pada puncak Zaman Es terakhir. Situs ini berada di antara Kepala Burung dan daratan Sahul yang lebih luas. Alat batu, ujung tulang, kerang, arang, serta oker mencatat kegiatan dalam beberapa lapisan hunian. Tembikar dan perhiasan berasal dari bagian yang lebih muda dalam urutan tersebut.

Batuan sedimen setempat diolah menjadi serpih kecil dan alat pengerik. Batuan beku yang didatangkan dari luar menimbulkan pertanyaan tentang perpindahan serta pertukaran melampaui lingkungan terdekat. Bersama catatan pedalaman Toé Kria, Andarewa memperlihatkan bahwa permukiman awal mencakup lingkungan yang berbeda, dari gua kapur pesisir hingga hutan Kepala Burung.

Penggalian membedakan rangkaian hunian panjang, bukan satu kumpulan benda yang ditinggalkan sekaligus. Mata alat tulang dan perhiasan dari sisa hewan pada lapisan lebih muda menunjukkan cara lain mengolah bahan; tembikar berasal dari penggunaan gua yang jauh lebih kemudian. Endapan cangkang serta arang membantu menghubungkan alat dengan kegiatan di sekitar hunian. Penggalian belum mencapai lapisan steril di bawah jejak hunian. Arang tertua yang ditemukan menandai kedalaman sejarah yang sudah diketahui, bukan kedatangan pertama manusia di Fakfak. Sumber: Last Glacial Maximum to Late Holocene occupation on the Bomberai Peninsula Mene, Setiawan & Gaffney · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch09.pdf

title.en: Inland settlement in the Bird’s Head

text.en:
Research at Toé Kria records occupation of inland rainforest in the Bird’s Head from around 24,000 calibrated years before present. Its stone-tool and occupation sequence adds an inland perspective to early settlement evidence from coastal and island caves.

The site helps archaeologists investigate how people used rainforest environments during the late Pleistocene. Read beside Andarewa and Mololo, it documents several local histories of settlement rather than one route that explains every part of New Guinea.

An inland shelter asks different questions from a coastal cave. Its occupants needed routes through forest, access to materials for tools and knowledge of resources away from reefs and beaches. The occupation sequence shows that rainforest use was already part of human life during the late Pleistocene. Comparing Toé Kria with the Bomberai caves makes the geographical range of that life clearer: the early record is distributed across environments, with each excavation preserving only part of people’s movements and work. Sources: Late Pleistocene human occupation of inland rainforest, Bird’s Head, Irian Jaya Pasveer, Clarke & Miller · 2002 https://researchportalplus.anu.edu.au/en/publications/late-pleistocene-human-occupation-of-inland-rainforest-birds-head/
text.pmy:
Penelitian di Toé Kria mencatat hunian di hutan pedalaman Kepala Burung sejak sekitar 24.000 tahun terkalibrasi sebelum kini. Urutan alat batu serta huniannya menambahkan sudut pandang pedalaman pada bukti permukiman awal dari gua pesisir dan pulau.

Situs ini membantu arkeolog menyelidiki pemanfaatan hutan pada akhir Pleistosen. Dibaca bersama Andarewa dan Mololo, temuan tersebut mencatat beberapa riwayat permukiman setempat, bukan satu jalur yang menjelaskan seluruh Nugini.

Hunian pedalaman mengajukan pertanyaan berbeda dari gua pantai. Penghuninya memerlukan jalan melalui hutan, bahan untuk alat serta pengetahuan sumber daya di luar terumbu dan pesisir. Urutan hunian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan hutan hujan sudah menjadi bagian kehidupan manusia pada Pleistosen akhir. Perbandingan Toé Kria dengan gua di Bomberai memperjelas jangkauan kehidupan tersebut. Jejak awal tersebar di berbagai lingkungan, sementara setiap penggalian hanya menyimpan sebagian perjalanan dan pekerjaan manusia. Sumber: Late Pleistocene human occupation of inland rainforest, Bird’s Head, Irian Jaya Pasveer, Clarke & Miller · 2002 https://researchportalplus.anu.edu.au/en/publications/late-pleistocene-human-occupation-of-inland-rainforest-birds-head/

text.en:
Rising seas changed the geography of Sahul and the smaller islands along its western approaches. The Mololo study reconstructs a coastline much closer to Waigeo’s cave before flooding of the surrounding shelf around 9,500 years ago. Forest and marine resources were already part of the site’s early record.

Changing access to coasts, rivers and islands provides context for settlement and travel. It does not mean that every community moved at the same time, or that today’s island groups had their present shape throughout human occupation.

As low-lying land flooded, distances between shelters, landing places and fishing grounds changed. The broad continental connection between New Guinea and Australia also gave way to the waters of Torres Strait. Some former landscapes are now beneath the sea, making their settlements harder to investigate than caves above the present shoreline. This helps explain gaps in the archaeological record: an absence of excavated coastal sites need not mean an absence of people or voyaging. Sources: West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea
text.pmy:
Naiknya permukaan laut mengubah geografi Sahul dan pulau-pulau kecil di sebelah baratnya. Kajian Mololo merekonstruksi pantai yang dahulu jauh lebih dekat ke gua di Waigeo, sebelum paparan di sekitarnya tergenang sekitar 9.500 tahun lalu. Sumber daya hutan dan laut sudah tercatat dalam aktivitas awal di situs itu.

Perubahan akses ke pesisir, sungai, dan pulau memberi konteks bagi permukiman dan perjalanan. Perubahan ini tidak berarti semua masyarakat berpindah pada saat yang sama, atau bahwa kepulauan sekarang selalu memiliki bentuk yang sama.

Ketika daratan rendah tergenang, jarak antara hunian, tempat pendaratan dan daerah penangkapan ikan berubah. Hubungan darat luas antara Nugini dan Australia juga terpisah oleh perairan Selat Torres. Sebagian bentang lama kini berada di bawah laut sehingga permukimannya lebih sulit diteliti daripada gua di atas garis pantai sekarang. Hal ini membantu menjelaskan kekosongan catatan arkeologi: tidak adanya situs pantai yang digali belum berarti tidak ada manusia atau perjalanan laut. Sumber: West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea

text.en:
New Guinea’s food histories include the cultivation of plants alongside hunting, fishing and gathering. The archaeological record at Kuk, in present-day Papua New Guinea, documents changes in wetland cultivation and drainage over several millennia. It is important island-wide context, rather than a timetable for every part of western Papua.

The western region needs its own evidence from excavated sites, plant remains and environmental records. Sago forests, gardens and exchanges between ecological zones also matter; agricultural history cannot be reduced to the arrival of a single crop or an outside farming population.

At Kuk, cultivation mounds date to around 7,000–6,400 years ago, while later ditches drained wet ground for planting. The evidence includes vegetative propagation of bananas, taro and yam. Farmers altered the soil and water regime with wooden tools, creating productive areas through repeated labour. These remains place New Guinea among the regions where agriculture developed independently. They also show that farming was an accumulated body of technical knowledge, rather than a sudden replacement of hunting and gathering. Sources: West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea; Kuk Early Agricultural Site UNESCO World Heritage Centre https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/887/
text.pmy:
Sejarah pangan Nugini mencakup budidaya tumbuhan bersama berburu, menangkap ikan, dan meramu. Rekaman arkeologi Kuk, di wilayah Papua Nugini sekarang, menunjukkan perubahan budidaya lahan basah dan drainase selama beberapa milenium. Kuk memberi konteks sejarah pulau, bukan jadwal perkembangan bagi seluruh Papua bagian barat.

Wilayah barat memerlukan bukti tersendiri dari penggalian, sisa tumbuhan, dan rekaman lingkungan. Hutan sagu, kebun, serta pertukaran antarwilayah ekologis juga penting; sejarah pertanian tidak dapat diringkas sebagai kedatangan satu tanaman atau satu kelompok petani dari luar.

Di Kuk, gundukan budidaya berumur sekitar 7.000–6.400 tahun, sedangkan parit pada masa berikutnya mengeringkan lahan basah untuk ditanami. Bukti mencakup pembiakan vegetatif pisang, talas dan ubi. Petani mengubah tanah serta aliran air dengan alat kayu dan pekerjaan berulang. Temuan ini menempatkan Nugini di antara kawasan dengan perkembangan pertanian mandiri. Bertani merupakan pengetahuan teknis yang bertambah dari waktu ke waktu, bukan penggantian mendadak seluruh kegiatan berburu dan meramu. Sumber: West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea; Kuk Early Agricultural Site UNESCO World Heritage Centre https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/887/

text.en:
Archaeological surveys around western Lake Sentani link settlement choices to reliable freshwater and productive environments. The sites preserve evidence of fishing, collecting shellfish, hunting on land and gathering sago. Lake and forest resources supported people through different forms of work, rather than one single subsistence activity.

Marine shells found inland suggest links with the northern coast. People may have travelled to obtain them, or acquired them through exchanges with coastal communities. The material demonstrates connections without settling which route each object followed. The study does not assign every surveyed settlement one founding date.

Lake settlement joined water-based work with access to surrounding land. Fish and freshwater shellfish could be obtained near the settlement, while sago and hunted animals required knowledge of neighbouring habitats. Marine shells extend that picture beyond the lake basin. These finds make Sentani part of a connected landscape in which food production, movement and relationships with coastal communities overlapped; the lake was not an isolated cultural boundary. Sources: Prehistoric sites in the western Lake Sentani area Hari Suroto · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch12.pdf
text.pmy:
Survei arkeologi di bagian barat Danau Sentani menghubungkan pilihan tempat tinggal dengan air tawar yang tersedia serta lingkungan produktif. Situs-situsnya menyimpan bukti penangkapan ikan, pengumpulan kerang, perburuan darat, serta pengambilan sagu. Sumber daya danau dan hutan menopang kehidupan melalui beragam pekerjaan.

Cangkang laut yang ditemukan di pedalaman menunjukkan hubungan dengan pesisir utara. Orang mungkin bepergian untuk memperolehnya atau mendapatkannya melalui pertukaran dengan masyarakat pesisir. Benda tersebut memperlihatkan hubungan tanpa memastikan rute setiap benda. Kajian tidak menetapkan satu tanggal pendirian bagi seluruh permukiman yang disurvei.

Permukiman danau menghubungkan pekerjaan di air dengan akses ke daratan sekitarnya. Ikan dan kerang air tawar dapat diperoleh dekat hunian, sedangkan sagu serta hewan buruan memerlukan pengetahuan lingkungan lain. Cangkang laut memperluas hubungan itu ke luar cekungan danau. Temuan menjadikan Sentani bagian bentang yang terhubung: pangan, perjalanan dan hubungan dengan masyarakat pantai saling bertemu. Danau bukan batas kebudayaan yang tertutup. Sumber: Prehistoric sites in the western Lake Sentani area Hari Suroto · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch12.pdf

text.en:
Three burial sites near Jayapura—Gua Tubara, Tubara Sugu and Aturboyah Suwiyah—contained pottery associated with human remains. The vessels were richly decorated with triangles, straight lines, arrow-like forms and horizontal or circular incisions. Their placement as grave goods shows that pottery had uses beyond cooking and storing food.

Klementin Fairyo’s study compares these decorations with ethnographic and archaeological records and consults local informants. Styles help investigate affiliations and contacts; the assemblages have not yet been assigned an absolute date.

Burial vessels bring household technology into relationships with the dead. Their decoration gives archaeologists more than a dateable object: the arrangement of motifs and the setting of a pot beside human remains indicate choices made by the people conducting a burial. Fairyo places these choices alongside local knowledge and comparative material. The resulting account connects pottery with social memory and mortuary practice, without reducing each design to a fixed ethnic label. Sources: Decorated pottery from the Kayu Batu area, Jayapura Klementin Fairyo · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch13.pdf
text.pmy:
Tiga situs kubur dekat Jayapura—Gua Tubara, Tubara Sugu, dan Aturboyah Suwiyah—mengandung tembikar bersama sisa manusia. Wadahnya dihias segitiga, garis lurus, bentuk menyerupai panah, serta goresan mendatar atau melingkar. Penempatannya sebagai bekal kubur menunjukkan kegunaan di luar memasak dan menyimpan makanan.

Kajian Klementin Fairyo membandingkan hiasan ini dengan catatan etnografi dan arkeologi serta penuturan informan setempat. Gaya membantu menelusuri hubungan antarmasyarakat; kumpulan temuan belum memiliki penanggalan mutlak.

Wadah kubur membawa teknologi rumah tangga ke dalam hubungan dengan orang yang meninggal. Hiasannya memberi arkeolog lebih dari benda untuk ditentukan umur: susunan motif dan penempatan wadah bersama sisa manusia menunjukkan pilihan orang yang mengurus pemakaman. Fairyo membaca pilihan tersebut bersama pengetahuan setempat serta bahan pembanding. Tembikar terhubung dengan ingatan sosial dan praktik pemakaman, tanpa menjadikan setiap corak sebagai penanda suku yang tetap. Sumber: Decorated pottery from the Kayu Batu area, Jayapura Klementin Fairyo · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch13.pdf

title.en: Rock art and territory in Keerom
title.pmy: Lukisan cadas dan wilayah di Keerom

text.en:
Rock paintings at Web and Kibay, near the border with Papua New Guinea, include figurative and non-figurative motifs. A regional study combines analysis of the paintings with interviews and a review of earlier records. Local people describe the sites through religion, communication, identity and relationships to territory.

These accounts make the paintings part of a living social landscape. They add information that an inventory of shapes cannot supply. The paintings have not been assigned an absolute date.

A cave’s importance therefore includes who knows its stories, how people approach it and how its location relates to neighbouring territory. Recording the paintings without these relationships would leave out much of their meaning. The Keerom account illustrates why archaeological documentation and knowledge held by communities need to be read together: the visible marks survive on rock, while interpretations are maintained through people and their continuing use of the landscape. Sources: Rock art from caves in the Keerom Regency, Papua Province Klementin Fairyo · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch11.pdf
text.pmy:
Lukisan cadas di Web dan Kibay, dekat perbatasan Papua Nugini, mencakup motif figuratif dan nonfiguratif. Kajian regional memadukan analisis lukisan, wawancara, serta tinjauan catatan terdahulu. Masyarakat setempat menuturkan hubungan situs dengan agama, komunikasi, identitas, dan wilayah.

Penuturan menjadikan lukisan bagian bentang sosial yang hidup dan memberi pengetahuan di luar daftar bentuk. Lukisan belum memiliki penanggalan mutlak.

Arti penting gua juga mencakup siapa yang mengetahui ceritanya, bagaimana orang mendatanginya dan hubungannya dengan wilayah tetangga. Mencatat lukisan tanpa hubungan tersebut menghilangkan banyak maknanya. Kajian Keerom memperlihatkan perlunya membaca dokumentasi arkeologi bersama pengetahuan masyarakat. Goresan bertahan pada batu, sementara penjelasannya diteruskan melalui manusia dan hubungan mereka dengan bentang setempat. Sumber: Rock art from caves in the Keerom Regency, Papua Province Klementin Fairyo · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch11.pdf

text.en:
Austronesian-speaking communities became established along parts of western New Guinea and its islands. The Cenderawasih Bay language record points to a history of contact extending back around 3,500 years. Migration formed part of that history alongside trade, marriage and language shift.

Local populations shaped these encounters. Papuan and Austronesian languages borrowed words and grammatical patterns from one another, with different outcomes in different places. Language affiliation does not reliably identify one biological ancestry, and a new language need not imply the disappearance of the people who lived there before.

Laura Arnold’s linguistic synthesis uses shared vocabulary and language relationships to follow these contacts. Coastal and island communities connected New Guinea with networks reaching through eastern Indonesia and into the Pacific. Neighbours also adopted words and patterns through sustained interaction, so the history includes people remaining in place as well as migrants. Present-day diversity reflects those repeated encounters, not a clean boundary between an arriving population and an unchanged interior. Sources: Language as a lens into the prehistory of West New Guinea Laura Arnold · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch03.pdf
text.pmy:
Masyarakat penutur Austronesia berkembang di sebagian pesisir Nugini Barat dan pulau-pulaunya. Rekaman bahasa Teluk Cenderawasih menunjukkan hubungan yang menjangkau sekitar 3.500 tahun lalu. Perpindahan penduduk menjadi bagian sejarah ini, bersama perdagangan, perkawinan, dan peralihan bahasa.

Penduduk setempat ikut membentuk perjumpaan tersebut. Bahasa Papua dan Austronesia saling meminjam kosakata serta pola tata bahasa, dengan hasil yang berbeda di tiap tempat. Rumpun bahasa tidak menunjukkan satu asal biologis secara pasti. Bahasa baru juga tidak selalu berarti hilangnya masyarakat yang sebelumnya tinggal di sana.

Sintesis bahasa Laura Arnold menggunakan kosakata bersama serta kekerabatan bahasa untuk menelusuri hubungan tersebut. Masyarakat pantai dan pulau menghubungkan Nugini dengan jaringan melalui Indonesia timur hingga Pasifik. Tetangga juga menyerap kata serta pola melalui hubungan berkelanjutan. Sejarah ini mencakup penduduk yang tetap tinggal, bukan migran saja. Keragaman sekarang terbentuk dari pertemuan berulang, bukan batas tegas antara pendatang dan pedalaman yang tidak berubah. Sumber: Language as a lens into the prehistory of West New Guinea Laura Arnold · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch03.pdf

title.en: Pottery and contact in Raja Ampat
title.pmy: Tembikar dan hubungan di Raja Ampat

text.en:
Excavations at Mololo Cave on Waigeo recovered pottery dated to about 3,100–2,700 years ago, with a possible earlier occurrence around 3,800–3,500 years ago. Plain, red-slipped and incised vessels share features with ceramics elsewhere in Island Southeast Asia and the Pacific. The elaborate dentate stamping of early Lapita pottery is absent.

At Manwen Bokor Cave, later pottery from about 1,300–1,000 years ago includes more varied impressed and incised decoration. Gaffney and Tanudirjo compare these assemblages with eastern Wallacea and northern New Guinea, describing changes in the reach of regional networks. Pots and manufacturing techniques provide evidence of contact without requiring the movement of whole populations.

The differences between the two caves matter as much as the shared use of pottery. Red surfaces, incised lines and later impressed designs document changing choices in making and finishing vessels. Comparisons with neighbouring islands help locate these choices within wider exchanges of objects and knowledge. Raja Ampat thus records repeated connections across the seas west and north of New Guinea, with local potters participating in regional networks rather than simply receiving a finished culture from elsewhere.

For households, a vessel could change how food was prepared or stored; for archaeology, its fragments preserve a durable record after fibres and wood have decayed. Reading that material alongside stone tools and other cave deposits helps distinguish technological change from the much broader question of who moved between islands. Sources: Late Holocene potting traditions in the far western Pacific: Evidence from the Raja Ampat Islands, 3500–1000 BP Dylan Gaffney & Daud Tanudirjo · ANU Press https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n12314/pdf/ch17.pdf
text.pmy:
Penggalian di Gua Mololo, Waigeo, menemukan tembikar berumur sekitar 3.100–2.700 tahun, dengan kemungkinan temuan lebih awal sekitar 3.800–3.500 tahun. Wadah polos, bersalut merah, dan bergores memiliki kesamaan dengan keramik di kawasan Asia Tenggara Kepulauan serta Pasifik. Cap bergerigi rumit yang menjadi ciri tembikar Lapita awal tidak ditemukan.

Di Gua Manwen Bokor, tembikar lebih muda dari sekitar 1.300–1.000 tahun lalu memperlihatkan hiasan tekan dan gores yang lebih beragam. Gaffney dan Tanudirjo membandingkan temuan ini dengan Wallacea timur serta Nugini utara dan menjelaskan perubahan jangkauan jaringan regional. Wadah dan teknik pembuatannya menjadi bukti hubungan tanpa harus berarti perpindahan seluruh penduduk.

Perbedaan kedua gua sama pentingnya dengan kesamaan penggunaan tembikar. Permukaan merah, goresan dan ragam cap pada masa berikutnya merekam perubahan pilihan pembuatan serta penyelesaian wadah. Perbandingan dengan pulau tetangga menempatkan pilihan itu dalam pertukaran benda dan pengetahuan yang lebih luas. Raja Ampat merekam hubungan berulang melalui laut di barat serta utara Nugini, dengan pembuat tembikar setempat ikut membentuk jaringan regional.

Bagi rumah tangga, wadah dapat mengubah cara menyiapkan atau menyimpan makanan. Bagi arkeologi, pecahannya menyimpan jejak ketika serat dan kayu sudah lapuk. Membaca tembikar bersama alat batu serta endapan gua membantu membedakan perubahan teknologi dari pertanyaan yang lebih luas tentang perpindahan manusia antarpulau. Sumber: Late Holocene potting traditions in the far western Pacific: Evidence from the Raja Ampat Islands, 3500–1000 BP Dylan Gaffney & Daud Tanudirjo · ANU Press https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n12314/pdf/ch17.pdf

text.en:
West New Guinea contains numerous language families and isolates alongside Austronesian languages. “Papuan” groups the non-Austronesian languages geographically; it does not name a single language family. Laura Arnold’s synthesis brings together classifications, regional distributions and evidence of contact.

The Bird’s Head includes several distinct families and isolates within a relatively small area. Elsewhere, larger proposed groupings coexist with languages whose deeper relationships remain under study. Borrowed words and grammatical features record encounters between neighbouring communities. A language map is useful for locating these relationships, but its present-day distribution cannot be read as an unchanged map of ancient peoples.

Arnold’s overview identifies more than 260 languages, approximately 30 families and 18 isolates in western New Guinea. An isolate is a language whose relationship to another family has not been established, not a community without neighbours. Such density means that interpretation, marriage networks and multilingual speakers have long mattered in travel and public life. Shared features can reveal contact across language boundaries even where the languages themselves have different origins. Sources: Language as a lens into the prehistory of West New Guinea Laura Arnold · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch03.pdf
text.pmy:
Papua bagian barat memiliki banyak rumpun bahasa serta bahasa isolat, bersama bahasa-bahasa Austronesia. Sebutan “Papua” mengelompokkan bahasa non-Austronesia secara geografis, bukan menamai satu rumpun. Sintesis Laura Arnold menghimpun klasifikasi, persebaran regional, dan bukti hubungan antarmasyarakat.

Kepala Burung memuat beberapa rumpun serta bahasa isolat dalam kawasan yang relatif kecil. Di tempat lain, pengelompokan yang lebih besar berdampingan dengan bahasa yang hubungan asalnya masih diteliti. Kata pinjaman serta unsur tata bahasa mencatat perjumpaan masyarakat bertetangga. Peta bahasa membantu menemukan hubungan tersebut, tetapi persebaran sekarang tidak dapat dibaca sebagai peta masyarakat kuno yang tidak berubah.

Ikhtisar Arnold mencatat lebih dari 260 bahasa, sekitar 30 keluarga bahasa dan 18 bahasa isolat di barat Nugini. Isolat berarti hubungan dengan keluarga lain belum terbukti, bukan masyarakat tanpa tetangga. Keragaman ini membuat penerjemahan, hubungan perkawinan dan penutur multibahasa penting dalam perjalanan serta kehidupan publik. Ciri yang dipakai bersama dapat memperlihatkan hubungan antarmasyarakat meskipun asal bahasanya berbeda. Sumber: Language as a lens into the prehistory of West New Guinea Laura Arnold · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch03.pdf

text.en:
Genome-wide research describes varied population histories across New Guinea, shaped by regional separation, movement and later contact. Studies including Korowai samples contribute evidence from western Papua, but coverage remains uneven. Findings from a sampled community cannot simply stand for the whole island.

Y-chromosome K2b1, including lineages described as M and S in the cited classification, concerns one paternal line. It does not represent a person’s whole ancestry, language or identity. Archaeology and linguistics provide other kinds of evidence; together they offer a richer account than assigning modern peoples to a genetic tree.

Genetic research also traces encounters with archaic humans, including Denisovan ancestry preserved in some present-day genomes. The regional differences concern histories of separation and contact over many generations. A genome-wide analysis follows numerous inherited segments, whereas a paternal lineage follows only a narrow branch of a family tree. These different scales help explain why the same person can carry histories that do not fit one simple migration label. Sources: Deep histories in New Guinea: Insights from human genetics on regional demography and archaic introgression Guy Jacobs, Pradiptajati Kusuma & Robert Attenborough · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch04.pdf; Improved phylogenetic resolution and rapid diversification of Y-chromosome haplogroup K-M526 Karafet et al. · 2014 https://www.nature.com/articles/ejhg2014106
text.pmy:
Penelitian genom menunjukkan sejarah penduduk Nugini yang beragam, dipengaruhi pemisahan regional, perpindahan, dan hubungan berikutnya. Kajian yang menyertakan sampel Korowai menambah bukti dari Papua bagian barat, tetapi cakupan penelitian masih tidak merata. Temuan satu masyarakat tidak dapat langsung mewakili seluruh pulau.

K2b1 pada kromosom Y, termasuk garis M dan S dalam klasifikasi yang dirujuk, hanya menyangkut satu garis paternal. Penanda itu tidak mewakili seluruh leluhur, bahasa, atau identitas seseorang. Arkeologi dan linguistik menyediakan bukti lain yang bersama-sama memberi gambaran lebih lengkap daripada menempatkan masyarakat modern pada pohon genetik.

Penelitian genetika juga menelusuri pertemuan dengan manusia purba, termasuk leluhur Denisovan yang jejaknya tersimpan dalam sebagian genom sekarang. Perbedaan regional berkaitan dengan pemisahan serta pertemuan selama banyak generasi. Analisis seluruh genom mengikuti banyak bagian yang diwariskan, sedangkan garis ayah hanya mengikuti cabang sempit silsilah keluarga. Perbedaan skala ini menjelaskan mengapa satu orang dapat membawa riwayat yang tidak cocok dengan satu label migrasi saja. Sumber: Deep histories in New Guinea: Insights from human genetics on regional demography and archaic introgression Guy Jacobs, Pradiptajati Kusuma & Robert Attenborough · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch04.pdf; Improved phylogenetic resolution and rapid diversification of Y-chromosome haplogroup K-M526 Karafet et al. · 2014 https://www.nature.com/articles/ejhg2014106

text.en:
Melanesia and Polynesia are regional names, not two uniform biological populations. Pacific settlement involved several movements and encounters. Ancient genomes from early Vanuatu and Tonga show that the ancestry represented in those particular burials differs from that of many present-day islanders, reflecting later interactions.

These studies illuminate specific places, dates and small sample sets. They do not give a complete origin story for western Papua. Language, kinship, voyaging and political relationships connect Pacific communities in ways that cannot be inferred from DNA alone.

Early Lapita-associated individuals studied in Vanuatu and Tonga carried predominantly East Asian-related ancestry, while later Pacific populations also carry substantial Papuan-related ancestry. The sequence indicates further movement and mixture after the first settlements represented by those burials. It helps explain connections between eastern New Guinea, island Melanesia and Polynesia without treating those regional names as separate races. Voyaging brought people, skills and kinship relationships into a history that continued after any first arrival. Sources: Genomic insights into the peopling of the Southwest Pacific Skoglund et al. · 2016 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5515717/; Deep histories in New Guinea: Insights from human genetics on regional demography and archaic introgression Guy Jacobs, Pradiptajati Kusuma & Robert Attenborough · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch04.pdf
text.pmy:
Melanesia dan Polinesia adalah nama regional, bukan dua populasi biologis yang seragam. Permukiman Pasifik melibatkan beberapa gelombang perpindahan serta perjumpaan. Genom kuno dari Vanuatu dan Tonga awal menunjukkan bahwa leluhur yang tercatat pada pemakaman tertentu berbeda dari banyak penduduk pulau sekarang, sejalan dengan interaksi berikutnya.

Kajian tersebut menjelaskan tempat, waktu, dan sampel kecil yang tertentu, bukan seluruh asal-usul Papua bagian barat. Bahasa, kekerabatan, pelayaran, dan hubungan politik menghubungkan masyarakat Pasifik dengan cara yang tidak dapat disimpulkan dari DNA saja.

Individu awal terkait Lapita yang diteliti di Vanuatu dan Tonga terutama membawa leluhur yang berkerabat dengan Asia Timur, sedangkan penduduk Pasifik pada masa berikutnya juga membawa unsur leluhur terkait Papua yang besar. Urutan ini menunjukkan perpindahan serta percampuran setelah permukiman awal yang diwakili kuburan tersebut. Temuan membantu menjelaskan hubungan antara timur Nugini, Melanesia kepulauan dan Polinesia tanpa menjadikan nama regional itu ras terpisah. Pelayaran mempertemukan manusia, keterampilan dan kekerabatan dalam sejarah yang terus berjalan setelah kedatangan awal. Sumber: Genomic insights into the peopling of the Southwest Pacific Skoglund et al. · 2016 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5515717/; Deep histories in New Guinea: Insights from human genetics on regional demography and archaic introgression Guy Jacobs, Pradiptajati Kusuma & Robert Attenborough · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch04.pdf

text.en:
Mansoben’s comparative study describes regional forms of authority recorded in ethnographic research. Around Sentani, the office of ondoafi is connected to descent, kin groups and village territory. Among Mee, a tonowi builds standing through wealth, generosity and the ability to organise relationships. Maybrat bobot and Muyu kayepak also gain influence through exchange and social obligations.

Pigs, cowrie shells and kain timur circulated through relationships that connected leadership with marriage, work and reciprocity. On the western coasts, raja in Raja Ampat, Onin and Kaimana linked local authority to maritime networks and Maluku. Some offices were inherited; others depended more on achievement and support. These documented regional systems help explain the institutions and land relationships encountered by colonial administration, without assigning them a single ancient origin.

Authority carried responsibilities as well as status. A leader who organised exchange depended on the people willing to work, contribute valuables and recognise obligations; an inherited office rested on relationships between descent groups and territory. Colonial officials later tried to identify particular people as representatives of whole communities. Those selections could narrow a much wider field of customary decision-making. Mansoben’s distinctions explain why recognising a single officeholder is not the same as understanding how consent and responsibility operate locally. Sources: Sistem Politik Tradisional di Irian Jaya J. R. Mansoben · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-01/Mansoben_1995_Sistem.pdf
text.pmy:
Kajian perbandingan Mansoben menjelaskan bentuk kewenangan regional yang dicatat dalam penelitian etnografi. Di sekitar Sentani, kedudukan ondoafi berkaitan dengan keturunan, kelompok kekerabatan, dan wilayah kampung. Di kalangan Mee, tonowi membangun kedudukan melalui kekayaan, kemurahan hati, dan kemampuan mengatur hubungan. Bobot di Maybrat serta kayepak di Muyu juga memperoleh pengaruh melalui pertukaran dan kewajiban sosial.

Babi, kerang kauri, dan kain timur beredar melalui hubungan yang mengaitkan kepemimpinan dengan perkawinan, kerja, dan timbal balik. Di pesisir barat, raja di Raja Ampat, Onin, dan Kaimana menghubungkan kewenangan setempat dengan jaringan maritim serta Maluku. Sebagian jabatan diwariskan; yang lain lebih bergantung pada pencapaian dan dukungan. Catatan regional ini membantu menjelaskan lembaga serta hubungan tanah yang dihadapi pemerintahan kolonial, tanpa menetapkan satu masa asal bagi semuanya.

Wewenang membawa tanggung jawab selain kedudukan. Pemimpin pertukaran bergantung pada orang yang bersedia bekerja, menyumbang benda berharga dan mengakui kewajiban. Jabatan warisan bertumpu pada hubungan kelompok keturunan dengan wilayah. Pejabat kolonial kemudian memilih orang tertentu sebagai wakil seluruh masyarakat. Pilihan itu dapat mempersempit ruang pengambilan keputusan adat yang lebih luas. Pembedaan Mansoben menjelaskan mengapa mengenali satu pemegang jabatan belum sama dengan memahami cara persetujuan dan tanggung jawab dijalankan setempat. Sumber: Sistem Politik Tradisional di Irian Jaya J. R. Mansoben · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-01/Mansoben_1995_Sistem.pdf

text.en:
Exchange connected communities across valleys, coasts and ecological zones. People moved shells, pigs, food and other valuables through kinship, marriage and trading relationships. These transactions could create obligations and establish a person’s standing, alongside meeting practical needs.

Mansoben describes cowrie wealth in Mee and Muyu leadership and kain timur in Maybrat social life. Access to valuables depended on wider relationships: goods arriving through coastal networks could acquire new uses and meanings inland. The systems varied by place and changed over time, but they show how authority and economic life were organised through social relationships rather than a separate administrative office.

Beatrice Voirol follows shells such as cowries and Melo through coastal and highland settings. A shell’s value was not only its usefulness or rarity: its circulation could connect families, mark a payment and maintain relationships across distance. As it moved inland, an object obtained at the coast entered local systems of wealth and obligation. Shell histories consequently join marine knowledge with highland social life, showing how communities made outside materials part of their own institutions. Sources: Sistem Politik Tradisional di Irian Jaya J. R. Mansoben · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-01/Mansoben_1995_Sistem.pdf; West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea; Shell material culture in the West New Guinea Highlands: An ethnographic kaleidoscope Beatrice Voirol · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch17.pdf
text.pmy:
Pertukaran menghubungkan masyarakat antarlembah, pesisir, dan wilayah ekologis. Kerang, babi, pangan, serta benda berharga lain berpindah melalui kekerabatan, perkawinan, dan hubungan dagang. Transaksi dapat membentuk kewajiban serta kedudukan seseorang, sekaligus memenuhi kebutuhan sehari-hari.

Mansoben menjelaskan kekayaan kerang dalam kepemimpinan Mee dan Muyu serta kain timur dalam kehidupan sosial Maybrat. Akses pada benda berharga bergantung pada hubungan yang lebih luas: barang yang masuk melalui jaringan pesisir dapat memperoleh kegunaan serta makna baru di pedalaman. Sistem ini berbeda antardaerah dan berubah dari waktu ke waktu, tetapi memperlihatkan bagaimana kewenangan serta kehidupan ekonomi diatur melalui hubungan sosial.

Beatrice Voirol mengikuti cangkang seperti kerang kauri dan Melo melalui masyarakat pantai serta pegunungan. Nilainya bukan hanya kegunaan atau kelangkaan: peredarannya dapat menghubungkan keluarga, menandai pembayaran dan memelihara hubungan lintas wilayah. Ketika masuk pedalaman, benda dari pantai menjadi bagian sistem kekayaan dan kewajiban setempat. Sejarah cangkang mempertemukan pengetahuan laut dengan kehidupan sosial pegunungan, menunjukkan cara masyarakat memasukkan bahan dari luar ke dalam lembaganya sendiri. Sumber: Sistem Politik Tradisional di Irian Jaya J. R. Mansoben · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-01/Mansoben_1995_Sistem.pdf; West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea; Shell material culture in the West New Guinea Highlands: An ethnographic kaleidoscope Beatrice Voirol · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch17.pdf

text.en:
Maritime networks connected western New Guinea with Maluku over centuries. The ANU synthesis discusses tributary relations along the coasts between the fifteenth and nineteenth centuries; Overweel’s study follows the claims and negotiations described in nineteenth-century memoranda. Tidore exercised influence through coastal leaders and intermediaries rather than a uniform administration of the interior.

Trade, tribute and slave trading formed part of these encounters. Local rulers and communities negotiated relationships with competing outside powers. Dutch claims later drew on agreements with Tidore, but declaring sovereignty did not establish an administrative presence across Papua. The early Fort Du Bus settlement and the much later permanent stations illustrate that difference.

These connections gave coastal leaders access to imported goods and outside patrons, but also exposed communities to extraction and violence. The reach of a tributary relationship depended on intermediaries, travel and the ability to enforce a demand. It differed from later government with permanent stations and officials. When Dutch authorities invoked Tidore’s claims, they converted a varied maritime history into a territorial argument over people who had not collectively agreed to become Dutch subjects. Sources: Topics relating to Netherlands New Guinea in nineteenth-century memoranda J. A. Overweel · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-10/Overweel_1995_Topics_13.pdf
text.pmy:
Jaringan maritim menghubungkan Papua bagian barat dengan Maluku selama berabad-abad. Sintesis ANU membahas hubungan upeti di pesisir antara abad ke-15 dan ke-19; kajian Overweel menelusuri klaim serta perundingan dalam memorandum abad ke-19. Tidore menjalankan pengaruh melalui pemimpin pesisir dan perantara, bukan satu pemerintahan yang merata di pedalaman.

Perdagangan, upeti, dan perdagangan budak menjadi bagian dari perjumpaan ini. Penguasa serta masyarakat setempat berunding dengan kekuatan luar yang bersaing. Klaim Belanda kemudian bertumpu pada perjanjian dengan Tidore, tetapi pernyataan kedaulatan belum membentuk kehadiran pemerintahan di seluruh Papua. Permukiman awal Benteng Du Bus dan pos permanen yang baru berdiri jauh kemudian memperlihatkan perbedaan itu.

Hubungan ini memberi pemimpin pantai akses ke barang impor serta dukungan luar, tetapi juga membawa pengambilan sumber daya dan kekerasan. Jangkauan hubungan upeti bergantung pada perantara, perjalanan dan kemampuan memaksakan tuntutan. Bentuknya berbeda dari pemerintahan dengan pos serta pejabat tetap. Ketika Belanda menggunakan klaim Tidore, sejarah maritim yang beragam dijadikan argumen wilayah atas masyarakat yang tidak pernah bersama-sama menyetujui menjadi rakyat Belanda. Sumber: Topics relating to Netherlands New Guinea in nineteenth-century memoranda J. A. Overweel · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-10/Overweel_1995_Topics_13.pdf

text.en:
Malind accounts gathered in the Forest Peoples Programme’s MIFEE study describe customary land through food, work and relationships between people and places. Sago groves, gardens, hunting areas and waterways support livelihoods alongside knowledge passed through families. Decisions about land therefore affect access to existing sources of food and the ability to continue using them.

The 2013 field study records negotiations with a sugarcane company and community concerns about forest conversion. It asks whether information and consent processes enabled people to make decisions about their territories. These accounts provide an important background to later food and energy projects in Merauke: the terms of an investment agreement and the effects on everyday access to land need to be read together.

Sago and forest foods reduce the amount a household must buy, while hunting and fishing connect knowledge of particular places with the work of obtaining food. Clearing a concession can therefore remove productive resources before new wages or services exist to replace them. The Malind testimony links this change with dependence on purchased food and loss of control over daily decisions. A territory’s value cannot be captured by the price of timber or a one-off payment for land. Sources: A sweetness like unto death: voices of the indigenous Malind of Merauke Forest Peoples Programme · 2013 https://www.forestpeoples.org/publications-resources/reports/article/a-sweetness-like-unto-death-voices-of-the-indigenous-malind-of-merauke-papua/; A sweetness like unto death FPP, Pusaka & Sawit Watch · 2013 https://www.forestpeoples.org/fileadmin/uploads/fpp/migration/publication/2013/10/asweetnessundodeathmifeeindonesiaenglish2.pdf
text.pmy:
Kesaksian Malind dalam kajian MIFEE Forest Peoples Programme menjelaskan tanah adat melalui pangan, kerja, serta hubungan manusia dengan tempat. Dusun sagu, kebun, wilayah berburu, dan perairan menopang penghidupan bersama pengetahuan yang diteruskan melalui keluarga. Keputusan tentang tanah dengan demikian memengaruhi akses pada sumber pangan yang sudah ada serta kemampuan untuk terus memanfaatkannya.

Kajian lapangan 2013 mencatat perundingan dengan perusahaan tebu dan kekhawatiran masyarakat tentang perubahan hutan. Kajian ini menanyakan apakah informasi serta proses persetujuan memungkinkan masyarakat mengambil keputusan atas wilayah mereka. Kesaksian tersebut menjadi latar penting bagi proyek pangan dan energi berikutnya di Merauke: ketentuan perjanjian investasi serta dampaknya pada akses tanah sehari-hari perlu dibaca bersama.

Sagu serta pangan hutan mengurangi makanan yang harus dibeli keluarga. Berburu dan menangkap ikan menghubungkan pengetahuan tempat tertentu dengan pekerjaan memperoleh pangan. Pembukaan konsesi dapat menghilangkan sumber produktif sebelum upah atau layanan baru tersedia sebagai pengganti. Kesaksian Malind menghubungkan perubahan ini dengan ketergantungan pada makanan yang dibeli serta berkurangnya kendali atas keputusan sehari-hari. Nilai wilayah tidak dapat diwakili harga kayu atau satu pembayaran tanah. Sumber: A sweetness like unto death: voices of the indigenous Malind of Merauke Forest Peoples Programme · 2013 https://www.forestpeoples.org/publications-resources/reports/article/a-sweetness-like-unto-death-voices-of-the-indigenous-malind-of-merauke-papua/; A sweetness like unto death FPP, Pusaka & Sawit Watch · 2013 https://www.forestpeoples.org/fileadmin/uploads/fpp/migration/publication/2013/10/asweetnessundodeathmifeeindonesiaenglish2.pdf

text.en:
Bark cloth is prepared and painted in communities around Lake Sentani, including Asei. Makers turn the processed bark into paintings and crafted objects, working with motifs and knowledge associated with their communities. Individual artists also develop new works for galleries and exhibitions.

Accounts of Fansoway Art and Agustinus Ongge show how teaching, family work and wider audiences shape the practice today. The practice continues through identifiable makers, families and galleries.

Asei’s painted bark cloth carries knowledge through work as well as through the finished image. Preparing a surface, choosing a design and teaching another maker sustain a practice that galleries alone cannot preserve. Fansoway Art gives that work a local place of display and sale, while artists such as Agustinus Ongge connect it with audiences elsewhere. The contemporary history includes individual invention, family teaching and opportunities to earn from art without separating the object from the people who make it. Sources: Fansoway Art: galeri karya seni dan kerajinan Kampung Asei Besar Jubi · 2024 https://jubi.id/seni-budaya/2024/fansoway-art-galeri-karya-seni-dan-kerajinan-kampung-asei-besar-sentani/; Agustinus Ongge and Rebirthing Traditions Sentani Arts https://sentaniarts.wordpress.com/about/
text.pmy:
Kulit kayu diolah dan dilukis oleh masyarakat sekitar Danau Sentani, termasuk Asei. Pembuatnya menjadikan kulit yang diproses sebagai lukisan dan benda kerajinan, dengan motif serta pengetahuan masyarakat setempat. Seniman juga mengembangkan karya baru untuk galeri dan pameran.

Catatan Fansoway Art dan Agustinus Ongge menunjukkan bagaimana pengajaran, pekerjaan keluarga serta penonton yang lebih luas membentuk praktik sekarang. Khombouw terus berkembang melalui pembuat, keluarga dan galeri yang dapat dikenal.

Kulit kayu lukis Asei membawa pengetahuan melalui pekerjaan, bukan gambar akhirnya saja. Menyiapkan permukaan, memilih corak dan mengajar pembuat lain meneruskan praktik yang tidak dapat dijaga oleh galeri saja. Fansoway Art memberi tempat setempat untuk memamerkan serta menjual karya, sementara seniman seperti Agustinus Ongge menghubungkannya dengan penonton di tempat lain. Sejarah sekarang mencakup penciptaan individu, pengajaran keluarga dan kesempatan memperoleh penghasilan tanpa memisahkan benda dari pembuatnya. Sumber: Fansoway Art: galeri karya seni dan kerajinan Kampung Asei Besar Jubi · 2024 https://jubi.id/seni-budaya/2024/fansoway-art-galeri-karya-seni-dan-kerajinan-kampung-asei-besar-sentani/; Agustinus Ongge and Rebirthing Traditions Sentani Arts https://sentaniarts.wordpress.com/about/

text.en:
Among Mee communities in the central ranges, cowrie shells known as meege are used in marriage payments. Martinus Tekege’s account describes a payment from the groom’s side to the bride’s family as part of customary recognition of a marriage. The shells also express a relationship between families, with obligations that extend beyond the wedding itself.

Tekege writes from personal experience and Mee perspectives. He records debate about the practice’s continuing relevance, including concerns about gender and changing economic circumstances.

The payment draws on relatives who contribute and on relationships that may require further support later. Its significance therefore reaches beyond the transfer of shells between two individuals. Arguments about costs, women’s position and the use of money concern who can enter a recognised marriage and how families meet the obligations involved. Tekege’s account shows people reasoning within their own institution and seeking changes in it, rather than a custom simply surviving untouched from the past. Sources: Meege as bride price in Mee culture Martinus Tekege · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch18.pdf
text.pmy:
Di masyarakat Mee di pegunungan tengah, cangkang kerang yang disebut meege digunakan dalam pembayaran perkawinan. Martinus Tekege menjelaskan pembayaran dari pihak laki-laki kepada keluarga perempuan sebagai bagian pengakuan perkawinan secara adat. Kerang juga menyatakan hubungan antarkeluarga, dengan kewajiban yang melampaui hari perkawinan.

Tekege menulis dari pengalaman pribadi serta sudut pandang Mee. Ia mencatat perdebatan mengenai keberlanjutan praktik, termasuk kedudukan perempuan dan perubahan ekonomi.

Pembayaran melibatkan kerabat yang menyumbang serta hubungan yang dapat menuntut bantuan lagi di kemudian hari. Maknanya melampaui perpindahan kerang antara dua orang. Perdebatan tentang biaya, kedudukan perempuan dan penggunaan uang berkaitan dengan siapa yang dapat menjalani perkawinan yang diakui serta bagaimana keluarga memenuhi kewajibannya. Catatan Tekege memperlihatkan masyarakat menimbang dan mengubah lembaganya sendiri, bukan adat yang sekadar bertahan tanpa perubahan. Sumber: Meege as bride price in Mee culture Martinus Tekege · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch18.pdf

text.en:
Noken are made by knotting or weaving fibres into bags used for carrying food, possessions and sometimes children, as well as in social and ceremonial exchange. Materials, forms and skills differ between communities. Making them connects practical work with teaching across generations.

UNESCO’s record describes pressure from changing materials, livelihoods and transmission of skills. The 2012 safeguarding decision appears later in this chronology. It is the date of an institutional recognition, not the beginning of noken-making. Contemporary makers continue to adapt the practice rather than merely preserve one unchanging form.

A bag’s flexibility, size and carrying method suit different work, from bringing garden produce home to transporting household belongings. Knowing the plant material and how to turn it into fibre is part of the skill, before knotting or weaving begins. Learning usually depends on access to experienced makers and time to practise. When livelihoods or available materials change, those conditions change too. Safeguarding the craft therefore concerns the daily circumstances of making, not only collecting finished bags. Sources: Noken, multifunctional knotted or woven bag handcraft UNESCO https://ich.unesco.org/en/USL/noken-multifunctional-knotted-or-woven-bag-handcraft-of-the-people-of-papua-00619
text.pmy:
Noken dibuat dengan merajut atau menganyam serat menjadi tas untuk membawa pangan, barang, dan kadang anak, serta untuk pertukaran sosial maupun upacara. Bahan, bentuk, dan keterampilannya berbeda antarmasyarakat. Pembuatannya menghubungkan pekerjaan praktis dengan pengajaran antargenerasi.

Catatan UNESCO menjelaskan tekanan akibat perubahan bahan, penghidupan, dan pewarisan keterampilan. Keputusan pelindungan 2012 muncul kemudian dalam kronologi ini. Tahun tersebut menandai pengakuan kelembagaan, bukan awal pembuatan noken. Pembuat masa kini terus menyesuaikan praktiknya, bukan sekadar mempertahankan satu bentuk tanpa perubahan.

Kelenturan, ukuran dan cara membawa noken menyesuaikan pekerjaan, dari mengangkut hasil kebun hingga membawa barang rumah tangga. Mengenali tumbuhan dan mengolahnya menjadi serat merupakan bagian keterampilan sebelum merajut atau menganyam. Belajar memerlukan pembuat berpengalaman serta waktu untuk berlatih. Ketika penghidupan atau bahan berubah, kondisi belajar ikut berubah. Perlindungan kerajinan karena itu menyangkut kehidupan sehari-hari pembuat, bukan mengumpulkan tas yang sudah jadi saja. Sumber: Noken, multifunctional knotted or woven bag handcraft UNESCO https://ich.unesco.org/en/USL/noken-multifunctional-knotted-or-woven-bag-handcraft-of-the-people-of-papua-00619

text.en:
The Dutch established Fort Du Bus on the southwest coast in 1828 and proclaimed a territorial claim over western New Guinea. The settlement was short-lived. A declaration and a coastal fort did not establish effective control over the island’s many communities.

Later colonial accounts used this claim as part of a legal and diplomatic history. Reading it alongside the long gap before permanent administrative stations helps distinguish claimed territory from the actual reach of government. Papuan societies and their regional relationships continued beyond the fort’s limited presence.

The fort was an attempt to turn a claim on a map into an occupied place. Maintaining supplies and a garrison on the coast was different from governing inland communities or obtaining their consent. Its failure left a claim that officials could revive in later negotiations without the continuous administration normally associated with it. The interval before the stations of 1898 is consequently part of the political history: colonial ownership was asserted long before the state acquired an extensive local presence. Sources: Topics relating to Netherlands New Guinea in nineteenth-century memoranda J. A. Overweel · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-10/Overweel_1995_Topics_13.pdf
text.pmy:
Belanda mendirikan Benteng Du Bus di pesisir barat daya pada 1828 dan menyatakan klaim atas Nugini Barat. Permukiman itu tidak bertahan lama. Pernyataan klaim dan sebuah benteng pesisir tidak membentuk penguasaan efektif atas banyak masyarakat di pulau ini.

Catatan kolonial berikutnya memakai klaim tersebut dalam sejarah hukum serta diplomasi. Jarak waktu yang panjang sebelum pendirian pos pemerintahan menetap membantu membedakan wilayah yang diklaim dari jangkauan pemerintah sebenarnya. Masyarakat Papua beserta hubungan regionalnya terus berlangsung di luar kehadiran benteng yang terbatas.

Benteng merupakan upaya mengubah klaim pada peta menjadi tempat yang diduduki. Menjaga pasokan dan pasukan pantai berbeda dari memerintah masyarakat pedalaman atau memperoleh persetujuan mereka. Kegagalannya menyisakan klaim yang dapat digunakan lagi dalam perundingan tanpa pemerintahan berkelanjutan. Jarak waktu sebelum pos 1898 karena itu merupakan bagian sejarah politik: kepemilikan kolonial dinyatakan jauh sebelum negara membangun kehadiran setempat yang luas. Sumber: Topics relating to Netherlands New Guinea in nineteenth-century memoranda J. A. Overweel · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-10/Overweel_1995_Topics_13.pdf

text.en:
Kamoro objects entered European museums through encounters with traders, expeditions, colonial officers, missionaries and anthropologists. Karen Jacobs traces acquisitions from the Triton expedition in 1828 to collections made during the Kamoro Arts Festival between 1998 and 2006. An armlet collected in 1828 illuminates exchange practices connected to eastern Indonesian trade recorded from the seventeenth century.

Museum holdings preserve an uneven record: this study finds relatively little material from the late 1960s to the 1990s. Collectors’ interests shaped what was kept. Reading the objects alongside Kamoro accounts makes visible the makers, their exchange relationships and the continuing relevance of collections to artists today.

The history of a collection also records unequal power: visitors selected portable objects while museums decided which names and explanations to retain. The long gap in later holdings can make a continuing practice appear to disappear from the archive. Festival collections changed what museums could show, bringing more recent making into view. Returning to these objects with Kamoro knowledge can recover relationships and uses that an old catalogue reduced to material, shape and acquisition date. Sources: A collection of relationships: Kamoro material culture in the museum Karen Jacobs · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch20.pdf
text.pmy:
Benda Kamoro masuk museum Eropa melalui perjumpaan dengan pedagang, ekspedisi, pejabat kolonial, misionaris, serta antropolog. Karen Jacobs menelusuri perolehan sejak ekspedisi Triton pada 1828 hingga koleksi dari Festival Seni Kamoro pada 1998–2006. Gelang lengan yang dikoleksi pada 1828 menerangkan praktik pertukaran terkait perdagangan dengan Indonesia timur yang tercatat sejak abad ketujuh belas.

Koleksi museum menyimpan catatan yang tidak merata. Kajian menemukan relatif sedikit benda dari akhir 1960-an hingga 1990-an. Minat pengoleksi menentukan benda yang disimpan. Membaca benda bersama penuturan Kamoro memperlihatkan pembuat, hubungan pertukaran, serta arti koleksi bagi seniman sekarang.

Sejarah koleksi juga merekam ketimpangan kuasa: pengunjung memilih benda yang dapat dibawa, sedangkan museum menentukan nama serta penjelasan yang disimpan. Kekosongan panjang dalam koleksi lebih muda dapat membuat praktik yang terus hidup tampak hilang dari arsip. Koleksi festival mengubah apa yang dapat ditampilkan museum dengan menghadirkan karya baru. Membaca kembali benda bersama pengetahuan Kamoro dapat memulihkan hubungan serta kegunaan yang dulu diringkas katalog menjadi bahan, bentuk dan tanggal perolehan. Sumber: A collection of relationships: Kamoro material culture in the museum Karen Jacobs · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch20.pdf

text.en:
Manokwari and Fak-Fak became centres of permanent Dutch administration in 1898. These stations expanded the colonial state’s presence after earlier claims had left much of the territory beyond regular administration. Government reach remained uneven.

Officials relied on intermediaries, mission networks and selected local leaders. The emergence of a station did not make every surrounding community subject to the same institutions at once. Photographs and administrative memoranda preserve parts of this process, largely from the perspective of those producing the colonial record.

Permanent stations changed the terms of encounter. An official could now record a population, appoint an intermediary and respond to disputes from an established base. Coastal communities faced a government seeking to make its categories and demands routine. Papuan authority did not simply vanish, but its relationship with outside power became more sustained. Administration expanded through selected ports before reaching further inland, leaving substantial differences in how and when communities encountered the colonial state. Sources: Topics relating to Netherlands New Guinea in nineteenth-century memoranda J. A. Overweel · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-10/Overweel_1995_Topics_13.pdf
text.pmy:
Manokwari dan Fak-Fak menjadi pusat pemerintahan Belanda yang menetap pada 1898. Pos tersebut memperluas kehadiran negara kolonial setelah klaim sebelumnya meninggalkan sebagian besar wilayah di luar pemerintahan rutin. Jangkauan pemerintah tetap tidak merata.

Pejabat mengandalkan perantara, jaringan misi, dan pemimpin setempat yang dipilih. Berdirinya pos tidak membuat seluruh masyarakat di sekitarnya langsung mengikuti lembaga yang sama. Foto dan memorandum pemerintahan mencatat sebagian proses ini, terutama melalui sudut pandang pembuat rekaman kolonial.

Pos tetap mengubah hubungan dengan kuasa luar. Pejabat kini dapat mencatat penduduk, menunjuk perantara dan menangani perselisihan dari pangkalan yang menetap. Masyarakat pantai menghadapi pemerintahan yang ingin menjadikan penggolongan serta tuntutannya bagian kehidupan rutin. Wewenang Papua tidak hilang begitu saja, tetapi hubungannya dengan kuasa luar menjadi lebih berkelanjutan. Pemerintahan meluas melalui pelabuhan tertentu sebelum masuk pedalaman, sehingga pengalaman masyarakat dengan negara kolonial berbeda menurut tempat dan waktu. Sumber: Topics relating to Netherlands New Guinea in nineteenth-century memoranda J. A. Overweel · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-10/Overweel_1995_Topics_13.pdf

text.en:
A Dutch administrative station was established at Merauke in 1902. Expansion in the south involved policing, mission activity and intervention in local settlements and movement. The colonial record describes these measures through the government’s own objectives.

Research on missions and schools shows that administration did not advance through European officials alone. Non-European teachers and local relationships were central to the process. The effects on children, communities and authority need to be read as part of Papuan history, as well as the history of the colonial state.

The southern station linked river and coastal movement with a new administrative centre. Policing and mission schooling brought decisions about where people lived, how children learned and which authorities intervened in disputes into closer contact with colonial power. For Marind communities, these changes entered an existing social landscape of kinship, ritual and exchange. The history of Merauke therefore includes the reorganisation of local life, alongside the establishment of a town and a government office. Sources: Topics relating to Netherlands New Guinea in nineteenth-century memoranda J. A. Overweel · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-10/Overweel_1995_Topics_13.pdf; Educating Children, Civilizing Society Maaike Derksen · International Review of Social History https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/international-review-of-social-history/article/educating-children-civilizing-society-missionary-schools-and-noneuropean-teachers-in-south-dutch-new-guinea-19021942/2991790133D3B7E11667F9C5AFE1B065
text.pmy:
Pos pemerintahan Belanda didirikan di Merauke pada 1902. Perluasan kekuasaan di selatan melibatkan kepolisian, misi, serta campur tangan dalam permukiman dan pergerakan masyarakat. Rekaman kolonial menjelaskan tindakan itu melalui tujuan pemerintah sendiri.

Penelitian tentang misi dan sekolah menunjukkan bahwa pemerintahan tidak berkembang melalui pejabat Eropa saja. Guru non-Eropa dan hubungan setempat menjadi bagian penting prosesnya. Dampaknya terhadap anak, masyarakat, dan kewenangan perlu dibaca sebagai sejarah Papua sekaligus sejarah negara kolonial.

Pos selatan menghubungkan perjalanan sungai serta pantai dengan pusat pemerintahan baru. Kepolisian dan sekolah misi membawa keputusan tentang tempat tinggal, pendidikan anak serta penanganan perselisihan ke dalam hubungan lebih dekat dengan kuasa kolonial. Bagi masyarakat Marind, perubahan masuk ke kehidupan yang sudah memiliki kekerabatan, ritual dan pertukaran. Sejarah Merauke karena itu mencakup penataan ulang kehidupan setempat, selain berdirinya kota dan kantor pemerintahan. Sumber: Topics relating to Netherlands New Guinea in nineteenth-century memoranda J. A. Overweel · 1995 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2004-10/Overweel_1995_Topics_13.pdf; Educating Children, Civilizing Society Maaike Derksen · International Review of Social History https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/international-review-of-social-history/article/educating-children-civilizing-society-missionary-schools-and-noneuropean-teachers-in-south-dutch-new-guinea-19021942/2991790133D3B7E11667F9C5AFE1B065

text.en:
Mission schools in southern Dutch New Guinea combined teaching with projects to change settlement, family life and social practice. Research follows the work of non-European teachers as well as missionaries, showing that education was mediated through people with different backgrounds and aims.

Schooling opened new routes to literacy and employment while also advancing colonial intervention. Boarding arrangements and efforts to separate children from their home environments could disrupt family relationships. Papuan responses were varied; participation, adaptation and resistance belong in the account alongside the institutions’ stated purposes.

Teachers were intermediaries between the mission’s programme and the families whose children attended. Their language skills and local relationships could determine whether lessons took root or met resistance. Training children for a new social order also made schooling a struggle over authority: missionaries sought to change practices at home, while families retained their own expectations for children. Literacy created tools later used by Papuan organisers, but access to it was entangled with attempts to reorganise Indigenous life. Sources: Educating Children, Civilizing Society Maaike Derksen · International Review of Social History https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/international-review-of-social-history/article/educating-children-civilizing-society-missionary-schools-and-noneuropean-teachers-in-south-dutch-new-guinea-19021942/2991790133D3B7E11667F9C5AFE1B065
text.pmy:
Sekolah misi di selatan Nugini Belanda menggabungkan pengajaran dengan proyek perubahan permukiman, kehidupan keluarga, dan praktik sosial. Penelitian mengikuti kerja guru non-Eropa serta misionaris, sehingga memperlihatkan bahwa pendidikan berlangsung melalui orang dengan latar dan tujuan yang beragam.

Sekolah membuka jalan menuju literasi dan pekerjaan sekaligus memperluas campur tangan kolonial. Sistem asrama dan upaya menjauhkan anak dari lingkungan asal dapat mengganggu hubungan keluarga. Tanggapan Papua beragam; keikutsertaan, penyesuaian, dan perlawanan perlu dicatat bersama tujuan lembaga.

Guru menjadi penghubung antara program misi dan keluarga murid. Kemampuan bahasa serta hubungan setempat dapat menentukan apakah pengajaran diterima atau ditolak. Pendidikan untuk tatanan sosial baru juga menjadi perebutan wewenang: misionaris ingin mengubah praktik di rumah, sedangkan keluarga memiliki harapan sendiri bagi anak. Baca-tulis memberi alat yang kemudian digunakan penggerak Papua, tetapi aksesnya berkaitan dengan upaya menata ulang kehidupan masyarakat adat. Sumber: Educating Children, Civilizing Society Maaike Derksen · International Review of Social History https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/international-review-of-social-history/article/educating-children-civilizing-society-missionary-schools-and-noneuropean-teachers-in-south-dutch-new-guinea-19021942/2991790133D3B7E11667F9C5AFE1B065

text.en:
After the 1926–1927 uprisings in the Netherlands East Indies, Dutch authorities exiled political prisoners to the Boven Digoel detention settlement at Tanahmerah. The camp was remote from the colonial centres on Java, but situated within an inhabited southern Papuan landscape, along the Digul River.

The settlement extended colonial administration and coercive institutions into the interior. Accounts of the exiles describe confinement, work, illness and political networks; the location also connected the camp with Papuan communities, river transport and the administration based in Merauke. The camp photograph in this account records its built environment, rather than the whole experience of people living around it.

Digoel also worked as a threat to organisers far from Papua. Accounts of isolation and disease circulated through newspapers, making exile there an instrument of intimidation throughout the colony. Authorities presented the settlement as a place of supervision and re-education, while prisoners experienced removal from their communities and political networks. Papua was used to confine opponents of colonial rule even as Papuan communities faced the extension of that same rule along their rivers. Sources: West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea; Boven Digoel: Projecting a New Society Southeast Asian Studies · 2025 https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/seas/14/1/14_87/_pdf/-char/en
text.pmy:
Setelah pemberontakan 1926–1927 di Hindia Belanda, pemerintah kolonial mengasingkan tahanan politik ke permukiman penahanan Boven Digoel di Tanahmerah. Kamp ini jauh dari pusat pemerintahan kolonial di Jawa, tetapi berada dalam bentang selatan Papua yang telah dihuni, di sepanjang Sungai Digul.

Permukiman ini memperluas pemerintahan kolonial dan lembaga pemaksaan ke pedalaman. Catatan para buangan membahas pembatasan, pekerjaan, penyakit, dan jaringan politik; letaknya juga menghubungkan kamp dengan masyarakat Papua, transportasi sungai, serta pemerintahan di Merauke. Foto kamp dalam bagian ini merekam lingkungan bangunannya, bukan seluruh pengalaman masyarakat di sekitarnya.
