Digoel juga menjadi ancaman bagi penggerak yang tinggal jauh dari Papua. Kisah keterasingan serta penyakit beredar melalui surat kabar, menjadikan pengasingan alat intimidasi di seluruh koloni. Pemerintah menggambarkan permukiman sebagai tempat pengawasan dan pendidikan ulang, sedangkan tahanan dipisahkan dari masyarakat serta jaringan politiknya. Papua digunakan untuk mengurung penentang kolonialisme ketika masyarakat Papua sendiri menghadapi perluasan pemerintahan yang sama di sepanjang sungainya. Sumber: West New Guinea: Social, Biological, and Material Histories Gaffney & Tolla · ANU Press · 2025 https://press.anu.edu.au/publications/series/terra-australis/west-new-guinea; Boven Digoel: Projecting a New Society Southeast Asian Studies · 2025 https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/seas/14/1/14_87/_pdf/-char/en

text.en:
Koreri traditions in the Biak-Numfor region connect ideas of renewal with religious and political imagination. The large movements of 1938–1943 brought those ideas into encounters with colonial administration, missions and wartime occupation. Participants did not all give Koreri the same meaning.

Missionary-scholar Kamma documented the movement through participant accounts and his own interpretation. Koreri demonstrates that Papuan political imagination had a history before the institutions and symbols of Dutch decolonisation in 1961.

Kamma traces the major movement from Supiori into Biak, Numfor and Yapen, with leaders including Stephanus Simopyaref. Expectations of Manseren Manggundi’s return joined hopes for renewed life with resistance to outside domination. Missionary teaching, colonial demands and then Japanese occupation entered that field of expectations. Organising and armed resistance during the occupation met violent repression. The sequence places Indigenous ideas of renewal and collective action within the political history before the later referendum and diplomatic movements. Sources: Koreri: Messianic Movements in the Biak-Numfor Culture Area Freerk Kamma · 1972 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2003-10/Kamma%201972_koreri.pdf
text.pmy:
Tradisi Koreri di wilayah Biak-Numfor menghubungkan gagasan pembaruan dengan imajinasi keagamaan dan politik. Gerakan besar 1938–1943 membawa gagasan tersebut ke dalam perjumpaan dengan pemerintahan kolonial, misi, serta pendudukan perang. Para peserta tidak semuanya memberi Koreri makna yang sama.

Misionaris-peneliti Kamma mendokumentasikan gerakan melalui kesaksian peserta serta penafsirannya sendiri. Koreri memperlihatkan bahwa gagasan politik Papua sudah berkembang sebelum lembaga dan simbol dekolonisasi Belanda pada 1961.

Kamma menelusuri gerakan besar dari Supiori ke Biak, Numfor dan Yapen, dengan tokoh termasuk Stephanus Simopyaref. Harapan kembalinya Manseren Manggundi menghubungkan pembaruan kehidupan dengan penolakan terhadap penguasaan luar. Pengajaran misi, tuntutan kolonial dan kemudian pendudukan Jepang masuk ke dalam harapan tersebut. Pengorganisasian serta perlawanan bersenjata pada masa pendudukan menghadapi penindasan keras. Urutan ini menempatkan gagasan pembaruan dan tindakan bersama masyarakat Papua dalam sejarah politik sebelum gerakan referendum serta diplomasi kemudian. Sumber: Koreri: Messianic Movements in the Biak-Numfor Culture Area Freerk Kamma · 1972 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2003-10/Kamma%201972_koreri.pdf

text.en:
Japanese occupation and Allied campaigns transformed parts of New Guinea into military landscapes. Biak and Hollandia were major sites in the 1944 campaigns. Airfields, wrecks and other material remains continue to mark places where Papuan communities lived through occupation, labour demands and fighting.

Military archives often focus on operations and equipment. Archaeological work on Biak adds another route into the record, while local memory can describe experiences left out of official accounts. A wartime photograph documents a particular scene; it does not by itself explain the civilian experience around it.

The remains surveyed on Biak include defensive positions, aircraft, vehicles and wrecks on land and underwater. They show how infrastructure for war occupied the same island landscape used for settlements and subsistence. After the fighting, these objects became part of local places and memory rather than disappearing with the armies. The war also interrupted the colonial order: the Dutch return after Japan’s defeat occurred amid Indonesian independence and a new struggle over the future of West New Guinea. Sources: Tracing the remains of World War II on Biak Island ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch14.pdf; Constructing Papuan Nationalism Richard Chauvel · 2005 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf
text.pmy:
Pendudukan Jepang dan operasi Sekutu mengubah sebagian Nugini menjadi bentang militer. Biak dan Hollandia menjadi lokasi utama operasi 1944. Lapangan terbang, bangkai peralatan, dan sisa lain masih menandai tempat masyarakat Papua mengalami pendudukan, tuntutan tenaga kerja, dan pertempuran.

Arsip militer sering berpusat pada operasi serta perlengkapan. Penelitian arkeologi Biak menambah jalur pembacaan, sementara ingatan setempat dapat menjelaskan pengalaman di luar catatan resmi. Foto perang merekam adegan tertentu; foto itu sendiri tidak menjelaskan seluruh pengalaman warga sipil di sekitarnya.

Peninggalan yang diteliti di Biak mencakup pertahanan, pesawat, kendaraan serta bangkai di darat dan bawah air. Infrastruktur perang menggunakan bentang pulau yang sama dengan permukiman dan penghidupan warga. Setelah pertempuran, benda menjadi bagian tempat serta ingatan setempat, tidak menghilang bersama pasukan. Perang juga memutus pemerintahan kolonial. Kembalinya Belanda setelah kekalahan Jepang berlangsung di tengah kemerdekaan Indonesia serta perebutan baru mengenai masa depan barat Nugini. Sumber: Tracing the remains of World War II on Biak Island ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch14.pdf; Constructing Papuan Nationalism Richard Chauvel · 2005 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf

text.en:
The 1949 transfer of Dutch sovereignty to Indonesia left West New Guinea under Dutch administration. Indonesia claimed it as part of the former Netherlands East Indies; Dutch policy increasingly pursued a separate political future. The unresolved territory became a diplomatic dispute, but political organising within Papua also took several directions.

In Serui, Silas Papare’s organising connected Papua with the Indonesian republic. Johan Ariks and other leaders advocated a distinct Papuan future. Chauvel’s regional study follows these different positions through Serui, Biak, Hollandia and Fakfak, where local networks, education and relations with officials shaped political choices.

Petitions, parties and delegations became ways to address the Netherlands, Indonesia and the United Nations. These records reveal named participants and changing demands before the Council of 1961. They also show why later accounts of decolonisation need to include Papuan political disagreement and participation, alongside negotiations between states.

The dispute left Papuans living under a colonial government while two states argued over their future. Regional organisers used the openings available to them to press different programmes. Education and employment connected people across communities, making a territory-wide public life more possible. By the end of the 1950s, this organising could no longer be described only as a dispute inherited from the Netherlands East Indies: Papuan participants were asserting political demands of their own. Sources: Constructing Papuan Nationalism: History, Ethnicity, and Adaptation Richard Chauvel · 2005 · pp. 20–35 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf; Papuan Petitions as an Archive of Decolonisation Emma Kluge · Journal of Imperial and Commonwealth History https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/03086534.2025.2500357
text.pmy:
Penyerahan kedaulatan Belanda kepada Indonesia pada 1949 meninggalkan Nugini Barat di bawah pemerintahan Belanda. Indonesia mengklaimnya sebagai bagian bekas Hindia Belanda; kebijakan Belanda makin mengarah pada masa depan politik yang terpisah. Wilayah yang belum disepakati ini menjadi sengketa diplomatik, sementara organisasi politik di Papua berkembang dalam beberapa arah.

Di Serui, kegiatan Silas Papare menghubungkan Papua dengan Republik Indonesia. Johan Ariks dan tokoh lain memperjuangkan masa depan Papua yang tersendiri. Kajian regional Chauvel mengikuti perbedaan sikap ini di Serui, Biak, Hollandia, dan Fakfak, tempat jaringan setempat, pendidikan, serta hubungan dengan pejabat membentuk pilihan politik.

Petisi, partai, dan delegasi menjadi cara menyampaikan tuntutan kepada Belanda, Indonesia, dan Perserikatan Bangsa-Bangsa. Catatan ini memperlihatkan para pelaku serta perubahan tuntutan sebelum Dewan 1961. Sejarah dekolonisasi dengan demikian mencakup perbedaan pendapat dan partisipasi politik Papua, bersama perundingan antarnegara.

Sengketa meninggalkan orang Papua di bawah pemerintahan kolonial ketika dua negara memperebutkan masa depannya. Penggerak regional menggunakan kesempatan yang tersedia untuk menyampaikan program berbeda. Pendidikan dan pekerjaan menghubungkan masyarakat, memungkinkan kehidupan publik yang lebih luas. Menjelang akhir 1950-an, pengorganisasian ini tidak lagi dapat dipahami hanya sebagai sengketa warisan Hindia Belanda. Orang Papua sudah menyampaikan tuntutan politiknya sendiri. Sumber: Constructing Papuan Nationalism: History, Ethnicity, and Adaptation Richard Chauvel · 2005 · pp. 20–35 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf; Papuan Petitions as an Archive of Decolonisation Emma Kluge · Journal of Imperial and Commonwealth History https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/03086534.2025.2500357

text.en:
In the final period of Dutch rule, expanded schooling and Papuan participation in administration helped form a new institutional political field. Papuanisation was also part of a Dutch programme for the territory’s future, pursued amid the dispute with Indonesia.

Papuan organisers were not one unified bloc. They debated independence, relations with Indonesia and the pace and form of political change. Council proceedings and later historical studies should be read alongside those differing aspirations, rather than treating Papuan politics as only the product of Dutch policy.

Schools, administrative work and political meetings put representatives from different regions in contact. They supplied skills for writing petitions, debating policy and organising delegations. These institutions remained colonial, but Papuan participants used them to articulate claims that were not reducible to Dutch interests. The Council of 1961 grew out of this expanding public field. Its formation raised a practical question that would continue through later movements: who could speak for the territory, and how would its many communities take part? Sources: Papua Road Map LIPI · 2009 https://www.obor.or.id/Papua-Road-Map; Constructing Papuan Nationalism Richard Chauvel · East-West Center · 2005 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf
text.pmy:
Pada periode akhir pemerintahan Belanda, perluasan sekolah serta keikutsertaan orang Papua dalam administrasi membantu membentuk ruang politik kelembagaan baru. Papuanisasi juga menjadi bagian program Belanda untuk masa depan wilayah, di tengah sengketa dengan Indonesia.

Pengorganisasi Papua bukan satu kelompok yang seragam. Mereka memperdebatkan kemerdekaan, hubungan dengan Indonesia, serta kecepatan dan bentuk perubahan politik. Catatan dewan dan kajian sejarah perlu dibaca bersama aspirasi yang berbeda itu, bukan memperlakukan politik Papua semata-mata sebagai hasil kebijakan Belanda.

Sekolah, pekerjaan pemerintahan dan pertemuan politik mempertemukan wakil berbagai wilayah. Keterampilan menulis petisi, membahas kebijakan serta membentuk delegasi berkembang melalui hubungan ini. Lembaganya masih kolonial, tetapi orang Papua menggunakannya untuk menyampaikan tuntutan yang tidak sama dengan kepentingan Belanda. Dewan 1961 muncul dari kehidupan publik yang meluas tersebut. Pembentukannya membawa pertanyaan yang terus hadir dalam gerakan kemudian: siapa yang dapat berbicara untuk wilayah ini dan bagaimana beragam masyarakatnya ikut menentukan? Sumber: Papua Road Map LIPI · 2009 https://www.obor.or.id/Papua-Road-Map; Constructing Papuan Nationalism Richard Chauvel · East-West Center · 2005 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf

text.en:
The New Guinea Council opened in Hollandia on 5 April 1961. Its elected and appointed members debated government and the territory’s future while Indonesia demanded a transfer and the Netherlands proposed preparations for self-determination. The Council gave Papuan representatives an institutional platform, within a colonial administration that still controlled the timetable.

On 19 October, a meeting in Hollandia established a Papuan National Committee and issued a political manifesto. It called for the name West Papua, the Morning Star flag and the anthem Hai Tanahku Papua. Nicolaas Jouwe, E.J. Bonay, Nicolaas Tanggahma and F. Torey were among the political figures seeking a Papuan voice in the negotiations.

The representatives differed over the next step. Some wanted an immediate declaration of independence; others favoured introducing national symbols before a transfer of sovereignty. The Morning Star was raised alongside the Dutch flag on 1 December, while colonial government continued. These debates document Papuan political initiatives that cannot be reduced to the competing Dutch and Indonesian positions.

The symbols gave a common public form to aspirations developed through regional parties, petitions and political meetings. The flag and anthem could travel beyond the Council chamber and link communities with different languages. Their introduction did not settle sovereignty, but it made Papuan participation in deciding the territory’s future visible. When the Netherlands and Indonesia negotiated the following year without Papuan signatories, this institutional and popular organising was excluded from the agreement that determined the transfer. Sources: Constructing Papuan Nationalism: History, Ethnicity, and Adaptation Richard Chauvel · 2005 · pp. 20–35 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf
text.pmy:
Dewan Nugini dibuka di Hollandia pada 5 April 1961. Anggota yang dipilih dan ditunjuk membahas pemerintahan serta masa depan wilayah ketika Indonesia menuntut penyerahan dan Belanda mengusulkan persiapan penentuan nasib sendiri. Dewan memberi wakil Papua ruang kelembagaan, dalam pemerintahan kolonial yang masih mengendalikan jadwalnya.

Pada 19 Oktober, pertemuan di Hollandia membentuk Komite Nasional Papua dan mengeluarkan Manifest Politik. Dokumen ini meminta penggunaan nama Papua Barat, bendera Bintang Kejora, dan lagu Hai Tanahku Papua. Nicolaas Jouwe, E.J. Bonay, Nicolaas Tanggahma, dan F. Torey termasuk tokoh yang mengupayakan keterlibatan Papua dalam perundingan.

Para wakil berbeda pendapat tentang langkah selanjutnya. Sebagian menginginkan pernyataan kemerdekaan segera; yang lain mendukung penggunaan simbol nasional sebelum penyerahan kedaulatan. Bintang Kejora dikibarkan bersama bendera Belanda pada 1 Desember, sementara pemerintahan kolonial tetap berjalan. Perdebatan ini mencatat prakarsa politik Papua di tengah persaingan kepentingan Belanda dan Indonesia.

Simbol memberi bentuk publik bersama kepada aspirasi yang berkembang melalui partai regional, petisi serta pertemuan politik. Bendera dan lagu dapat menjangkau masyarakat dengan bahasa berbeda di luar ruang dewan. Pengenalannya belum menyelesaikan kedaulatan, tetapi memperlihatkan keikutsertaan Papua dalam menentukan masa depan wilayahnya. Ketika Belanda dan Indonesia berunding tahun berikutnya tanpa penandatangan Papua, pengorganisasian lembaga serta masyarakat ini dikeluarkan dari perjanjian yang menentukan penyerahan. Sumber: Constructing Papuan Nationalism: History, Ethnicity, and Adaptation Richard Chauvel · 2005 · pp. 20–35 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf

text.en:
Indonesia and the Netherlands signed the New York Agreement on 15 August 1962. It arranged a temporary United Nations administration before the transfer to Indonesia on 1 May 1963. It also provided for an act of self-determination before the end of 1969. Papuan representatives were not signatories. For many independence advocates, this exclusion is central: decisions about the territory’s future were negotiated by others, while the promised opportunity to choose remained ahead.

President Sukarno’s Trikora campaign and Indonesian military pressure increased the urgency of the dispute. US diplomacy sought an agreement that would preserve relations with Jakarta during the Cold War. The resulting treaty fixed the transfer timetable while leaving Papuans to exercise their political choice later, under Indonesian administration. Article XVIII provided for participation by all adult inhabitants and freedom to determine their future. That promise became the standard against which Papuans judged the process imposed in 1969. Sources: Agreement concerning West New Guinea (West Irian) United Nations Treaty Collection https://treaties.un.org/Pages/showDetails.aspx?clang=_en&objid=0800000280133981; United Nations Security Force in West New Guinea — Background United Nations Peacekeeping https://peacekeeping.un.org/sites/default/files/past/unsfbackgr.html; UN Involvement with the Act of Self Determination in West Irian, 1968–1969 John Saltford · hosted by Free West Papua Campaign https://www.freewestpapua.org/documents/un-involvement-with-the-act-of-self-determination-in-west-irian-1968-to-1969-by-john-saltford/; New York Agreement, 15 August 1962 United Nations Treaty Series https://treaties.un.org/doc/publication/unts/volume%20437/volume-437-i-6311-english.pdf; Indonesia’s 1969 Takeover of West Papua US diplomatic records · National Security Archive https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB128/
text.pmy:
Indonesia dan Belanda menandatangani Perjanjian New York pada 15 Agustus 1962. Perjanjian mengatur pemerintahan sementara PBB sebelum penyerahan administrasi kepada Indonesia pada 1 Mei 1963, serta penentuan nasib sendiri sebelum akhir 1969. Wakil Papua bukan penanda tangan. Bagi banyak pendukung kemerdekaan, pengabaian ini mendasar: masa depan wilayah dirundingkan pihak lain, sementara kesempatan yang dijanjikan untuk menentukan pilihan belum berlangsung.

Kampanye Trikora Presiden Sukarno dan tekanan militer Indonesia mempercepat sengketa. Diplomasi Amerika Serikat mencari kesepakatan yang menjaga hubungan dengan Jakarta pada Perang Dingin. Perjanjian menetapkan jadwal penyerahan, sedangkan pilihan politik Papua ditunda hingga pemerintahan Indonesia. Pasal XVIII mengatur keikutsertaan seluruh penduduk dewasa dan kebebasan menentukan masa depan. Janji ini menjadi ukuran bagi orang Papua untuk menilai proses yang diberlakukan pada 1969. Sumber: Agreement concerning West New Guinea (West Irian) United Nations Treaty Collection https://treaties.un.org/Pages/showDetails.aspx?clang=_en&objid=0800000280133981; United Nations Security Force in West New Guinea — Background United Nations Peacekeeping https://peacekeeping.un.org/sites/default/files/past/unsfbackgr.html; UN Involvement with the Act of Self Determination in West Irian, 1968–1969 John Saltford · hosted by Free West Papua Campaign https://www.freewestpapua.org/documents/un-involvement-with-the-act-of-self-determination-in-west-irian-1968-to-1969-by-john-saltford/; New York Agreement, 15 August 1962 United Nations Treaty Series https://treaties.un.org/doc/publication/unts/volume%20437/volume-437-i-6311-english.pdf; Indonesia’s 1969 Takeover of West Papua US diplomatic records · National Security Archive https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB128/

text.en:
The United Nations Temporary Executive Authority took over administration from the Netherlands on 1 October 1962. Under the New York Agreement, UNTEA was responsible for public administration, law and order, protection of inhabitants’ rights and uninterrupted services. The UN Security Force supported the existing Papuan police.

This transition involved civil servants, schools, communications, military movements and daily administration, alongside diplomacy. The agreement was signed by Indonesia and the Netherlands; Papuans were not signatories. UNTEA handed administration to Indonesia on 1 May 1963. The later procedure to determine the territory’s status remained a separate obligation under the agreement.

UNTEA’s presence put international personnel between the departing Dutch administration and the incoming Indonesian one. Maintaining schools, communications and public services required local staff, while the transfer of security responsibilities changed who exercised force. The temporary authority did not conduct the promised political choice before handing over. Its short duration meant that international administration ended years before the referendum obligation fell due, leaving the conditions for that choice increasingly in Indonesian hands. Sources: UNSF / UNTEA historical background United Nations Peacekeeping https://peacekeeping.un.org/en/mission/past/unsfbackgr.html; New York Agreement, 15 August 1962 United Nations Treaty Series https://treaties.un.org/doc/publication/unts/volume%20437/volume-437-i-6311-english.pdf
text.pmy:
United Nations Temporary Executive Authority mengambil alih administrasi dari Belanda pada 1 Oktober 1962. Menurut Perjanjian New York, UNTEA bertanggung jawab atas pemerintahan, ketertiban, pelindungan hak penduduk, serta kelangsungan layanan. Pasukan keamanan PBB membantu polisi Papua yang sudah ada.

Masa peralihan melibatkan pegawai, sekolah, komunikasi, pergerakan militer, serta pemerintahan sehari-hari, selain diplomasi. Indonesia dan Belanda menandatangani perjanjian; orang Papua bukan pihak penandatangan. UNTEA menyerahkan administrasi kepada Indonesia pada 1 Mei 1963. Prosedur penentuan status wilayah kemudian tetap menjadi kewajiban tersendiri dalam perjanjian.

Kehadiran UNTEA menempatkan petugas internasional di antara pemerintahan Belanda yang pergi dan Indonesia yang masuk. Sekolah, komunikasi serta layanan publik bergantung pada staf setempat, sementara pergantian tanggung jawab keamanan mengubah pemegang kekuatan bersenjata. Pemerintahan sementara tidak menjalankan pilihan politik yang dijanjikan sebelum menyerahkan wilayah. Masa singkatnya berakhir bertahun-tahun sebelum kewajiban penentuan nasib sendiri, sehingga kondisi pelaksanaannya semakin berada di tangan Indonesia. Sumber: UNSF / UNTEA historical background United Nations Peacekeeping https://peacekeeping.un.org/en/mission/past/unsfbackgr.html; New York Agreement, 15 August 1962 United Nations Treaty Series https://treaties.un.org/doc/publication/unts/volume%20437/volume-437-i-6311-english.pdf

text.en:
UNTEA transferred administration to Indonesia on 1 May 1963 under the New York Agreement. This was a transfer of administrative authority. The agreement’s provision for an act of self-determination remained to be implemented before the end of 1969.

Separating those stages helps explain why 1963 and 1969 appear differently in official narratives and Papuan accounts. The agreement also contained guarantees concerning rights and freedoms. Later debates concern both how the political procedure was conducted and the conditions under which Papuans could express a choice.

Under Indonesian rule, independent political activity and expression were restricted. Saltford’s study follows the banning of political parties, arrests and the use of security power in the years before Pepera. Papuans were expected to make a future choice while the institutions through which they could organise were being closed. Resistance consequently developed alongside petitions and protests. The transfer did not end the struggle over political status; it changed the authorities against whom that struggle was directed. Sources: Papua Road Map LIPI · 2009 https://www.obor.or.id/Papua-Road-Map; UN Involvement with the Act of Self-Determination John Saltford · 2000 https://resources.huygens.knaw.nl/papoeawestnieuwguinea/papers_pdf/saltford
text.pmy:
UNTEA menyerahkan administrasi kepada Indonesia pada 1 Mei 1963 berdasarkan Perjanjian New York. Tahap ini merupakan penyerahan kewenangan administrasi. Ketentuan perjanjian mengenai penentuan nasib sendiri masih harus dilaksanakan sebelum akhir 1969.

Pemisahan kedua tahap membantu menjelaskan perbedaan makna 1963 dan 1969 dalam narasi resmi serta penuturan Papua. Perjanjian juga memuat jaminan hak dan kebebasan. Perdebatan berikutnya menyangkut pelaksanaan prosedur politik sekaligus kondisi yang memungkinkan orang Papua menyatakan pilihan.

Di bawah pemerintahan Indonesia, kegiatan politik mandiri serta kebebasan berpendapat dibatasi. Kajian Saltford menelusuri pelarangan partai, penangkapan dan penggunaan kekuatan keamanan sebelum Pepera. Orang Papua dijanjikan pilihan masa depan ketika lembaga untuk mengorganisir diri ditutup. Perlawanan berkembang bersama petisi serta demonstrasi. Penyerahan tidak mengakhiri perjuangan mengenai status politik, melainkan mengubah pihak berkuasa yang dihadapi. Sumber: Papua Road Map LIPI · 2009 https://www.obor.or.id/Papua-Road-Map; UN Involvement with the Act of Self-Determination John Saltford · 2000 https://resources.huygens.knaw.nl/papoeawestnieuwguinea/papers_pdf/saltford

text.en:
Freeport signed its first contract with Indonesia in 1967, before Pepera. The company’s own history records the agreement as the start of its mining development in Papua. The mine became part of a much larger system of roads, settlements, processing and river transport.

Amungme highland and Kamoro lowland relationships with land and water are central to its local history. Company production and investment records answer different questions from community testimony about access, compensation and environmental change. Following the mine requires connecting those records rather than treating one corporate account as the whole history.

The contract placed a major economic decision before Papuans had exercised the promised choice over their political future. For Amungme communities, the highland mining area was already a lived and meaningful territory; downstream, Kamoro communities depended on rivers and lowland resources. Mine construction joined these regions through roads, settlements and waste flows. Later demands for compensation and environmental protection arose from those concrete relationships with land and water, rather than from an abstract objection to investment. Sources: History of PT Freeport Indonesia PT Freeport Indonesia https://ptfi.co.id/en/about/history; Papua Road Map LIPI · 2009 https://www.obor.or.id/Papua-Road-Map; The Amungme, Kamoro & Freeport Abigail Abrash · Cultural Survival https://www.culturalsurvival.org/publications/cultural-survival-quarterly/amungme-kamoro-freeport-how-indigenous-papuans-have
text.pmy:
Freeport menandatangani kontrak pertamanya dengan Indonesia pada 1967, sebelum Pepera. Sejarah perusahaan mencatat perjanjian itu sebagai awal pengembangan tambangnya di Papua. Tambang kemudian menjadi bagian sistem jalan, permukiman, pengolahan, dan pengangkutan melalui sungai.

Hubungan Amungme di pegunungan serta Kamoro di dataran rendah dengan tanah dan air menjadi bagian utama sejarah setempat. Catatan produksi serta investasi perusahaan menjawab pertanyaan berbeda dari kesaksian masyarakat tentang akses, ganti rugi, dan perubahan lingkungan. Pemantauan perlu menghubungkan catatan tersebut, bukan menjadikan penuturan perusahaan sebagai seluruh sejarah.

Kontrak menempatkan keputusan ekonomi besar sebelum orang Papua menjalankan pilihan yang dijanjikan mengenai masa depan politiknya. Bagi masyarakat Amungme, wilayah tambang pegunungan sudah merupakan tanah kehidupan yang bermakna. Di hilir, masyarakat Kamoro bergantung pada sungai serta sumber daya dataran rendah. Pembangunan tambang menghubungkan kawasan ini melalui jalan, permukiman dan aliran limbah. Tuntutan ganti rugi serta perlindungan lingkungan kemudian lahir dari hubungan nyata dengan tanah dan air, bukan penolakan abstrak terhadap investasi. Sumber: History of PT Freeport Indonesia PT Freeport Indonesia https://ptfi.co.id/en/about/history; Papua Road Map LIPI · 2009 https://www.obor.or.id/Papua-Road-Map; The Amungme, Kamoro & Freeport Abigail Abrash · Cultural Survival https://www.culturalsurvival.org/publications/cultural-survival-quarterly/amungme-kamoro-freeport-how-indigenous-papuans-have

text.en:
The New York Agreement promised an act of self-determination for Papua's inhabitants by the end of 1969. When Pepera took place in July and August, Indonesia used eight consultation assemblies with around a thousand selected representatives. Papuan adults were not allowed to cast individual votes. The government described this method as suited to local conditions, while controlling both the selection of participants and the proceedings.

Representatives were separated from their families before the assemblies. Historical testimony records death threats, pressure and inducements; some participants were instructed to rehearse the statements they would deliver. Demonstrations demanding a direct vote were broken up. In Biak, journalist Hugh Lunn witnessed soldiers selecting representatives and arresting protesters in front of UN officials. Every assembly was subsequently declared to support integration with Indonesia.

The UN team led by Fernando Ortiz Sanz knew how tightly political activity was controlled. US diplomatic records also show that foreign officials recognised substantial Papuan opposition and expected Indonesia to prevent an outcome favouring independence. Influential governments chose to protect their relations with Jakarta. Papuans' right to determine their future was subordinated to relations between states.

On 19 November, General Assembly Resolution 2504 took note of the Secretary-General's report on the process. There was no new vote for Papua's population. Indonesia treated Pepera's result as the basis of integration, while Papuan independence movements continued to demand the self-determination that had been promised. The control and threats surrounding Pepera became central to that demand. Sources: General Assembly Resolution 2504 (XXIV) United Nations Digital Library https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/202193; An analysis of the 1969 Act of Free Choice Thomas Musgrave · 2015 https://www.ulmwp.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Thomas-Musgrave-An-analysis-of-the-1969-Act-of-Free-Choice-in-West-Papua-2015.pdf; UN Involvement with the Act of Self-Determination John Saltford · 2000 https://resources.huygens.knaw.nl/papoeawestnieuwguinea/papers_pdf/saltford; US records on the 1969 takeover National Security Archive https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB128/; Constructing Papuan Nationalism: History, Ethnicity, and Adaptation Richard Chauvel · 2005 · p. 18 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf
text.pmy:
Perjanjian New York menjanjikan penentuan nasib sendiri bagi penduduk Papua sebelum akhir 1969. Ketika Pepera berlangsung pada Juli–Agustus, pemerintah Indonesia menggunakan delapan dewan musyawarah dengan sekitar seribu wakil pilihannya. Penduduk dewasa Papua tidak diberi kesempatan memberikan suara masing-masing. Pemerintah menyebut cara ini sesuai dengan keadaan setempat, sementara pilihan peserta dan jalannya musyawarah berada di bawah kendalinya.

Peserta dipisahkan dari keluarga sebelum musyawarah. Kesaksian yang dihimpun dalam penelitian sejarah mencatat ancaman pembunuhan, tekanan dan pemberian imbalan; sebagian peserta diperintahkan melatih pernyataan yang akan mereka bacakan. Demonstrasi yang menuntut pemungutan suara langsung dibubarkan. Di Biak, wartawan Hugh Lunn menyaksikan tentara memilih wakil dan menangkap pengunjuk rasa di hadapan petugas PBB. Hasil seluruh dewan kemudian dinyatakan mendukung integrasi dengan Indonesia.

Tim PBB yang dipimpin Fernando Ortiz Sanz mengetahui ketatnya pengendalian politik tersebut. Dokumen diplomatik Amerika Serikat juga memperlihatkan bahwa pejabat asing mengetahui besarnya penolakan Papua dan memperkirakan Indonesia tidak akan membiarkan hasil yang mendukung kemerdekaan. Pemerintah-pemerintah yang berpengaruh memilih menjaga hubungan dengan Jakarta. Hak orang Papua untuk menentukan masa depan mereka ditempatkan di bawah kepentingan hubungan antarnegara.

Pada 19 November, Resolusi Majelis Umum PBB 2504 mencatat laporan Sekretaris Jenderal mengenai proses itu. Tidak ada pemungutan suara baru bagi penduduk Papua. Indonesia menjadikan hasil Pepera dasar integrasi, sementara gerakan kemerdekaan Papua terus menuntut pemenuhan hak penentuan nasib sendiri yang telah dijanjikan. Pengendalian dan ancaman dalam Pepera menjadi bagian pokok tuntutan tersebut. Sumber: General Assembly Resolution 2504 (XXIV) United Nations Digital Library https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/202193; An analysis of the 1969 Act of Free Choice Thomas Musgrave · 2015 https://www.ulmwp.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/Thomas-Musgrave-An-analysis-of-the-1969-Act-of-Free-Choice-in-West-Papua-2015.pdf; UN Involvement with the Act of Self-Determination John Saltford · 2000 https://resources.huygens.knaw.nl/papoeawestnieuwguinea/papers_pdf/saltford; US records on the 1969 takeover National Security Archive https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB128/; Constructing Papuan Nationalism: History, Ethnicity, and Adaptation Richard Chauvel · 2005 · p. 18 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf

text.en:
Mining, plantations and migration changed livelihoods and control over land. An economic project could be described by government or business as development while the people living there experienced loss of forests, food sources or decision-making power. Research by AJAR and the Papuan Women’s Working Group begins with these lived relationships. Its case studies ask what land means to women and how they respond when forests become concessions.

Women’s accounts show how a change in land control redistributes work. Families may travel further for food, rely more on cash or lose places where children learned from older relatives. The consequences continue after a clearing operation or compensation meeting has ended. AJAR’s participatory research follows women who maintain knowledge, organise with others and insist on being heard in land decisions. Their experience puts the ongoing costs of extraction alongside the revenue and infrastructure used to justify it. Sources: All the Birds Are Gone AJAR and the Papuan Women’s Working Group https://asia-ajar.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/ABAG_FINAL_compressed.pdf; Grasberg Mine, Indonesia NASA Earth Observatory https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/grasberg-mine-indonesia-5718/
text.pmy:
Pertambangan, perkebunan, dan migrasi mengubah penghidupan serta penguasaan tanah. Proyek yang disebut pembangunan oleh pemerintah atau perusahaan dapat dialami penduduk sebagai kehilangan hutan, sumber pangan, atau kuasa mengambil keputusan. Penelitian AJAR dan Kelompok Kerja Perempuan Papua bertolak dari hubungan yang dialami sehari-hari. Studi kasusnya membahas arti tanah bagi perempuan dan tanggapan mereka ketika hutan menjadi konsesi.

Kesaksian perempuan menunjukkan bagaimana perubahan penguasaan tanah mengubah pekerjaan. Keluarga dapat berjalan lebih jauh untuk pangan, lebih bergantung pada uang atau kehilangan tempat anak belajar dari kerabat tua. Akibatnya berlangsung setelah pembukaan lahan atau pertemuan ganti rugi selesai. Penelitian partisipatif AJAR mengikuti perempuan yang menjaga pengetahuan, mengorganisir diri dan menuntut suara dalam keputusan tanah. Pengalaman mereka menempatkan biaya pengambilan sumber daya yang terus berjalan di samping pendapatan serta infrastruktur yang digunakan sebagai pembenarannya. Sumber: All the Birds Are Gone AJAR and the Papuan Women’s Working Group https://asia-ajar.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/ABAG_FINAL_compressed.pdf; Grasberg Mine, Indonesia NASA Earth Observatory https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/grasberg-mine-indonesia-5718/

text.en:
Opposition to Indonesian rule spread in parts of the highlands before the 1977 election. Residents refused to participate, while OPM forces attacked posts and damaged airstrips. Indonesia's military deployed ground and aerial operations. Attacks reached villages around Wamena, the Baliem Valley, Karubaga and Bokondini, with civilians subjected to violence.

Survivors described aerial bombing and strafing, burned homes, arrests, torture, sexual violence and killings. Some residents who did not recognise warplanes went into the open, believing the aircraft carried assistance. Research by the Asian Human Rights Commission and International Coalition for Papua also connects the aerial attacks to OV-10 Bronco aircraft and helicopter deployments through military accounts and contemporary reporting.

Families left their homes and gardens to seek shelter. Hunger and disease caused further deaths among people who survived the direct attacks. Interviewed decades later, survivors still remembered parents, children, partners and neighbours they had lost. The investigation published in 2013 compiled 4,146 names of people reported killed from interviews in 15 districts; its record did not cover every victim.

Displacement broke up village life and access to food. Returning families faced the loss of relatives and damage to their livelihoods, while survivors continued to demand disclosure and accountability for the military operations. Sources: Central Highlands investigation, 1977–78 Asian Human Rights Commission · 2013 https://tapol.org/sites/default/files/sites/default/files/pdfs/NeglectedGenocideAHRC.pdf
text.pmy:
Menjelang pemilihan umum 1977, penolakan terhadap pemerintahan Indonesia meluas di sejumlah wilayah pegunungan. Warga menolak mengikuti pemilu, sementara pasukan OPM menyerang pos dan merusak lapangan terbang. Militer Indonesia mengerahkan operasi darat dan udara. Serangan menjangkau kampung-kampung di sekitar Wamena, Baliem, Karubaga dan Bokondini, dengan warga sipil menjadi sasaran kekerasan.

Kesaksian penyintas mencatat pengeboman dan penembakan dari udara, pembakaran rumah, penangkapan, penyiksaan, kekerasan seksual dan pembunuhan. Warga yang tidak mengenali pesawat perang keluar ke tempat terbuka, mengira pesawat membawa bantuan. Penelitian Asian Human Rights Commission dan International Coalition for Papua juga menghubungkan serangan udara dengan pengerahan pesawat OV-10 Bronco serta helikopter melalui catatan militer dan laporan pada masa itu.

Keluarga meninggalkan rumah dan kebun untuk berlindung. Kelaparan dan penyakit menambah kematian di antara mereka yang selamat dari serangan langsung. Penyintas yang diwawancarai puluhan tahun kemudian masih mengingat orang tua, anak, pasangan dan tetangga yang hilang. Penyelidikan yang diterbitkan pada 2013 menghimpun 4.146 nama orang yang dilaporkan meninggal dari wawancara di 15 distrik; catatan tersebut tidak mencakup seluruh korban.

Pengungsian memutus kehidupan kampung dan akses terhadap pangan. Keluarga yang kembali harus hidup dengan kehilangan anggota keluarga dan kerusakan penghidupan, sementara penyintas terus menuntut pengungkapan kekerasan dan pertanggungjawaban atas operasi tersebut. Sumber: Central Highlands investigation, 1977–78 Asian Human Rights Commission · 2013 https://tapol.org/sites/default/files/sites/default/files/pdfs/NeglectedGenocideAHRC.pdf

text.en:
Mambesak was founded on 5 August 1978 in Jayapura. Led by anthropologist, musician and museum curator Arnold Ap, the group gathered songs from different Papuan regions and brought them into performances, cassette recordings and radio. Students from several communities participated. Weekly performances at the university museum made it a meeting place where people could hear their own languages and learn those of others.

That work connected cultural documentation with public confidence in being Papuan. Songs and stories could circulate beyond the communities where they originated without losing their local roots. The museum became a place of teaching rather than only a store of collected objects. Mambesak’s reach also made it a target for authorities who regarded Papuan cultural organising as a political threat.

Ap was murdered in 1984 and the group disbanded. Its recordings and the memories of surviving members continued to carry the work beyond that rupture. The documentary Muman Minggil follows filmmakers Yonri Revolt and Mahardhika Yhuda as they recover this history through interviews, radio programmes and cassette tapes. It reconnects today’s listeners with an experiment in cultural education that violence ended but did not erase. Sources: Muman Minggil: Road to the Ancestors Yoikatra Association / Cenderawasih University Cultural Museum · Restitution Matters https://restitutionmatters.org/publication/muman-minggil-docu-about-a-cultural-papuan-group-colonialism-and-restitution/
text.pmy:
Mambesak berdiri pada 5 Agustus 1978 di Jayapura. Dipimpin antropolog, musisi dan kurator museum Arnold Ap, kelompok ini menghimpun lagu dari berbagai wilayah Papua untuk pertunjukan, rekaman kaset dan radio. Mahasiswa dari sejumlah masyarakat ikut terlibat. Pertunjukan mingguan di museum universitas menjadikannya tempat pertemuan untuk mendengar bahasa sendiri serta mengenal bahasa orang lain.

Pekerjaan itu menghubungkan dokumentasi budaya dengan kepercayaan diri sebagai orang Papua. Lagu serta cerita beredar di luar masyarakat asalnya sambil tetap membawa akar setempat. Museum menjadi tempat belajar, bukan hanya penyimpanan benda. Jangkauan Mambesak juga menjadikannya sasaran aparat yang memandang pengorganisasian budaya Papua sebagai ancaman politik.

Ap dibunuh pada 1984 dan kelompok ini bubar. Rekaman serta ingatan anggota yang masih hidup terus membawa karya mereka setelah peristiwa tersebut. Dokumenter Muman Minggil mengikuti Yonri Revolt dan Mahardhika Yhuda yang menelusuri sejarah ini melalui wawancara, siaran radio dan kaset. Film menghubungkan pendengar sekarang dengan usaha pendidikan budaya yang dihentikan oleh kekerasan tetapi tidak terhapus. Sumber: Muman Minggil: Road to the Ancestors Yoikatra Association / Cenderawasih University Cultural Museum · Restitution Matters https://restitutionmatters.org/publication/muman-minggil-docu-about-a-cultural-papuan-group-colonialism-and-restitution/

title.en: FORERI, Team 100 and the Papuan Congress

text.en:
After Suharto’s fall, Papuan organisers sought to turn the political opening into a decision about independence. FORERI, the Forum for Reconciliation of Irian Jaya, brought church figures, academics and civil-society participants into a shared process. In February 1999, a Team of 100 met President B.J. Habibie in Jakarta and presented an independence demand. The delegation connected regional networks beyond the older political elite of Hollandia.

The Mubes in February 2000 and the second Papuan Congress, held from 29 May to 4 June, consolidated the Papuan Presidium Council. Participants debated representation and the history of the territory’s incorporation into Indonesia. Public meetings made demands previously suppressed under military rule visible across communities. The movement’s leadership sought a shared political mandate, while differing regional experiences continued to shape its membership and priorities.

Jakarta did not accept the independence demand. The widening public space coexisted with arrests and renewed restrictions on pro-independence organising. Biak’s violence had already shown the danger of assuming that Reformasi would protect Papuan political expression. The Congress period was followed by the killing of Theys Eluay and the introduction of special autonomy in 2001. The opening produced enduring institutions and networks without delivering the political choice their participants sought. Sources: Constructing Papuan Nationalism: History, Ethnicity, and Adaptation Richard Chauvel · 2005 · pp. 11–19 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf
text.pmy:
Setelah Suharto jatuh, penggerak Papua berusaha mengubah pembukaan politik menjadi keputusan mengenai kemerdekaan. FORERI, Forum Rekonsiliasi Rakyat Irian Jaya, mempertemukan tokoh gereja, akademisi dan masyarakat sipil. Pada Februari 1999, Tim 100 bertemu Presiden B.J. Habibie di Jakarta dan menyampaikan tuntutan kemerdekaan. Delegasi menghubungkan jaringan regional di luar elite politik lama Hollandia.

Mubes Februari 2000 serta Kongres Papua II pada 29 Mei–4 Juni mengukuhkan Presidium Dewan Papua. Peserta membahas keterwakilan dan sejarah penggabungan wilayah ke Indonesia. Pertemuan publik menyebarkan tuntutan yang sebelumnya ditekan pemerintahan militer. Pemimpin gerakan mencari mandat politik bersama, sementara pengalaman regional yang berbeda tetap membentuk anggota serta prioritasnya.

Jakarta tidak menerima tuntutan kemerdekaan. Ruang publik yang meluas tetap disertai penangkapan serta pembatasan kembali pengorganisasian kemerdekaan. Kekerasan Biak sudah memperlihatkan bahaya menganggap Reformasi akan melindungi ekspresi politik Papua. Masa kongres diikuti pembunuhan Theys Eluay serta pemberlakuan otonomi khusus pada 2001. Pembukaan menghasilkan lembaga dan jaringan yang bertahan, tetapi belum memberikan pilihan politik yang dituntut pesertanya. Sumber: Constructing Papuan Nationalism: History, Ethnicity, and Adaptation Richard Chauvel · 2005 · pp. 11–19 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf

text.en:
Papuan women’s testimony records violence alongside the work of sustaining families, gardens and community relationships. AJAR’s collection, I am Here, brings together accounts developed through participatory work with women. The stories describe particular experiences rather than a representative statistical sample of all Papuan women.

These accounts broaden what counts as political history. Displacement, access to land and the loss of relatives affect everyday labour and the transmission of knowledge. Reading the voices themselves also preserves differences between places and generations that a general summary can flatten.

The women describe a continuity between violence and its aftermath: losing a relative can leave someone responsible for children, food and income while still seeking information about the death. Displacement can remove the land and relationships that made those tasks possible. Speaking together creates a record of these burdens and of the responses women organised. Their testimony makes survival, care and the demand for truth part of the same history, rather than treating women only as witnesses to events carried out by others. Sources: I am Here: Voices of Papuan Women AJAR · 2019 https://asia-ajar.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/I-am-Here-Voices-of-Papuan-Women-2019.pdf
text.pmy:
Kesaksian perempuan Papua mencatat kekerasan bersama pekerjaan menopang keluarga, kebun, dan hubungan masyarakat. Koleksi AJAR, I am Here, menghimpun penuturan melalui kerja partisipatif bersama perempuan. Cerita tersebut menggambarkan pengalaman tertentu, bukan sampel statistik yang mewakili seluruh perempuan Papua.

Penuturan ini memperluas cakupan sejarah politik. Pengungsian, akses tanah, dan kehilangan kerabat memengaruhi kerja sehari-hari serta pewarisan pengetahuan. Membaca suara mereka secara langsung juga mempertahankan perbedaan tempat dan generasi yang dapat hilang dalam ringkasan umum.

Para perempuan menghubungkan kekerasan dengan akibatnya: kehilangan kerabat dapat meninggalkan tanggung jawab atas anak, pangan dan penghasilan, sambil terus mencari penjelasan tentang kematian tersebut. Pengungsian dapat memutus akses ke tanah serta hubungan yang memungkinkan pekerjaan itu. Berbicara bersama merekam beban tersebut dan tindakan yang mereka bangun. Kesaksian menjadikan bertahan hidup, merawat dan menuntut kebenaran bagian sejarah yang sama, bukan menempatkan perempuan hanya sebagai saksi tindakan orang lain. Sumber: I am Here: Voices of Papuan Women AJAR · 2019 https://asia-ajar.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/I-am-Here-Voices-of-Papuan-Women-2019.pdf

text.en:
Law No. 21 of 2001 established special autonomy for Papua within Indonesia, following the independence mobilisation of 1998–2000. It provided additional provincial authority and financing and recognised Indigenous participation, customary rights and protections for human rights. The government offered an institutional response to Papuan demands while retaining Indonesian sovereignty over the territory.

The law provided for the Majelis Rakyat Papua, representing customary, religious and women’s constituencies. This body had a different role from an elected provincial legislature: it was intended to protect Indigenous interests within the autonomy framework. Recognition of customary rights and Papuan participation created grounds on which communities could demand that government decisions account for their position.

The framework did not meet the independence movement’s demand to determine political status. Its practical value depended on forming institutions, implementing protections and making public spending accountable to the people it was meant to serve. Later disputes over consultation, revisions and new provinces returned to the same issue of representation. Special autonomy changed the machinery of government without resolving the self-determination claim that had brought people into the streets and Congress. Sources: UU No. 21 Tahun 2001 — Otonomi Khusus Bagi Provinsi Papua BPK RI — Peraturan https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/44901/uu-no-21-tahun-2001
text.pmy:
Undang-Undang 21 Tahun 2001 menetapkan otonomi khusus Papua di dalam Indonesia setelah pengorganisasian kemerdekaan 1998–2000. Undang-undang mengatur kewenangan serta pendanaan tambahan, keikutsertaan orang asli, hak adat dan perlindungan HAM. Pemerintah menawarkan jawaban kelembagaan atas tuntutan Papua sambil mempertahankan kedaulatan Indonesia atas wilayah ini.

Undang-undang mengatur Majelis Rakyat Papua yang mewakili unsur adat, agama dan perempuan. Perannya berbeda dari legislatif provinsi yang dipilih: MRP dimaksudkan melindungi kepentingan orang asli dalam kerangka otonomi. Pengakuan hak adat serta keikutsertaan Papua memberi dasar bagi masyarakat untuk menuntut keputusan pemerintah yang memperhatikan kedudukan mereka.

Kerangka ini tidak memenuhi tuntutan gerakan kemerdekaan untuk menentukan status politik. Manfaat nyata bergantung pada pembentukan lembaga, pelaksanaan perlindungan dan pertanggungjawaban belanja kepada masyarakat. Perselisihan kemudian mengenai konsultasi, revisi serta provinsi baru kembali pada persoalan keterwakilan. Otonomi khusus mengubah perangkat pemerintahan tanpa menyelesaikan tuntutan penentuan nasib sendiri yang membawa warga ke jalan dan kongres. Sumber: UU No. 21 Tahun 2001 — Otonomi Khusus Bagi Provinsi Papua BPK RI — Peraturan https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/44901/uu-no-21-tahun-2001

text.en:
The Merauke Integrated Food and Energy Estate programme, MIFEE, was launched in 2010 to develop food and energy production through plantations and large-scale enterprises. The proposed area included Malind customary lands, with sago forests, hunting grounds and rivers sustaining village life. Company negotiations over land rights brought decisions about food, income and relationships between clans into concession arrangements.

Field research by FPP, Pusaka and Sawit Watch in 2013 collected residents' experiences in Baad, Wayau, Koa and Zanegi. Residents described incomplete information, promises of assistance and employment, imposed compensation terms and unclear agreements. Negotiations through selected leaders also fragmented collective customary decisions. Families depending on the land could bear the consequences without understanding the full terms of an agreement.

In Zanegi, land had been ceded to PT Selaras Inti Semesta, a Medco subsidiary, in 2009, before MIFEE's launch. Residents subsequently reported reduced hunting grounds and fish. Researchers recorded child malnutrition and illness, while paid employment had not replaced food previously obtained from forests and rivers. A doctor reportedly visiting for only one day each month illustrated the limited care available as health needs grew.

Losing forest access changed families' ability to obtain food and sustain life on their land. Promises of development confronted residents' experience of greater dependence on cash income, purchased food and company decisions. These village accounts explain the demands for protection of land rights and community consent in subsequent projects in Merauke. Sources: A sweetness like unto death FPP, Pusaka & Sawit Watch · 2013 https://www.forestpeoples.org/fileadmin/uploads/fpp/migration/publication/2013/10/asweetnessundodeathmifeeindonesiaenglish2.pdf
text.pmy:
Program Merauke Integrated Food and Energy Estate, MIFEE, diluncurkan pada 2010 untuk mengembangkan produksi pangan dan energi melalui perkebunan serta usaha berskala besar. Wilayah yang direncanakan mencakup tanah adat Malind, dengan hutan sagu, tempat berburu dan sungai yang menopang kehidupan kampung. Perundingan perusahaan dengan pemegang hak tanah membawa keputusan mengenai pangan, penghasilan dan hubungan antarmarga ke dalam penguasaan konsesi.

Penelitian lapangan FPP, Pusaka dan Sawit Watch pada 2013 menghimpun pengalaman warga Baad, Wayau, Koa dan Zanegi. Warga menjelaskan informasi yang tidak lengkap, janji bantuan dan pekerjaan, ketentuan ganti rugi yang ditetapkan sepihak, serta kesepakatan yang tidak jelas. Perundingan melalui sebagian pemimpin juga memecah keputusan bersama masyarakat adat. Anggota keluarga yang bergantung pada tanah dapat menanggung akibat keputusan tanpa memahami seluruh isi kesepakatannya.

Di Zanegi, penyerahan tanah kepada PT Selaras Inti Semesta, anak perusahaan Medco, sudah berlangsung pada 2009, sebelum peluncuran MIFEE. Warga kemudian melaporkan berkurangnya tempat berburu dan ikan. Peneliti mencatat kekurangan gizi dan penyakit pada anak, sementara pekerjaan berupah belum menggantikan pangan yang sebelumnya diperoleh dari hutan dan sungai. Kunjungan dokter yang dilaporkan hanya sehari dalam sebulan memperlihatkan terbatasnya layanan ketika kebutuhan kesehatan meningkat.

Kehilangan akses terhadap hutan mengubah kemampuan keluarga memperoleh makanan dan mempertahankan kehidupan di tanahnya. Janji pembangunan dihadapkan pada pengalaman warga yang menjadi lebih bergantung pada penghasilan tunai, makanan yang dibeli dan keputusan perusahaan. Catatan kampung-kampung ini menjelaskan dasar tuntutan perlindungan hak tanah dan persetujuan masyarakat dalam proyek-proyek berikutnya di Merauke. Sumber: A sweetness like unto death FPP, Pusaka & Sawit Watch · 2013 https://www.forestpeoples.org/fileadmin/uploads/fpp/migration/publication/2013/10/asweetnessundodeathmifeeindonesiaenglish2.pdf

title.en: Muyu makers and the noken economy

text.en:
Veronika Triariyani Kanem examines the lives of Muyu women making and distributing string bags, known as men, in Merauke. Recognition of noken by UNESCO in 2012 brought greater visibility and tourism demand. Making bags can generate household income, but increased sales do not automatically ensure that the knowledge passes to a new generation.

The study records older women’s concerns about younger women having limited time or facing structural barriers to learning. Imported mass-produced bags from Java and Makassar also change what young people carry. Women’s accounts connect cultural knowledge to work, access to markets and the practical conditions of everyday life.

For a maker, the market involves finding buyers, obtaining materials and fitting production around other responsibilities. A finished men carries the time and skill invested before it reaches a customer. Kanem’s account shows a tension between greater demand for a recognised cultural product and the uneven conditions for learning to make it. Supporting sales and supporting transmission are related tasks, but neither happens automatically through a heritage label. Sources: Muyu noken (men): Shifting economic opportunities and cultural values Veronika Triariyani Kanem · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch19.pdf
text.pmy:
Veronika Triariyani Kanem meneliti kehidupan perempuan Muyu yang membuat dan mengedarkan tas tali, disebut men, di Merauke. Pengakuan UNESCO atas noken pada 2012 meningkatkan perhatian serta permintaan wisata. Pembuatan tas dapat menghasilkan pendapatan rumah tangga, tetapi bertambahnya penjualan tidak otomatis memastikan pewarisan pengetahuan.

Kajian mencatat kekhawatiran perempuan tua tentang waktu yang terbatas serta hambatan struktural bagi perempuan muda untuk belajar. Tas produksi massal dari Jawa dan Makassar turut mengubah pilihan tas anak muda. Penuturan perempuan menghubungkan pengetahuan budaya dengan pekerjaan, akses pasar, serta keadaan praktis kehidupan sehari-hari.

Bagi pembuat, pasar mencakup mencari pembeli, memperoleh bahan dan mengatur produksi di antara tanggung jawab lain. Men yang selesai membawa waktu serta keterampilan sebelum sampai kepada pelanggan. Catatan Kanem memperlihatkan hubungan antara permintaan yang meningkat dan kondisi belajar yang tidak merata. Mendukung penjualan serta pewarisan saling berkaitan, tetapi keduanya tidak terjadi otomatis karena label warisan budaya. Sumber: Muyu noken (men): Shifting economic opportunities and cultural values Veronika Triariyani Kanem · ANU Press · 2025 https://press-files.anu.edu.au/downloads/press/n13144/pdf/ch19.pdf

text.en:
UNESCO inscribed noken-making on the List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding in 2012. Noken are knotted or woven bags made from local fibres and used to carry food, goods and children. Making them connects plant knowledge, skilled work and everyday exchange.

The inscription identifies threats to transmission and calls for safeguarding the practice. Regional studies also show how makers negotiate changing markets and household needs. Their work continues through identifiable people and communities; contemporary works and maker photographs can be explored in Exhibition.

The urgent-safeguarding category recognises a practice whose continuation requires support, not a finished achievement that can be left to museums. UNESCO identifies declining transmission, changing materials and competition from manufactured bags among the pressures. Responses need to keep experienced makers able to teach and younger people able to learn. The inscription’s value lies in making those needs visible while leaving the practice in the hands of the communities who continue it. Sources: Noken: multifunctional knotted or woven bag, handcraft of the people of Papua UNESCO https://ich.unesco.org/en/USL/noken-multifunctional-knotted-or-woven-bag-handcraft-of-the-people-of-papua-00619
text.pmy:
UNESCO memasukkan pembuatan noken dalam Daftar Warisan Budaya Takbenda yang Memerlukan Pelindungan Mendesak pada 2012. Noken merupakan tas simpul atau anyaman dari serat setempat untuk membawa pangan, barang, dan anak. Pembuatannya menghubungkan pengetahuan tumbuhan, keterampilan kerja, serta pertukaran sehari-hari.

Pengakuan tersebut mencatat ancaman pada pewarisan pengetahuan dan kebutuhan pelindungan praktik. Kajian regional juga memperlihatkan cara pembuat menghadapi perubahan pasar serta kebutuhan rumah tangga. Karya dan foto pembuat masa kini dapat dijelajahi melalui Pameran.

Kategori perlindungan mendesak mengakui praktik yang kelanjutannya memerlukan dukungan, bukan pencapaian selesai untuk diserahkan kepada museum. UNESCO mencatat berkurangnya pewarisan, perubahan bahan serta persaingan tas buatan pabrik sebagai tekanan. Tanggapan perlu memungkinkan pembuat berpengalaman mengajar dan generasi muda belajar. Nilai pengakuan terletak pada perhatian terhadap kebutuhan tersebut sambil menjaga praktik di tangan masyarakat yang meneruskannya. Sumber: Noken: multifunctional knotted or woven bag, handcraft of the people of Papua UNESCO https://ich.unesco.org/en/USL/noken-multifunctional-knotted-or-woven-bag-handcraft-of-the-people-of-papua-00619

text.en:
West Papuan delegates meeting in Vanuatu agreed on the Saralana Declaration in December 2014 and formed the United Liberation Movement for West Papua, ULMWP. Its founding umbrella brought together the National Federal Republic of West Papua, the West Papua National Coalition for Liberation and the National Parliament of West Papua.

The agreement sought a common diplomatic vehicle for movements that had often competed over leadership and representation. IPAC’s 2015 assessment describes the organisational backgrounds and limits of that unity. A shared diplomatic body did not mean that all domestic organisers or armed commanders followed one leadership.

ULMWP’s institutional history later records a provisional government initiative in 2020. That is the movement’s own description of its political project. Its diplomatic activity belongs alongside the histories of OPM and TPNPB commands, KNPB mobilisation and older diaspora associations, rather than replacing them.

The coalition gave its members a way to present a common self-determination demand to Pacific governments and international audiences. It joined organisations with different domestic and diaspora histories around a diplomatic platform. Relations with armed commands remained a separate issue: a statement by an umbrella body did not necessarily determine a local TPNPB operation. Understanding that structure helps identify who issued a proposal, whose support it claimed and which people would need to take part in any political settlement. Sources: About ULMWP United Liberation Movement for West Papua · institutional account https://www.ulmwp.org/ulmwp; The Current Status of the Papuan Pro-Independence Movement IPAC · Report 21 · 24 August 2015 https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/gdc/gdcovop/2017344154/2017344154.pdf
text.pmy:
Delegasi Papua Barat yang bertemu di Vanuatu menyepakati Deklarasi Saralana pada Desember 2014 dan membentuk United Liberation Movement for West Papua, ULMWP. Organisasi payung ini mempertemukan Negara Federal Republik Papua Barat, West Papua National Coalition for Liberation, dan Parlemen Nasional West Papua.

Kesepakatan ini mengupayakan wadah diplomatik bersama bagi gerakan yang kerap bersaing dalam kepemimpinan dan keterwakilan. Penilaian IPAC pada 2015 menguraikan latar organisasi serta batas persatuan tersebut. Badan diplomatik bersama tidak berarti seluruh penggerak di dalam negeri atau komandan bersenjata mengikuti satu kepemimpinan.

Riwayat kelembagaan ULMWP kemudian mencatat prakarsa pemerintahan sementara pada 2020. Ini merupakan uraian gerakan tentang proyek politiknya sendiri. Kegiatan diplomatiknya dibaca bersama riwayat komando OPM dan TPNPB, mobilisasi KNPB, serta perkumpulan diaspora yang lebih lama.

Koalisi memberi anggotanya jalan untuk menyampaikan tuntutan penentuan nasib sendiri bersama kepada pemerintah Pasifik serta masyarakat internasional. Organisasi dengan sejarah domestik dan diaspora berbeda bertemu dalam wadah diplomatik. Hubungan dengan komando bersenjata tetap persoalan tersendiri: pernyataan organisasi payung belum tentu menentukan operasi TPNPB setempat. Memahami susunan ini membantu mengenali pengusul, dukungan yang diklaim serta pihak yang perlu terlibat dalam penyelesaian politik. Sumber: About ULMWP United Liberation Movement for West Papua · institutional account https://www.ulmwp.org/ulmwp; The Current Status of the Papuan Pro-Independence Movement IPAC · Report 21 · 24 August 2015 https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/gdc/gdcovop/2017344154/2017344154.pdf

text.en:
Racist abuse against Papuan students in Surabaya helped trigger protests across Papua in August 2019. Demonstrators connected discrimination with demands over rights and political treatment. Responses included arrests and restrictions on information, while events differed between locations.

Human Rights Watch’s investigation follows those experiences through interviews and case research. It documents discrimination affecting students and other Papuans beyond the demonstrations, placing the protests within a longer pattern of unequal treatment.

The protests made the relationship between everyday racism and political exclusion explicit. Papuans studying or living outside Papua described harassment and suspicion attached to their identity, while demonstrators linked dignity with self-determination. The state’s response included prosecutions of peaceful political expression as well as the information blackout. HRW’s later interviews show that the issue extended into education and ordinary public life. The protests challenged both individual insults and the institutions that allowed unequal treatment to continue. Sources: If It’s Not Racism, What Is It? Human Rights Watch · 2024 https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/09/18/if-its-not-racism-what-is-it/discrimination-and-other-abuses-against-papuans-in
text.pmy:
Penghinaan rasis terhadap mahasiswa Papua di Surabaya turut memicu protes di berbagai wilayah Papua pada Agustus 2019. Demonstran menghubungkan diskriminasi dengan tuntutan hak dan perlakuan politik. Tanggapan mencakup penangkapan serta pembatasan informasi, dengan kejadian yang berbeda di tiap tempat.

Penyelidikan Human Rights Watch menelusuri pengalaman tersebut melalui wawancara dan kajian kasus. Laporan mendokumentasikan diskriminasi yang dialami mahasiswa dan warga Papua di luar demonstrasi, menempatkan protes dalam pola perlakuan tidak setara yang lebih panjang.

Demonstrasi memperjelas hubungan rasisme sehari-hari dengan penyingkiran politik. Orang Papua yang belajar atau tinggal di luar Papua mengalami pelecehan serta kecurigaan karena identitasnya, sedangkan demonstran menghubungkan martabat dengan penentuan nasib sendiri. Tanggapan negara mencakup pemidanaan ekspresi politik damai serta pemutusan informasi. Wawancara HRW menunjukkan bahwa persoalan menjangkau pendidikan dan kehidupan publik biasa. Demonstrasi menantang penghinaan individu sekaligus lembaga yang membiarkan perlakuan tidak setara berlanjut. Sumber: If It’s Not Racism, What Is It? Human Rights Watch · 2024 https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/09/18/if-its-not-racism-what-is-it/discrimination-and-other-abuses-against-papuans-in

text.en:
On 3 June 2020, the Jakarta State Administrative Court ruled that the government’s internet throttling and shutdown in Papua and West Papua during the 2019 protests were unlawful. AJI and SAFEnet brought the case against the communications minister and president.

The interruption had affected journalism, organising and access to information. The ruling established a legal finding about those government actions, giving later debates over internet restrictions a concrete precedent.

The government had justified the restrictions as a response to unrest and the circulation of false information. AJI and SAFEnet challenged the measures because cutting access also prevented residents and journalists from communicating and documenting events. The court’s finding gave that harm a legal consequence: a security justification did not make the actions lawful. The case placed the ability to report from Papua within the struggle over rights, alongside the demonstrations that the blackout had obscured. Sources: Court ruling on internet blackout Amnesty International Indonesia · 2020 https://www.amnesty.id/kabar-terbaru/siaran-pers/court-ruling-on-internet-blackout-is-a-rare-victory-for-freedom-of-expression-in-papua/06/2020/
text.pmy:
Pada 3 Juni 2020, Pengadilan Tata Usaha Negara Jakarta menyatakan pelambatan dan pemutusan internet oleh pemerintah di Papua serta Papua Barat saat protes 2019 melanggar hukum. AJI dan SAFEnet menggugat menteri komunikasi serta presiden.

Gangguan tersebut berdampak pada jurnalisme, pengorganisasian, dan akses informasi. Putusan menetapkan temuan hukum atas tindakan pemerintah itu dan menjadi rujukan nyata bagi perdebatan pembatasan internet berikutnya.

Pemerintah membenarkan pembatasan sebagai tanggapan terhadap kerusuhan dan penyebaran informasi palsu. AJI serta SAFEnet menggugat karena pemutusan juga menghalangi warga dan wartawan berkomunikasi serta mendokumentasikan kejadian. Putusan memberi akibat hukum: alasan keamanan tidak membuat tindakan tersebut sah. Perkara menempatkan kemampuan melaporkan dari Papua dalam perjuangan hak, bersama demonstrasi yang tertutup oleh pemutusan informasi. Sumber: Court ruling on internet blackout Amnesty International Indonesia · 2020 https://www.amnesty.id/kabar-terbaru/siaran-pers/court-ruling-on-internet-blackout-is-a-rare-victory-for-freedom-of-expression-in-papua/06/2020/

text.en:
Law No. 2 of 2021 revised the special-autonomy framework established in 2001. Its changes concerned representation, funding, institutional authority and the process for creating provinces. Special autonomy therefore belongs in the history of political institutions and customary rights as well as the history of public spending.

The Majelis Rakyat Papua challenged parts of the framework in Constitutional Court case 47/PUU-XIX/2021. The proceedings preserve arguments about consultation, Papuan aspirations and the authority of representative bodies. The court rejected most of the application and found some claims inadmissible. The legal outcome and the competing accounts of participation are distinct parts of the record.

The MRP’s challenge put Indigenous representation at the centre of the revision dispute. A law concerning Papua’s institutions also determined how much influence those institutions would retain over future territorial changes. The court proceedings record this disagreement within the state’s own legal framework, rather than reducing it to support for or opposition to a funding package. The revised law remained in force, setting the conditions under which the government moved ahead with new provinces in 2022. Sources: Law No. 2 of 2021 JDIH Ministry of Finance https://jdih.kemenkeu.go.id/dok/uu-2-tahun-2021; Decision 47/PUU-XIX/2021 Constitutional Court https://www.mkri.id/public/content/persidangan/putusan/putusan_mkri_8639_1661992995.pdf
text.pmy:
UU Nomor 2 Tahun 2021 mengubah kerangka otonomi khusus yang ditetapkan pada 2001. Perubahannya menyangkut perwakilan, pendanaan, kewenangan lembaga, serta proses pembentukan provinsi. Karena itu, otonomi khusus termasuk sejarah lembaga politik dan hak adat, selain sejarah belanja publik.

Majelis Rakyat Papua menggugat bagian kerangka tersebut dalam perkara Mahkamah Konstitusi 47/PUU-XIX/2021. Persidangan menyimpan argumen tentang konsultasi, aspirasi Papua, serta kewenangan badan perwakilan. Mahkamah menolak sebagian besar permohonan dan menyatakan beberapa tuntutan tidak dapat diterima. Hasil hukum serta perbedaan penuturan tentang partisipasi merupakan bagian catatan yang berbeda.

Gugatan MRP menempatkan keterwakilan orang asli di pusat perselisihan revisi. Undang-undang mengenai lembaga Papua sekaligus menentukan pengaruh lembaga itu atas perubahan wilayah berikutnya. Persidangan merekam perselisihan dalam kerangka hukum negara sendiri, bukan sekadar dukungan atau penolakan terhadap pendanaan. Undang-undang hasil revisi tetap berlaku dan memberi kondisi bagi pemerintah untuk melanjutkan pembentukan provinsi pada 2022. Sumber: Law No. 2 of 2021 JDIH Ministry of Finance https://jdih.kemenkeu.go.id/dok/uu-2-tahun-2021; Decision 47/PUU-XIX/2021 Constitutional Court https://www.mkri.id/public/content/persidangan/putusan/putusan_mkri_8639_1661992995.pdf

text.en:
Laws 14, 15 and 16 of 2022 created Papua Selatan, Papua Tengah and Papua Pegunungan. Law 29 created Papua Barat Daya later that year. The changes brought the number of provinces in western Papua to six. Papua Selatan comprises Merauke, Boven Digoel, Mappi and Asmat, with its capital in Merauke.

The government presented new provinces as a way to bring administration and services closer to residents. Papuan responses differed: some regional actors supported expansion, while MRP and civil-society objections concerned consultation and the political consequences. New boundaries changed representative institutions, budgets and administrative centres; whether they improved services requires evidence beyond the legislation itself.

The new units divided the former provincial public sphere into additional governments, legislatures and representative bodies. For residents, a new capital promised closer administration but also introduced new institutions through which land and service decisions would be made. Objections over consent concerned who had authorised the change, not only the location of an office. Territorial reorganisation therefore became another chapter in the unresolved relationship between Indigenous representation and decisions made by the central government. Sources: Law No. 14 of 2022: Papua Selatan BPK legal database https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/217796/uu-no-14-tahun-2022; Law No. 29 of 2022: Papua Barat Daya BPK legal database https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/232726/uu-no-29-tahun-2022; Decision 47/PUU-XIX/2021 Constitutional Court https://www.mkri.id/public/content/persidangan/putusan/putusan_mkri_8639_1661992995.pdf
text.pmy:
UU 14, 15, dan 16 Tahun 2022 membentuk Papua Selatan, Papua Tengah, serta Papua Pegunungan. UU 29 membentuk Papua Barat Daya pada tahun yang sama. Perubahan tersebut menjadikan jumlah provinsi di Papua bagian barat enam. Papua Selatan mencakup Merauke, Boven Digoel, Mappi, serta Asmat, dengan ibu kota di Merauke.

Pemerintah menyatakan provinsi baru akan mendekatkan administrasi dan layanan kepada penduduk. Tanggapan orang Papua berbeda: sejumlah pelaku regional mendukung pemekaran, sedangkan keberatan MRP serta masyarakat sipil menyangkut konsultasi dan akibat politik. Batas baru mengubah lembaga perwakilan, anggaran, serta pusat administrasi. Perbaikan layanan memerlukan bukti di luar undang-undang pembentukannya.

Wilayah baru membagi ruang publik provinsi lama menjadi lebih banyak pemerintahan, legislatif dan lembaga perwakilan. Bagi warga, ibu kota baru menjanjikan pemerintahan lebih dekat sekaligus menghadirkan lembaga baru yang menentukan tanah serta layanan. Keberatan mengenai persetujuan menyangkut siapa yang mengesahkan perubahan, bukan lokasi kantor saja. Penataan wilayah menjadi bab lain dalam hubungan yang belum selesai antara keterwakilan orang asli dan keputusan pemerintah pusat. Sumber: Law No. 14 of 2022: Papua Selatan BPK legal database https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/217796/uu-no-14-tahun-2022; Law No. 29 of 2022: Papua Barat Daya BPK legal database https://peraturan.bpk.go.id/Details/232726/uu-no-29-tahun-2022; Decision 47/PUU-XIX/2021 Constitutional Court https://www.mkri.id/public/content/persidangan/putusan/putusan_mkri_8639_1661992995.pdf

text.en:
Humanitarian access remains a central issue in the recent record. UN experts called for urgent access in 2022, while the Human Rights Committee’s 2024 dialogue put questions about Papua to the Indonesian government. Human Rights Watch’s May 2025 investigation describes renewed fighting and displacement in several highland regencies.

Churches serve as places of refuge, and pastors, health workers and local journalists help document what happens in areas difficult to reach. Their accounts connect security operations with the practical conditions of food, shelter and care. Claims about the number of displaced people need to be read with the reporting date, area covered and access available to the investigator.

The release of New Zealand pilot Phillip Mehrtens in September 2024, after captivity beginning in February 2023, also illustrates the role of particular armed commanders and negotiations. The hostage-taking and its resolution are not interchangeable with the wider history of civilian displacement, but both affect movement and access to services in conflict areas.

The recent record brings political status, civilian protection and public services back into the same field. A school cannot function normally when its community is displaced; health care depends on staff and patients being able to travel safely. Independent access is also necessary for establishing deaths, damage and responsibility. Papuan community organisations, churches and journalists continue to press for that access and for a political process capable of addressing the causes of conflict, rather than treating each new emergency as an isolated event. Sources: UN experts call for urgent humanitarian access in Papua UN Human Rights Special Procedures https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2022/03/indonesia-un-experts-sound-alarm-serious-papua-abuses-call-urgent-aid; Human Rights Committee dialogue with Indonesia United Nations Human Rights https://www.ohchr.org/en/meeting-summaries/2024/03/dialogue-indonesia-experts-human-rights-committee-commend-measures; Renewed Fighting Threatens West Papua Civilians Human Rights Watch · 29 May 2025 https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/05/29/indonesia-renewed-fighting-threatens-west-papua-civilians; New Zealand pilot freed from captivity in Papua Bill Birtles · ABC News · 21 September 2024 https://www.abc.net.au/news/2024-09-21/new-zealand-pilot-phillip-mehrtens-freed-from-captivity-in-papua/104380250
text.pmy:
Akses kemanusiaan tetap menjadi persoalan utama dalam catatan terkini. Pakar PBB meminta akses mendesak pada 2022, sementara dialog Komite HAM pada 2024 mengajukan pertanyaan tentang Papua kepada pemerintah Indonesia. Penyelidikan Human Rights Watch pada Mei 2025 membahas pertempuran serta pengungsian di sejumlah kabupaten pegunungan.

Gereja menjadi tempat perlindungan, sementara pendeta, tenaga kesehatan, dan jurnalis setempat membantu mendokumentasikan kejadian di wilayah yang sulit dijangkau. Catatan mereka menghubungkan operasi keamanan dengan keadaan pangan, tempat tinggal, dan perawatan. Angka pengungsi perlu dibaca bersama tanggal pelaporan, wilayah yang dicakup, serta akses yang dimiliki peneliti.

Pembebasan pilot Selandia Baru Phillip Mehrtens pada September 2024, setelah disandera sejak Februari 2023, juga memperlihatkan peran komandan bersenjata tertentu serta perundingan. Penyanderaan dan penyelesaiannya berbeda dari sejarah pengungsian warga secara luas, tetapi keduanya memengaruhi pergerakan serta akses layanan di wilayah konflik.

Catatan terbaru mempertemukan kembali status politik, perlindungan sipil serta layanan publik. Sekolah tidak dapat berjalan biasa ketika masyarakatnya mengungsi; perawatan bergantung pada perjalanan aman petugas serta pasien. Akses mandiri juga diperlukan untuk memastikan kematian, kerusakan dan tanggung jawab. Organisasi masyarakat, gereja dan wartawan Papua terus menuntut akses serta proses politik yang menjawab penyebab konflik, bukan memperlakukan setiap keadaan darurat sebagai kejadian terpisah.
