Sumber: UN experts call for urgent humanitarian access in Papua UN Human Rights Special Procedures https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2022/03/indonesia-un-experts-sound-alarm-serious-papua-abuses-call-urgent-aid; Human Rights Committee dialogue with Indonesia United Nations Human Rights https://www.ohchr.org/en/meeting-summaries/2024/03/dialogue-indonesia-experts-human-rights-committee-commend-measures; Renewed Fighting Threatens West Papua Civilians Human Rights Watch · 29 May 2025 https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/05/29/indonesia-renewed-fighting-threatens-west-papua-civilians; New Zealand pilot freed from captivity in Papua Bill Birtles · ABC News · 21 September 2024 https://www.abc.net.au/news/2024-09-21/new-zealand-pilot-phillip-mehrtens-freed-from-captivity-in-papua/104380250

text.en:
Merauke’s later food and energy expansion includes sugar and bioethanol development alongside a separate rice programme. Pusaka’s timeline traces the 2023 strategic-project designation and the April 2024 presidential decision establishing a sugar and bioethanol task force. Subsequent land and environmental approvals have their own dates and boundaries.

Government targets describe planned development. Community and environmental records are needed to establish actual clearance, consent and effects on livelihoods. Keeping the branches separate makes it possible to follow which project, company and customary territory a new report concerns.

Pusaka connects these decisions with permits, company involvement, public objections and the experiences of customary landholders. The timeline makes the sequence visible: designation and task-force decisions create a policy framework, while land access and clearance occur through subsequent actions in particular territories. For communities, consent concerns those practical changes—who enters, what is cleared and whether families retain access to their food sources. The earlier MIFEE experience makes those questions concrete before the new targets are achieved. Sources: Merauke National Strategic Project timeline Yayasan Pusaka Bentala Rakyat https://pusaka.or.id/en/lini-masa/merauke-national-strategic-project-timeline/
text.pmy:
Perluasan pangan dan energi Merauke mencakup pengembangan gula serta bioetanol bersama program padi yang terpisah. Linimasa Pusaka menelusuri penetapan proyek strategis pada 2023 dan keputusan presiden April 2024 yang membentuk satgas gula serta bioetanol. Persetujuan tanah dan lingkungan berikutnya memiliki tanggal serta batas tersendiri.

Target pemerintah menjelaskan pembangunan yang direncanakan. Catatan masyarakat dan lingkungan diperlukan untuk memastikan pembukaan nyata, persetujuan, serta dampaknya terhadap penghidupan. Pemisahan cabang program memungkinkan pemantauan proyek, perusahaan, dan wilayah adat yang dibahas setiap laporan baru.

Pusaka menghubungkan keputusan tersebut dengan perizinan, perusahaan, penolakan publik serta pengalaman pemegang hak adat. Linimasa memperlihatkan urutannya: penetapan dan pembentukan satuan tugas memberi kerangka kebijakan, sedangkan akses tanah serta pembukaan berlangsung melalui tindakan berikutnya di wilayah tertentu. Bagi masyarakat, persetujuan menyangkut perubahan nyata—siapa yang masuk, apa yang dibuka dan apakah keluarga masih mengakses sumber pangan. Pengalaman MIFEE membuat pertanyaan ini nyata sebelum target baru tercapai. Sumber: Merauke National Strategic Project timeline Yayasan Pusaka Bentala Rakyat https://pusaka.or.id/en/lini-masa/merauke-national-strategic-project-timeline/

text.en:
On 10 June 2025, the government announced the revocation of mining permits for Anugerah Surya Pratama, Mulia Raymond Perkasa, Kawei Sejahtera Mining and Nurham in Raja Ampat. PT Gag Nikel’s permit remained in force.

The distinction matters for understanding what changed: the decision concerned four companies, while other mining activity and the condition of affected islands required continued monitoring. The followed story tracks subsequent operations and access to the revocation records.

The government described the decision as following an evaluation of environmental and licensing compliance. Naming each company allows communities and observers to distinguish an announced revocation from the continuing operation on Gag. A permit decision also does not restore a cleared site by itself. The next responsibilities concern enforcement, rehabilitation and the condition of affected land and waters. The episode shows how public scrutiny can change licensing while leaving work to establish what happens on the ground. Sources: Four mining permits revoked in Raja Ampat Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources · 2025 https://www.esdm.go.id/en/media-center/news-archives/pemerintah-cabut-empat-izin-perusahaan-tambang-di-raja-ampat
text.pmy:
Pada 10 Juni 2025, pemerintah mengumumkan pencabutan izin tambang Anugerah Surya Pratama, Mulia Raymond Perkasa, Kawei Sejahtera Mining, dan Nurham di Raja Ampat. Izin PT Gag Nikel tetap berlaku.

Perbedaan ini penting untuk memahami perubahan: keputusan menyangkut empat perusahaan, sementara kegiatan tambang lain dan kondisi pulau terdampak memerlukan pemantauan lanjutan. Kisah dalam pantauan menelusuri operasi berikutnya serta akses atas catatan pencabutan.

Pemerintah menjelaskan keputusan sebagai hasil evaluasi lingkungan dan kepatuhan perizinan. Nama setiap perusahaan memungkinkan masyarakat membedakan pencabutan yang diumumkan dari operasi yang tetap berjalan di Gag. Keputusan izin juga tidak memulihkan lokasi yang sudah dibuka dengan sendirinya. Tanggung jawab berikutnya menyangkut pelaksanaan, pemulihan serta keadaan tanah dan perairan terdampak. Peristiwa ini menunjukkan bagaimana perhatian publik dapat mengubah perizinan sambil menyisakan pekerjaan untuk memastikan keadaan di lapangan. Sumber: Four mining permits revoked in Raja Ampat Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources · 2025 https://www.esdm.go.id/en/media-center/news-archives/pemerintah-cabut-empat-izin-perusahaan-tambang-di-raja-ampat

text.en:
Carl Wilhelm Ottow and Johann Gottlob Geissler arrived at Mansinam near Manokwari in 1855. Their journey through the eastern Indonesian maritime network included support from the Sultan of Tidore. The mission became an important reference point in the history of Christianity in Papua.

Church accounts preserve the arrival as a founding event. Later schools and teachers connected religious work with changes in education and public life. The southern mission-school record, beginning in the early twentieth century, shows how Indigenous and other non-European teachers helped shape schooling rather than acting only as recipients of European instruction.

Conversion and teaching developed through relationships with Papuan communities, not simply through the arrival of two Europeans. The mission’s later importance lay in congregations, literacy and networks of teachers whose work extended beyond the island. The commemoration of Mansinam became part of a Christian public history shared across places with different church traditions. That institutional reach would later give Papuan churches a role in education, community organising and the protection of people facing violence. Sources: They brought us the light United Evangelical Mission · Martina Pauly https://www.vemission.org/en/details/they-brought-us-the-light; Educating Children, Civilizing Society Maaike Derksen · International Review of Social History https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/international-review-of-social-history/article/educating-children-civilizing-society-missionary-schools-and-noneuropean-teachers-in-south-dutch-new-guinea-19021942/2991790133D3B7E11667F9C5AFE1B065
text.pmy:
Carl Wilhelm Ottow dan Johann Gottlob Geissler tiba di Mansinam dekat Manokwari pada 1855. Perjalanan melalui jaringan maritim Indonesia timur mencakup bantuan Sultan Tidore. Misi tersebut menjadi salah satu titik penting dalam sejarah kekristenan di Papua.

Catatan gereja mempertahankan kedatangan ini sebagai peristiwa awal. Sekolah serta guru kemudian menghubungkan kerja keagamaan dengan perubahan pendidikan dan kehidupan publik. Catatan sekolah misi di selatan sejak awal abad ke-20 memperlihatkan bagaimana guru setempat dan guru non-Eropa lainnya ikut membentuk pendidikan.

Pertobatan dan pengajaran berkembang melalui hubungan dengan masyarakat Papua, bukan hanya kedatangan dua orang Eropa. Arti penting misi pada masa berikutnya terletak pada jemaat, kemampuan baca-tulis dan jaringan guru yang bekerja jauh di luar pulau. Peringatan Mansinam menjadi bagian sejarah publik Kristen yang dikenal di berbagai wilayah dengan tradisi gereja berbeda. Jangkauan lembaga ini kemudian memberi gereja Papua peran dalam pendidikan, pengorganisasian masyarakat dan perlindungan warga yang menghadapi kekerasan. Sumber: They brought us the light United Evangelical Mission · Martina Pauly https://www.vemission.org/en/details/they-brought-us-the-light; Educating Children, Civilizing Society Maaike Derksen · International Review of Social History https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/international-review-of-social-history/article/educating-children-civilizing-society-missionary-schools-and-noneuropean-teachers-in-south-dutch-new-guinea-19021942/2991790133D3B7E11667F9C5AFE1B065

text.en:
The Papuan independence struggle developed after the administrative transfer of 1963. Resistance in Manokwari in 1965 became an important point in the emergence of Organisasi Papua Merdeka, OPM. The name came to cover local armed commands, political organisers and supporters united by an independence demand but with different histories and strategies. Repression of political activity and the refusal of a genuine choice over the territory’s future shaped the movement’s growth.

In 1971, Seth Rumkorem and Jacob Prai proclaimed a Republic of West Papua. Subsequent disputes produced competing command networks, including the MARVIC and Pemka groupings. These divisions shaped the relationship between coastal leaders, highland commands and representatives abroad; they did not produce one continuously unified chain of command.

TPNPB, the West Papua National Liberation Army, fights for an independent West Papua through local armed commands. Civilian organisations pursue independence through mobilisation, petitions and diplomacy. The movement therefore includes different forms of struggle and leadership: an umbrella organisation’s statement does not necessarily direct a local military operation. These relationships have changed through alliances and disputes, while the unresolved demand for self-determination remains a common political foundation.

The attack on the Arfai military post on 28 July 1965 was followed by Operation Sadar and repression in areas around Manokwari. ICTJ and ELSHAM document burned villages, arrests, torture and restrictions on movement through survivor accounts. Teachers and former Council members also faced detention; Baldus Mofu described repeated imprisonment and torture. Military retaliation reached people beyond those who had taken up arms, making civilian safety and political freedom inseparable from the developing independence struggle. Sources: The Current Status of the Papuan Pro-Independence Movement IPAC · Report 21 · 24 August 2015 https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/gdc/gdcovop/2017344154/2017344154.pdf; Anatomy of an Occupation: The Indonesian Military in West Papua Jim Elmslie, Camellia Webb-Gannon & Peter King · 2011 https://documents.uow.edu.au/content/groups/public/@web/@socs/@has/documents/doc/uow270886.pdf; The Past That Has Not Passed ICTJ & ELSHAM · 2012 https://www.ictj.org/sites/default/files/ICTJ-ELSHAM-Indonesia-Papua-2012-English.pdf; Renewed Fighting Threatens West Papua Civilians Human Rights Watch · 29 May 2025 https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/05/29/indonesia-renewed-fighting-threatens-west-papua-civilians
text.pmy:
Perjuangan kemerdekaan Papua berkembang setelah penyerahan administrasi pada 1963. Perlawanan di Manokwari pada 1965 menjadi salah satu titik penting kemunculan Organisasi Papua Merdeka, OPM. Nama ini kemudian mencakup komando bersenjata setempat, penggerak politik dan pendukung yang bertemu dalam tuntutan kemerdekaan dengan riwayat serta strategi berbeda. Penindasan kegiatan politik dan penolakan pilihan nyata atas masa depan wilayah membentuk perkembangan gerakan.

Pada 1971, Seth Rumkorem dan Jacob Prai memproklamasikan Republik Papua Barat. Perselisihan berikutnya menghasilkan jaringan komando yang bersaing, termasuk kelompok MARVIC dan Pemka. Perpecahan ini memengaruhi hubungan antara pemimpin pesisir, komando pegunungan, dan wakil di luar negeri; struktur komandonya tidak selalu menyatu.

TPNPB, Tentara Pembebasan Nasional Papua Barat, memperjuangkan kemerdekaan Papua Barat melalui komando bersenjata setempat. Organisasi sipil mengusahakan kemerdekaan melalui pengorganisasian, petisi serta diplomasi. Gerakan mencakup cara perjuangan dan kepemimpinan berbeda: pernyataan organisasi payung belum tentu menentukan operasi militer setempat. Hubungan berubah melalui persekutuan serta perselisihan, sementara tuntutan penentuan nasib sendiri tetap menjadi dasar politik bersama.

Serangan terhadap pos militer Arfai pada 28 Juli 1965 diikuti Operasi Sadar serta penindasan di sekitar Manokwari. ICTJ dan ELSHAM mendokumentasikan kampung dibakar, penangkapan, penyiksaan dan pembatasan perjalanan melalui kesaksian penyintas. Guru serta mantan anggota dewan juga ditahan; Baldus Mofu menceritakan pemenjaraan dan penyiksaan berulang. Pembalasan militer menjangkau warga di luar pelaku serangan, sehingga keselamatan sipil dan kebebasan politik tidak terpisah dari perjuangan kemerdekaan yang berkembang. Sumber: The Current Status of the Papuan Pro-Independence Movement IPAC · Report 21 · 24 August 2015 https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/gdc/gdcovop/2017344154/2017344154.pdf; Anatomy of an Occupation: The Indonesian Military in West Papua Jim Elmslie, Camellia Webb-Gannon & Peter King · 2011 https://documents.uow.edu.au/content/groups/public/@web/@socs/@has/documents/doc/uow270886.pdf; The Past That Has Not Passed ICTJ & ELSHAM · 2012 https://www.ictj.org/sites/default/files/ICTJ-ELSHAM-Indonesia-Papua-2012-English.pdf; Renewed Fighting Threatens West Papua Civilians Human Rights Watch · 29 May 2025 https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/05/29/indonesia-renewed-fighting-threatens-west-papua-civilians

text.en:
In 1984, unrest and military operations were followed by a large movement of Papuans into Papua New Guinea. Rosemary Preston’s study examines refugees’ experience from 1984 to 1986, including the difficult relationship between humanitarian assistance, border policy and political aspirations.

People who crossed included families, political activists and people from communities with kinship ties across the border. Camps and settlements became sites of both everyday survival and organising. Later ethnographic work by Diana Glazebrook follows how refugees negotiated exile, education, subsistence and movement between settlement and border communities.

Another political initiative emerged in Jayapura in December 1988, when Thomas Wanggai proclaimed West Melanesia. Chauvel describes this initiative within the wider development of Papuan nationalism. Its symbols and organisational lineage differed from those of the Morning Star movement, adding to the political currents later brought into umbrella organisations.

Crossing the border could provide escape from military operations while creating new restrictions on residence and movement. Refugees had to secure food and schooling within policies that did not necessarily recognise their political aims. Kinship across the boundary offered relationships distinct from formal camp administration. Exile became both a prolonged condition of family life and a base for advocacy. Its history connects the independence struggle inside Papua with organising across the Pacific and abroad. Sources: The Integration of Refugees into a Host Country Rosemary Preston · International Migration Review · 1992 https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/019791839202600305; Dwelling in Exile Diana Glazebrook · 2001 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2007-12/glazebrook_2001_exile.pdf; Constructing Papuan Nationalism: History, Ethnicity, and Adaptation Richard Chauvel · 2005 · p. 18 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf
text.pmy:
Pada 1984, pergolakan dan operasi militer diikuti perpindahan besar orang Papua ke Papua Nugini. Kajian Rosemary Preston membahas pengalaman pengungsi pada 1984–1986, termasuk hubungan yang sulit antara bantuan kemanusiaan, kebijakan perbatasan, dan aspirasi politik.

Mereka yang menyeberang mencakup keluarga, aktivis politik, dan warga dari masyarakat yang memiliki hubungan kerabat lintas batas. Kamp dan permukiman menjadi tempat menjalani kehidupan sehari-hari sekaligus berorganisasi. Penelitian etnografi Diana Glazebrook kemudian mengikuti cara pengungsi menjalani pengasingan, pendidikan, penghidupan, dan perpindahan antara permukiman serta masyarakat perbatasan.

Prakarsa politik lain muncul di Jayapura pada Desember 1988, ketika Thomas Wanggai memproklamasikan Melanesia Barat. Chauvel membahas prakarsa ini dalam perkembangan nasionalisme Papua. Simbol dan garis organisasinya berbeda dari gerakan Bintang Kejora, menambah arus politik yang kemudian berhubungan dengan berbagai organisasi payung.

Menyeberangi perbatasan dapat memberi jalan keluar dari operasi militer sekaligus membawa pembatasan baru atas tempat tinggal dan perjalanan. Pengungsi harus memperoleh pangan serta pendidikan dalam kebijakan yang belum tentu mengakui tujuan politik mereka. Kekerabatan lintas batas menyediakan hubungan berbeda dari administrasi kamp. Pengasingan menjadi kondisi kehidupan keluarga yang panjang sekaligus tempat advokasi. Sejarahnya menghubungkan perjuangan di Papua dengan pengorganisasian melalui Pasifik dan luar negeri. Sumber: The Integration of Refugees into a Host Country Rosemary Preston · International Migration Review · 1992 https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/019791839202600305; Dwelling in Exile Diana Glazebrook · 2001 https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/sites/default/files/collectie/files/2007-12/glazebrook_2001_exile.pdf; Constructing Papuan Nationalism: History, Ethnicity, and Adaptation Richard Chauvel · 2005 · p. 18 https://www.files.ethz.ch/isn/26108/PS014.pdf

text.en:
Mama Yosepha Alomang organised Amungme resistance to the environmental and social effects of Freeport’s mining operations. Her work joined land claims with women’s livelihoods, collective action and the treatment of Indigenous people around the mine. The Goldman Environmental Prize recognised her work in 2001.

The prize’s account documents her detention and torture in 1994 after she was accused of assisting rebels. It also describes practical organising: demanding that the company purchase local produce, creating a cooperative, and supporting traditional culture. These activities made questions of livelihood and safety part of the struggle over land.

Abigail Abrash’s research describes Amungme and Kamoro concerns about land, environmental change, security and the terms of company engagement. The two communities have different territories and relationships with the operation. Their organising provides a local history of mining that is more detailed than the contract dates or production figures alone.

Alomang’s organising also challenged who was allowed to negotiate the consequences of mining. Women supplying food and sustaining households had a direct stake in land decisions and company practices. A cooperative and demands for local purchasing turned that stake into collective economic action. Recognition in 2001 made her work internationally visible, but its foundation lay in continuing community relationships. Her history joins resistance to violence with practical efforts to retain a livelihood and a voice on Amungme land. Sources: Yosepha Alomang Goldman Environmental Prize · 2001 recipient https://www.goldmanprize.org/recipient/yosepha-alomang/; The Amungme, Kamoro & Freeport: How Indigenous Papuans Have Resisted Abigail Abrash · Cultural Survival https://www.culturalsurvival.org/publications/cultural-survival-quarterly/amungme-kamoro-freeport-how-indigenous-papuans-have
text.pmy:
Mama Yosepha Alomang mengorganisasi perlawanan Amungme terhadap dampak lingkungan dan sosial operasi pertambangan Freeport. Kegiatannya menghubungkan tuntutan atas tanah dengan penghidupan perempuan, tindakan bersama, dan perlakuan terhadap masyarakat adat di sekitar tambang. Goldman Environmental Prize memberikan penghargaan atas pekerjaannya pada 2001.

Catatan penghargaan mendokumentasikan penahanan dan penyiksaannya pada 1994 setelah ia dituduh membantu pemberontak. Catatan itu juga menguraikan kegiatan nyata: menuntut perusahaan membeli hasil kebun setempat, membentuk koperasi, dan mendukung kebudayaan. Kegiatan ini menempatkan penghidupan serta keselamatan sebagai bagian perjuangan atas tanah.

Penelitian Abigail Abrash menguraikan persoalan Amungme dan Kamoro mengenai tanah, perubahan lingkungan, keamanan, serta syarat hubungan dengan perusahaan. Kedua masyarakat memiliki wilayah dan hubungan yang berbeda dengan operasi tambang. Pengorganisasian mereka memberikan sejarah pertambangan setempat yang melampaui tanggal kontrak atau angka produksi.

Pengorganisasian Alomang juga menantang siapa yang boleh merundingkan akibat tambang. Perempuan yang menyediakan pangan dan menjaga rumah tangga berkepentingan langsung terhadap keputusan tanah serta praktik perusahaan. Koperasi dan tuntutan pembelian hasil setempat mengubah kepentingan itu menjadi tindakan ekonomi bersama. Penghargaan 2001 memperkenalkan karyanya secara internasional, tetapi dasarnya adalah hubungan masyarakat yang terus dijaga. Sejarahnya menghubungkan penolakan kekerasan dengan usaha mempertahankan penghidupan serta suara di tanah Amungme. Sumber: Yosepha Alomang Goldman Environmental Prize · 2001 recipient https://www.goldmanprize.org/recipient/yosepha-alomang/; The Amungme, Kamoro & Freeport: How Indigenous Papuans Have Resisted Abigail Abrash · Cultural Survival https://www.culturalsurvival.org/publications/cultural-survival-quarterly/amungme-kamoro-freeport-how-indigenous-papuans-have

text.en:
The West Papua National Committee, KNPB, emerged in 2008 as a domestic mobilising organisation advocating a referendum. IPAC’s later account follows its relationship with the National Parliament of West Papua, PNWP, and distinguishes these political networks from armed commands and representatives based abroad.

At the same time, Neles Tebay and Muridan Widjojo worked through the Papua Peace Network to prepare dialogue between Jakarta and Papua. In a 2010 interview, Tebay described nine local consultations and the need to involve communities, different organisations and the diaspora. Representation, mistrust and an agreed agenda were practical obstacles, rather than matters resolved by announcing dialogue.

The 2011 report Anatomy of an Occupation analysed leaked Indonesian military documents mapping armed groups, political organisers and civilian networks. Its authors argue that this surveillance treated a broad range of Papuan civic activity as a security concern. The report is evidence about military classification and monitoring; its lists do not establish that every named civilian belonged to an armed organisation.

KNPB’s referendum demand placed the right to choose political status at the centre of civilian mobilisation. The Papua Peace Network pursued a negotiated process with an agreed agenda and credible participation. These were distinct approaches, both emerging from distrust created by violence and unfulfilled promises. Church and civil-society organisers sought conditions in which Papuan demands could be heard without criminalising public participation. Announcing a dialogue did not by itself remove the security practices that made participation dangerous. Sources: The Current Status of the Papuan Pro-Independence Movement IPAC · Report 21 · 24 August 2015 https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/gdc/gdcovop/2017344154/2017344154.pdf; Talks between Jakarta and Papua: An Interview with Neles Tebay Peace Brigades International · 7 July 2010 https://peacebrigades.org/en/news/talks-between-jakarta-and-papua-interview-neles-tebay; Anatomy of an Occupation: The Indonesian Military in West Papua Jim Elmslie, Camellia Webb-Gannon & Peter King · 2011 https://documents.uow.edu.au/content/groups/public/@web/@socs/@has/documents/doc/uow270886.pdf
text.pmy:
Komite Nasional Papua Barat, KNPB, muncul pada 2008 sebagai organisasi mobilisasi di dalam negeri yang memperjuangkan referendum. Kajian IPAC kemudian mengikuti hubungannya dengan Parlemen Nasional West Papua, PNWP, serta membedakan jaringan politik ini dari komando bersenjata dan wakil yang berbasis di luar negeri.

Pada waktu yang sama, Neles Tebay dan Muridan Widjojo bekerja melalui Jaringan Damai Papua untuk menyiapkan dialog Jakarta–Papua. Dalam wawancara 2010, Tebay menjelaskan sembilan konsultasi setempat dan kebutuhan melibatkan masyarakat, berbagai organisasi, serta diaspora. Keterwakilan, ketidakpercayaan, dan agenda yang disepakati menjadi hambatan nyata yang perlu dikerjakan.

Laporan Anatomy of an Occupation pada 2011 menganalisis dokumen militer Indonesia yang bocor, berisi pemetaan kelompok bersenjata, penggerak politik, dan jaringan sipil. Penulisnya menilai pengawasan ini memperlakukan beragam kegiatan masyarakat Papua sebagai persoalan keamanan. Laporan tersebut menjadi sumber tentang klasifikasi dan pemantauan militer; daftarnya tidak membuktikan bahwa setiap warga yang disebut merupakan anggota organisasi bersenjata.

Tuntutan referendum KNPB menempatkan hak memilih status politik di pusat pengorganisasian sipil. Jaringan Damai Papua mengusahakan perundingan dengan agenda bersama serta keikutsertaan yang dipercaya. Pendekatannya berbeda, tetapi sama-sama tumbuh dari ketidakpercayaan akibat kekerasan dan janji yang tidak dipenuhi. Penggerak gereja serta masyarakat sipil mencari kondisi untuk menyampaikan tuntutan Papua tanpa mempidanakan keikutsertaan publik. Pengumuman dialog belum menghapus praktik keamanan yang membuat keikutsertaan berbahaya. Sumber: The Current Status of the Papuan Pro-Independence Movement IPAC · Report 21 · 24 August 2015 https://tile.loc.gov/storage-services/service/gdc/gdcovop/2017344154/2017344154.pdf; Talks between Jakarta and Papua: An Interview with Neles Tebay Peace Brigades International · 7 July 2010 https://peacebrigades.org/en/news/talks-between-jakarta-and-papua-interview-neles-tebay; Anatomy of an Occupation: The Indonesian Military in West Papua Jim Elmslie, Camellia Webb-Gannon & Peter King · 2011 https://documents.uow.edu.au/content/groups/public/@web/@socs/@has/documents/doc/uow270886.pdf

text.en:
Amungme plaintiffs brought claims against Freeport in Jakarta in 2009 and again in March 2010. Contemporaneous reporting describes demands for compensation over customary land and the impacts of mining. The reported figures were amounts sought by plaintiffs, not damages awarded by a court.

BBC’s report of 9 March 2010 identifies lawyer Johnson Panjaitan and a filing at the South Jakarta District Court the previous day. It also reports Freeport’s written response that earlier cases had been dismissed. The filings document the use of legal proceedings alongside community organising, without establishing a successful remedy for the plaintiffs.

The claims linked a history of mining to continuing customary rights. In the March 2010 filing, lawyers sought compensation for material and non-material losses, using the courts to press demands that community action had not resolved. Freeport disputed liability and referred to earlier dismissals. The proceedings show the obstacles between submitting a land claim and obtaining a remedy: a large sum in a lawsuit is evidence of the demand, while the outcome depends on what a court actually orders. Sources: Amungme tuntut Freeport lagi Rohmatin Bonasir · BBC Indonesia · 9 March 2010 https://www.bbc.com/indonesia/berita_indonesia/2010/03/100308_freeportamungme; Papuan Tribesmen Sue Freeport for Rights Violations Jakarta Globe · 17 July 2009 · ETAN archive https://www.etan.org/et2009/07july/19/17papuan.htm
text.pmy:
Penggugat Amungme mengajukan tuntutan terhadap Freeport di Jakarta pada 2009 dan kembali pada Maret 2010. Pelaporan saat itu membahas permintaan ganti rugi atas tanah adat serta dampak pertambangan. Angka yang diberitakan merupakan tuntutan penggugat, bukan ganti rugi yang telah diputuskan pengadilan.

Laporan BBC pada 9 Maret 2010 menyebut pengacara Johnson Panjaitan dan pendaftaran gugatan di Pengadilan Negeri Jakarta Selatan sehari sebelumnya. Laporan itu juga memuat tanggapan tertulis Freeport bahwa perkara sebelumnya telah ditolak. Pengajuan ini mencatat penggunaan proses hukum bersama pengorganisasian masyarakat, tanpa membuktikan adanya pemulihan yang berhasil bagi penggugat.

Gugatan menghubungkan sejarah penambangan dengan hak adat yang tetap dituntut. Pada pengajuan Maret 2010, pengacara meminta ganti rugi atas kerugian materiil dan nonmateriil, menggunakan pengadilan untuk mendesak tuntutan yang belum selesai melalui aksi masyarakat. Freeport menolak tanggung jawab serta merujuk penolakan perkara sebelumnya. Proses menunjukkan jarak antara mengajukan hak tanah dan memperoleh pemulihan: nilai besar dalam gugatan mencatat tuntutan, sedangkan hasilnya ditentukan putusan pengadilan. Sumber: Amungme tuntut Freeport lagi Rohmatin Bonasir · BBC Indonesia · 9 March 2010 https://www.bbc.com/indonesia/berita_indonesia/2010/03/100308_freeportamungme; Papuan Tribesmen Sue Freeport for Rights Violations Jakarta Globe · 17 July 2009 · ETAN archive https://www.etan.org/et2009/07july/19/17papuan.htm

text.en:
On 13 September 2021, an attack in Kiwirok destroyed public facilities including the health centre. Jubi linked the alleged attack to TPNPB independence fighters associated with Lamek Taplo and reported nurse Gabriella Meliani’s death. Health workers were evacuated and residents lost local services. TPNPB spokesman Sebby Sambom denied that the group killed the nurse and called for a UN investigation. The competing accounts left the circumstances of her death disputed while the loss of care was immediate.

Human Rights Monitor’s 2023 investigation documents subsequent Indonesian military attacks on villages, using witness interviews and satellite-image analysis. It reports destroyed buildings and displacement into forests. These are the investigation’s findings about operations and civilian harm, separate from its legal assessment of possible crimes against humanity.

Displacement interrupted food production, schooling and medical care. The loss of a health centre, the evacuation of staff and the difficulty of reaching people in shelters show how conflict affects care beyond the immediate attack. UN experts called for urgent humanitarian access in March 2022, including assistance to people displaced by violence.

Human Rights Monitor reported 206 buildings destroyed across eight villages and 2,252 people displaced as of June 2023. Those dated findings describe a community crisis, not only damage to a battlefield. Ngalum families sheltering away from home had to obtain food without their normal gardens and reach care without local services. Their experience makes the protection of civilians and access for relief central to any account of the fighting and its aftermath. Sources: TPNPB allegedly attacks health center in Kiwirok, murders a nurse Jubi / West Papua Daily · 20 September 2021 https://en.jubi.id/tpnpb-allegedly-attacks-health-center-in-kiwirok-murders-nurse/; Destroy them first… discuss human rights later: Kiwirok investigation Human Rights Monitor · August 2023 https://humanrightsmonitor.org/reports/kiwirok-report-2023/; UN experts call for urgent humanitarian access in Papua UN Human Rights Special Procedures https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2022/03/indonesia-un-experts-sound-alarm-serious-papua-abuses-call-urgent-aid; Ketika pejuang kesehatan korban aksi KKB diselamatkan Kompas · 17 September 2021 https://www.kompas.id/artikel/ketika-pejuang-kesehatan-korban-aksi-kkb-di-pegunungan-bintang-diselamatkan
text.pmy:
Pada 13 September 2021, serangan di Kiwirok menghancurkan fasilitas publik termasuk puskesmas. Jubi menghubungkan dugaan serangan dengan pejuang kemerdekaan TPNPB yang terkait Lamek Taplo dan melaporkan kematian perawat Gabriella Meliani. Petugas dievakuasi dan warga kehilangan layanan setempat. Juru bicara TPNPB Sebby Sambom menyangkal pasukannya membunuh perawat serta meminta penyelidikan PBB. Penuturan berbeda menyisakan perselisihan mengenai kematiannya, sedangkan kehilangan perawatan langsung dirasakan warga.

Penyelidikan Human Rights Monitor pada 2023 mendokumentasikan serangan militer Indonesia berikutnya terhadap kampung, melalui wawancara saksi dan analisis citra satelit. Laporan mencatat bangunan yang hancur serta pengungsian ke hutan. Temuan tentang operasi dan dampak pada warga ini dibedakan dari penilaian hukumnya mengenai kemungkinan kejahatan terhadap kemanusiaan.

Pengungsian mengganggu produksi pangan, sekolah, dan perawatan kesehatan. Hilangnya puskesmas, evakuasi petugas, serta sulitnya menjangkau warga di tempat perlindungan memperlihatkan dampak konflik pada layanan di luar serangan langsung. Pakar PBB meminta akses kemanusiaan mendesak pada Maret 2022, termasuk bantuan bagi warga yang mengungsi akibat kekerasan.

Human Rights Monitor melaporkan 206 bangunan hancur di delapan kampung serta 2.252 orang mengungsi hingga Juni 2023. Temuan bertanggal ini menggambarkan krisis masyarakat, bukan kerusakan medan tempur saja. Keluarga Ngalum yang berlindung jauh dari rumah harus memperoleh pangan tanpa kebun biasa dan perawatan tanpa layanan setempat. Pengalaman mereka menempatkan perlindungan sipil serta akses bantuan di pusat sejarah pertempuran dan akibatnya. Sumber: TPNPB allegedly attacks health center in Kiwirok, murders a nurse Jubi / West Papua Daily · 20 September 2021 https://en.jubi.id/tpnpb-allegedly-attacks-health-center-in-kiwirok-murders-nurse/; Destroy them first… discuss human rights later: Kiwirok investigation Human Rights Monitor · August 2023 https://humanrightsmonitor.org/reports/kiwirok-report-2023/; UN experts call for urgent humanitarian access in Papua UN Human Rights Special Procedures https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-releases/2022/03/indonesia-un-experts-sound-alarm-serious-papua-abuses-call-urgent-aid; Ketika pejuang kesehatan korban aksi KKB diselamatkan Kompas · 17 September 2021 https://www.kompas.id/artikel/ketika-pejuang-kesehatan-korban-aksi-kkb-di-pegunungan-bintang-diselamatkan

title.pmy: Serangan udara dan masyarakat yang mengungsi

text.en:
By May 2025, renewed fighting was affecting communities in Intan Jaya, Yahukimo, Nduga and Pegunungan Bintang. Human Rights Watch collected accounts from pastors, church workers and local journalists describing helicopter gunships and drones dropping bombs. Residents fled attacks and insecurity, adding to displacement already prolonged by earlier operations. These accounts locate aerial warfare within inhabited highland territories, where families depend on the gardens and settlements they are forced to leave.

Church contacts and local reporting became essential where independent access was restricted. The investigations Paradise Bombed in 2023 and Frontier War in 2025 brought footage and testimony to wider audiences. Alongside the separate Kiwirok investigation, they challenged accounts that reduced operations to fighting between military units. Civilian buildings, food sources and the ability to remain at home were part of the damage under examination.

Frontier War prompted allegations about white phosphorus and calls for an international inquiry. The Indonesian military had denied earlier allegations concerning Nduga, and a UK parliamentary answer in February 2025 said it had found no compelling evidence of illegal use in those earlier allegations. The identity of particular munitions remains disputed; the documented destruction and displacement still require investigation and protection for affected communities. Sources: Free Fire Zone: West Papua Declassified Australia · 11 September 2023 https://declassifiedaus.org/2023/09/11/free-fire-zone-west-papua/; Destroy them first… discuss human rights later: Kiwirok investigation Human Rights Monitor · August 2023 https://humanrightsmonitor.org/reports/kiwirok-report-2023/; Calls for inquiry into Frontier War claims Asia Pacific Report · 31 January 2025 https://asiapacificreport.nz/2025/01/31/wenda-calls-for-international-inquiry-into-film-claim-that-indonesia-is-using-chemical-weapons-in-west-papua/; Military denies using chemical weapons in West Papua ABC News · 23 December 2018 https://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-12-23/indonesia-military-denies-using-chemical-weapons-in-west-papua/10664402; Papua: Chemical Weapons · written answer HL4760 UK Parliament · 19 February 2025 · reproduced by Parallel Parliament https://www.parallelparliament.co.uk/question/HL4760/papua-chemical-weapons; Renewed Fighting Threatens West Papua Civilians Human Rights Watch · 29 May 2025 https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/05/29/indonesia-renewed-fighting-threatens-west-papua-civilians
text.pmy:
Pada Mei 2025, pertempuran kembali berdampak pada masyarakat di Intan Jaya, Yahukimo, Nduga dan Pegunungan Bintang. Human Rights Watch menghimpun kesaksian pendeta, pekerja gereja serta wartawan setempat tentang helikopter tempur dan drone yang menjatuhkan bom. Warga meninggalkan serangan serta ketidakamanan, menambah pengungsian yang sudah panjang akibat operasi sebelumnya. Kesaksian menempatkan perang udara di wilayah pegunungan berpenghuni, tempat keluarga bergantung pada kebun dan kampung yang terpaksa ditinggalkan.

Hubungan gereja serta laporan setempat menjadi penting ketika akses mandiri dibatasi. Penyelidikan Paradise Bombed pada 2023 dan Frontier War pada 2025 menyampaikan rekaman serta kesaksian kepada publik lebih luas. Bersama penyelidikan Kiwirok yang terpisah, laporan menantang gambaran operasi sebagai pertempuran antarunit militer saja. Bangunan sipil, sumber pangan dan kemampuan menetap di rumah merupakan bagian kerusakan yang diteliti.

Frontier War memunculkan dugaan penggunaan fosfor putih serta tuntutan penyelidikan internasional. Militer Indonesia menyangkal dugaan sebelumnya mengenai Nduga, dan jawaban parlemen Inggris Februari 2025 menyatakan belum menemukan bukti meyakinkan penggunaan ilegal dalam dugaan terdahulu. Identitas amunisi tertentu masih diperselisihkan; kehancuran serta pengungsian yang terdokumentasi tetap memerlukan penyelidikan dan perlindungan masyarakat. Sumber: Free Fire Zone: West Papua Declassified Australia · 11 September 2023 https://declassifiedaus.org/2023/09/11/free-fire-zone-west-papua/; Destroy them first… discuss human rights later: Kiwirok investigation Human Rights Monitor · August 2023 https://humanrightsmonitor.org/reports/kiwirok-report-2023/; Calls for inquiry into Frontier War claims Asia Pacific Report · 31 January 2025 https://asiapacificreport.nz/2025/01/31/wenda-calls-for-international-inquiry-into-film-claim-that-indonesia-is-using-chemical-weapons-in-west-papua/; Military denies using chemical weapons in West Papua ABC News · 23 December 2018 https://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-12-23/indonesia-military-denies-using-chemical-weapons-in-west-papua/10664402; Papua: Chemical Weapons · written answer HL4760 UK Parliament · 19 February 2025 · reproduced by Parallel Parliament https://www.parallelparliament.co.uk/question/HL4760/papua-chemical-weapons; Renewed Fighting Threatens West Papua Civilians Human Rights Watch · 29 May 2025 https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/05/29/indonesia-renewed-fighting-threatens-west-papua-civilians

text.en:
On 7 December 2014, soldiers beat young people in Enarotali after a dispute concerning a vehicle’s lights. Residents gathered at Karel Gobay field the following day to protest the treatment. Security forces opened fire. Four young people were killed and others injured. The demand for an explanation of a beating became a mass shooting, leaving families to seek accountability for both the initial violence and the deaths.

Komnas HAM concluded in 2020 that the events constituted a gross human-rights violation, identifying elements of crimes against humanity. The finding connected the shootings with command responsibility rather than treating them only as the acts of unidentified individuals. Years had passed between the deaths and this formal recognition, while families continued to demand a credible investigation and prosecution.

Prosecutors brought only retired officer Isak Sattu to the Human Rights Court in Makassar. On 8 December 2022, the court acquitted him; two judges dissented over his command role. Victims’ representatives and civil-society organisations criticised a prosecution that had narrowed responsibility to one defendant. The result left the documented deaths without a conviction and renewed demands to investigate the wider chain of responsibility. Sources: Findings on the Paniai gross human-rights violation Komnas HAM · 2020 https://www.komnasham.go.id/files/20200604-surat-keterangan-pers-nomor-023-$4JJ6.pdf; Paniai trial and the acquittal BBC Indonesia · 9 December 2022 https://www.bbc.com/indonesia/articles/cjq7zx022y2o; Civil society response to the Paniai judgment Civil-society coalition · Amnesty Indonesia · 2022 https://www.amnesty.id/kabar-terbaru/siaran-pers/tanggapan-masyarakat-sipil-terhadap-putusan-pengadilan-ham-paniai/12/2022/
text.pmy:
Pada 7 Desember 2014, tentara memukuli pemuda di Enarotali setelah perselisihan mengenai lampu kendaraan. Warga berkumpul di Lapangan Karel Gobay keesokan hari untuk memprotes perlakuan tersebut. Aparat melepaskan tembakan. Empat pemuda tewas dan warga lain terluka. Tuntutan penjelasan atas pemukulan berubah menjadi penembakan massal, meninggalkan keluarga dengan perjuangan atas kekerasan awal sekaligus kematian.

Komnas HAM menyimpulkan pada 2020 bahwa peristiwa merupakan pelanggaran HAM berat dengan unsur kejahatan terhadap kemanusiaan. Temuan menghubungkan penembakan dengan tanggung jawab komando, bukan hanya tindakan individu yang tidak dikenal. Bertahun-tahun berlalu antara kematian dan pengakuan resmi ketika keluarga terus menuntut penyelidikan serta penuntutan yang dipercaya.

Penuntut hanya membawa purnawirawan Isak Sattu ke Pengadilan HAM di Makassar. Pada 8 Desember 2022, pengadilan membebaskannya; dua hakim berbeda pendapat mengenai peran komandonya. Wakil korban serta organisasi masyarakat sipil mengkritik penuntutan yang mempersempit tanggung jawab kepada satu terdakwa. Hasilnya meninggalkan kematian yang terdokumentasi tanpa penghukuman dan memperkuat tuntutan penyelidikan rantai tanggung jawab yang lebih luas. Sumber: Findings on the Paniai gross human-rights violation Komnas HAM · 2020 https://www.komnasham.go.id/files/20200604-surat-keterangan-pers-nomor-023-$4JJ6.pdf; Paniai trial and the acquittal BBC Indonesia · 9 December 2022 https://www.bbc.com/indonesia/articles/cjq7zx022y2o; Civil society response to the Paniai judgment Civil-society coalition · Amnesty Indonesia · 2022 https://www.amnesty.id/kabar-terbaru/siaran-pers/tanggapan-masyarakat-sipil-terhadap-putusan-pengadilan-ham-paniai/12/2022/

text.en:
GKI di Tanah Papua became an independent church in 1956, after the long history of Protestant missions that began at Mansinam. Its synod and congregations developed a Papuan institutional network linking education, pastoral work and public affairs. A historical study published by STFT GKI I.S. Kijne examines its ecumenical work for justice and peace between 1962 and 2020.

In the western highlands, Zakheus Pakage’s community shows another route into Christian life and Indigenous leadership. Benny Giay’s study follows how Mee religious discourse, social resistance and historical change were connected. This history helps explain the later public role of Kingmi leaders without treating Papuan congregations as passive recipients of missionary institutions.

GKI, Kingmi and Catholic institutions have distinct histories and positions. Churches later hosted consultations, provided places of refuge and documented violence, while leaders such as Neles Tebay helped prepare dialogue. Their public role developed through these institutions and local relationships, rather than one uniform political position shared by all churches.

Papuan church workers occupied positions that connected a village congregation with schools, synods and networks outside Papua. Those relationships enabled testimony to travel when official accounts excluded it. Church involvement in the Biak investigation, for example, linked documentation with pastoral contact and concern for missing relatives. The institutions also contained internal differences over dialogue and independence. Their historical significance lies in this capacity to organise and accompany communities, rather than in treating a church as one political party. Sources: Sejarah GKI di Tanah Papua Sinode GKI di Tanah Papua · institutional history https://sinodegkitp.com/bp-sinode-gkitp-2022-2027/; Pergerakan Ekumene GKI di Tanah Papua, 1962–2020 MURAI · STFT GKI I.S. Kijne · 2024 https://ojs.stftkijne.ac.id/index.php/jmp/article/view/146; Zakheus Pakage and His Communities Benny Giay · 1995 https://dacc.net.au/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Giay_1995_Zakheus.pdf; Interview with Neles Tebay Peace Brigades International · July 2010 https://peacebrigades.org/en/news/talks-between-jakarta-and-papua-interview-neles-tebay; Names Without Graves ELSHAM Papua & church investigators · 1999 https://www.biak-tribunal.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/Names-Without-Graves_Elsham-Papua-English.pdf
text.pmy:
GKI di Tanah Papua berdiri sebagai gereja mandiri pada 1956, setelah riwayat panjang misi Protestan yang bermula di Mansinam. Sinode dan jemaatnya membentuk jaringan kelembagaan Papua yang menghubungkan pendidikan, pelayanan, serta kehidupan publik. Kajian sejarah yang diterbitkan STFT GKI I.S. Kijne membahas karya ekumenisnya untuk keadilan dan perdamaian pada 1962–2020.

Di pegunungan barat, komunitas Zakheus Pakage memperlihatkan jalur lain dalam kehidupan Kristen dan kepemimpinan masyarakat adat. Kajian Benny Giay mengikuti hubungan wacana keagamaan Mee, perlawanan sosial, serta perubahan sejarah. Riwayat ini membantu menjelaskan peran publik pemimpin Kingmi berikutnya melalui prakarsa jemaat Papua sendiri.

GKI, Kingmi, dan lembaga Katolik memiliki riwayat serta sikap yang berbeda. Gereja kemudian menjadi tempat konsultasi, menyediakan perlindungan, dan mendokumentasikan kekerasan, sementara tokoh seperti Neles Tebay membantu menyiapkan dialog. Peran publik tersebut berkembang melalui lembaga dan hubungan setempat, dengan sikap politik yang beragam.

Pekerja gereja Papua menghubungkan jemaat kampung dengan sekolah, sinode dan jaringan di luar Papua. Hubungan ini memungkinkan kesaksian tersebar ketika catatan resmi mengabaikannya. Keterlibatan gereja dalam penyelidikan Biak, misalnya, menghubungkan dokumentasi dengan pelayanan serta perhatian kepada keluarga orang hilang. Lembaga gereja juga memiliki perbedaan sikap mengenai dialog dan kemerdekaan. Arti sejarahnya terletak pada kemampuan mengorganisir serta mendampingi masyarakat, bukan menjadikan gereja satu partai politik. Sumber: Sejarah GKI di Tanah Papua Sinode GKI di Tanah Papua · institutional history https://sinodegkitp.com/bp-sinode-gkitp-2022-2027/; Pergerakan Ekumene GKI di Tanah Papua, 1962–2020 MURAI · STFT GKI I.S. Kijne · 2024 https://ojs.stftkijne.ac.id/index.php/jmp/article/view/146; Zakheus Pakage and His Communities Benny Giay · 1995 https://dacc.net.au/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Giay_1995_Zakheus.pdf; Interview with Neles Tebay Peace Brigades International · July 2010 https://peacebrigades.org/en/news/talks-between-jakarta-and-papua-interview-neles-tebay; Names Without Graves ELSHAM Papua & church investigators · 1999 https://www.biak-tribunal.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/Names-Without-Graves_Elsham-Papua-English.pdf

text.en:
Kobe Oser appears in a Dutch diplomatic record dated 6 February 1962 as a Papuan student association. The record describes a meeting initiated by the association with representatives of mission and church organisations. It places student organising alongside the political negotiations over West New Guinea, rather than beginning the diaspora’s history with the later ULMWP.

A Nationaal Archief photograph dated 9 May 1969 documents Kobe Oser members and supporters marching in The Hague and submitting petitions to the Dutch parliament and the US and Indonesian embassies. The catalogue describes it as the closing stage of a West Papua freedom march. PACE also preserves a catalogue entry for the association’s Kobe Oser Koerier periodical.

Students abroad could bring petitions directly to institutions that had participated in the territory’s transfer. The 1969 march linked public demonstration with appeals to Dutch, US and Indonesian officials before Pepera. A periodical gave the association another means to circulate arguments and maintain relationships across distance. These records place diaspora advocacy within the decolonisation process itself, showing that Papuans continued to demand a political choice from governments that had already negotiated their future. Sources: Document 4430: Kobe Oser meeting Huygens ING · Dutch diplomatic records · 6 February 1962 https://resources.huygens.knaw.nl/Nederlands-indonesischeBetrekkingen1950-1963/Document/19905; Kobe Oser freedom march in The Hague Nationaal Archief · 9 May 1969 · inventory 347035 https://www.nationaalarchief.nl/onderzoeken/fotocollectie/725d8844-4cb4-d2b8-99c1-2eb6cb2b1085; Kobe Oser Koerier Stichting Papua Erfgoed · catalogue https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/nl/BK/40/297
text.pmy:
Kobe Oser tercatat dalam dokumen diplomatik Belanda bertanggal 6 Februari 1962 sebagai perkumpulan mahasiswa Papua. Dokumen menguraikan pertemuan yang diprakarsai perkumpulan tersebut bersama wakil organisasi misi dan gereja. Catatan ini menempatkan kegiatan mahasiswa di tengah perundingan Nugini Barat, jauh sebelum pembentukan ULMWP.

Foto Nationaal Archief bertanggal 9 Mei 1969 mendokumentasikan anggota Kobe Oser serta pendukung yang berbaris di Den Haag dan menyampaikan petisi kepada parlemen Belanda serta kedutaan Amerika Serikat dan Indonesia. Katalog menyebutnya sebagai penutup suatu pawai kebebasan Papua Barat. PACE juga menyimpan entri katalog terbitan Kobe Oser Koerier dari perkumpulan ini.

Mahasiswa di luar negeri dapat menyampaikan petisi langsung kepada lembaga yang terlibat dalam penyerahan wilayah. Pawai 1969 menghubungkan demonstrasi dengan tuntutan kepada pejabat Belanda, Amerika Serikat dan Indonesia sebelum Pepera. Terbitan berkala memberi jalan lain untuk menyebarkan argumen serta menjaga hubungan lintas jarak. Catatan menempatkan advokasi diaspora dalam proses dekolonisasi sendiri: orang Papua terus menuntut pilihan politik dari pemerintah yang sudah merundingkan masa depannya. Sumber: Document 4430: Kobe Oser meeting Huygens ING · Dutch diplomatic records · 6 February 1962 https://resources.huygens.knaw.nl/Nederlands-indonesischeBetrekkingen1950-1963/Document/19905; Kobe Oser freedom march in The Hague Nationaal Archief · 9 May 1969 · inventory 347035 https://www.nationaalarchief.nl/onderzoeken/fotocollectie/725d8844-4cb4-d2b8-99c1-2eb6cb2b1085; Kobe Oser Koerier Stichting Papua Erfgoed · catalogue https://www.papuaerfgoed.org/nl/BK/40/297

title.pmy: Wasior: konsesi kayu dan operasi keamanan

text.en:
Violence in Wasior in June 2001 developed around a logging concession and the presence of Brimob. Disputes concerned company promises and relations with local communities. After five Brimob members and a civilian were killed on 13 June, security forces carried out operations that subjected residents to killings, torture and disappearances. The reprisals extended the conflict into civilian life rather than limiting the response to those responsible for the attack.

Komnas HAM investigated Wasior as an alleged gross human-rights violation. Survivors’ experiences joined the concession’s history with a demand for accountability over security operations. The case concerned the power exercised over communities living on land sought for extraction. Investigation files did not by themselves return missing people or compensate households for violence and displacement.

By 2016, the commission was resisting proposals to settle Wasior and Wamena only through a political approach, insisting that legal accountability remain part of the response. The unresolved route from investigation to prosecution prolonged the burden on survivors. Wasior’s record shows how the presence of security forces around commercial activity could produce civilian harm followed by a much longer struggle to have that harm recognised and prosecuted. Sources: Komnas HAM Tolak Pendekatan Politik dalam Selesaikan Kasus Wasior-Wamena VOA Indonesia · 2016 https://www.voaindonesia.com/a/komnas-ham-tolak-pendekatan-politik-kasus-wasior-wamena-/3305241.html; Tragedi Wasior Amnesty International Indonesia · 2022 https://www.amnesty.id/referensi-ham/artikel-ham/tragedi-wasior/06/2022/; Wasior and Wamena: the cases awaiting justice BBC Indonesia · 2017 https://www.bbc.com/indonesia/indonesia-39031020
text.pmy:
Kekerasan Wasior pada Juni 2001 berkembang di sekitar konsesi kayu dan kehadiran Brimob. Perselisihan menyangkut janji perusahaan serta hubungan dengan masyarakat. Setelah lima anggota Brimob dan seorang warga sipil tewas pada 13 Juni, aparat menjalankan operasi yang membawa pembunuhan, penyiksaan serta penghilangan kepada penduduk. Pembalasan memperluas konflik ke kehidupan sipil, bukan membatasi tindakan pada pelaku serangan.

Komnas HAM menyelidiki Wasior sebagai dugaan pelanggaran HAM berat. Pengalaman penyintas menghubungkan sejarah konsesi dengan tuntutan pertanggungjawaban operasi keamanan. Perkara menyangkut kuasa atas masyarakat di tanah yang dicari untuk pengambilan sumber daya. Berkas penyelidikan belum dengan sendirinya mengembalikan orang hilang atau memulihkan keluarga yang mengalami kekerasan dan pengungsian.

Pada 2016, komisi menolak usulan penyelesaian Wasior dan Wamena hanya melalui pendekatan politik serta menuntut pertanggungjawaban hukum tetap dijalankan. Jalan dari penyelidikan ke penuntutan yang belum selesai memperpanjang beban penyintas. Catatan Wasior menunjukkan bagaimana kehadiran aparat di sekitar usaha komersial membawa kekerasan sipil, diikuti perjuangan jauh lebih panjang untuk memperoleh pengakuan dan penuntutan. Sumber: Komnas HAM Tolak Pendekatan Politik dalam Selesaikan Kasus Wasior-Wamena VOA Indonesia · 2016 https://www.voaindonesia.com/a/komnas-ham-tolak-pendekatan-politik-kasus-wasior-wamena-/3305241.html; Tragedi Wasior Amnesty International Indonesia · 2022 https://www.amnesty.id/referensi-ham/artikel-ham/tragedi-wasior/06/2022/; Wasior and Wamena: the cases awaiting justice BBC Indonesia · 2017 https://www.bbc.com/indonesia/indonesia-39031020

text.en:
Rumah Sakit Mitra Masyarakat in Timika developed through cooperation between Freeport Indonesia, the local community development institution, the Mimika government and the Catholic diocese. Its institutional history places medical services within the changing mining region, where communities also organised over land and environmental harm.

The hospital’s public history and the LPMAK sustainability report document the role of community development funding and service institutions. LPMAK’s transition to YPMAK in 2019 changed the organisational arrangement. These records help trace access to care and institutional responsibilities; they do not by themselves establish that environmental claims against mining were resolved.

The hospital began serving the region in 1999. Its partnership brought clinical care into a landscape where mining-related migration and changes in settlement had increased demands on services. Community development funds linked health provision with decisions about who represented the Amungme and Kamoro and how resources were managed. The 2019 institutional transition retained that relationship between care and collective funding. Hospitals and referral services became another arena in which local people sought practical benefits and accountable institutions. Sources: About Rumah Sakit Mitra Masyarakat RSMM · institutional history https://rsmitramasyarakat.com/artikel/about/; LPMAK Sustainability Report 2019 LPMAK / YPMAK · 2019 https://www.ypmak.or.id/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/SR-LPMAK-2019_Final-Kecil.pdf
text.pmy:
Rumah Sakit Mitra Masyarakat di Timika berkembang melalui kerja sama Freeport Indonesia, lembaga pengembangan masyarakat setempat, pemerintah Mimika, dan keuskupan Katolik. Riwayat kelembagaannya menempatkan layanan medis dalam kawasan pertambangan yang berubah, sementara masyarakat juga berorganisasi mengenai tanah serta kerusakan lingkungan.

Riwayat publik rumah sakit serta laporan keberlanjutan LPMAK mencatat peran dana pengembangan masyarakat dan lembaga layanan. Peralihan LPMAK menjadi YPMAK pada 2019 mengubah pengaturan organisasinya. Catatan ini membantu menelusuri akses perawatan dan tanggung jawab lembaga; keberadaan layanan tersebut tidak dengan sendirinya menyelesaikan tuntutan lingkungan terhadap pertambangan.

Rumah sakit mulai melayani wilayah ini pada 1999. Kemitraannya membawa layanan klinis ke kawasan dengan migrasi terkait tambang serta perubahan permukiman yang meningkatkan kebutuhan pelayanan. Dana pengembangan masyarakat menghubungkan kesehatan dengan keputusan tentang perwakilan Amungme dan Kamoro serta pengelolaan sumber daya. Perubahan kelembagaan pada 2019 tetap membawa hubungan antara perawatan dan pendanaan bersama. Rumah sakit serta layanan rujukan menjadi ruang lain bagi masyarakat untuk memperoleh manfaat nyata dan lembaga yang bertanggung jawab. Sumber: About Rumah Sakit Mitra Masyarakat RSMM · institutional history https://rsmitramasyarakat.com/artikel/about/; LPMAK Sustainability Report 2019 LPMAK / YPMAK · 2019 https://www.ypmak.or.id/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/SR-LPMAK-2019_Final-Kecil.pdf

text.en:
Military operations around Timika in 1994–1995 subjected Amungme communities to killings, detention, torture and disappearances. Reports by the Catholic Church brought testimony from the mining region into public view. The National Human Rights Commission subsequently confirmed serious abuses; Amnesty’s September 1995 account records its findings of 16 extrajudicial executions and four disappearances.

One incident concerned a prayer gathering at Hoea on 31 May 1995. The church report described soldiers shooting civilians, including children and church worker Martinus Kibak. The events formed part of a wider pattern in which suspected links with independence fighters became grounds for violence against villagers. People living around a major mine faced security forces whose operations could reach homes, gatherings and everyday community life.

The commission’s acknowledgement challenged official denials but did not itself provide criminal accountability or restore missing relatives. Amnesty pressed for independent investigation and prosecution. The case connects the region’s land struggle with demands for physical safety and truth: church documentation and community organising made abuses visible where military power and economic development were closely intertwined. Sources: Irian Jaya: National Commission confirms violations Amnesty International · 1995 https://www.amnesty.org/en/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/asa210471995en.pdf
text.pmy:
Operasi militer di sekitar Timika pada 1994–1995 membawa pembunuhan, penahanan, penyiksaan serta penghilangan kepada masyarakat Amungme. Laporan Gereja Katolik menyampaikan kesaksian dari wilayah tambang kepada publik. Komnas HAM kemudian mengonfirmasi pelanggaran serius. Catatan Amnesty September 1995 memuat temuan komisi berupa 16 eksekusi di luar hukum dan empat penghilangan.

Salah satu kejadian berlangsung pada pertemuan doa di Hoea, 31 Mei 1995. Laporan gereja menggambarkan tentara menembaki warga, termasuk anak-anak dan pekerja gereja Martinus Kibak. Kejadian berada dalam pola lebih luas ketika dugaan hubungan dengan pejuang kemerdekaan dijadikan alasan kekerasan terhadap warga kampung. Masyarakat di sekitar tambang besar menghadapi aparat yang operasinya menjangkau rumah, pertemuan dan kehidupan sehari-hari.

Pengakuan komisi menantang penyangkalan resmi, tetapi belum dengan sendirinya menghasilkan pertanggungjawaban pidana atau mengembalikan kerabat yang hilang. Amnesty menuntut penyelidikan mandiri serta penuntutan. Perkara menghubungkan perjuangan tanah dengan keselamatan dan kebenaran. Dokumentasi gereja serta pengorganisasian masyarakat mengungkap pelanggaran di wilayah tempat kekuatan militer dan pembangunan ekonomi saling terkait erat. Sumber: Irian Jaya: National Commission confirms violations Amnesty International · 1995 https://www.amnesty.org/en/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/asa210471995en.pdf

text.en:
In January 1996, an OPM unit led by Kelly Kwalik took members of a scientific expedition hostage in Mapenduma. Church workers and the International Committee of the Red Cross participated in negotiations. A Kopassus operation under Prabowo Subianto followed in May. Nine remaining hostages were recovered on 15 May; two Indonesian hostages died during the final phase. The hostage crisis brought international attention to the highlands, while the experience of villagers received much less notice.

A separate attack at Geselema on 9 May became the subject of later investigation. Mark Davis recorded villagers’ accounts of gunmen arriving in a white helicopter associated with the relief visits people expected. Le Temps reported that an inquiry commissioned by the ICRC confirmed deception involving the familiar helicopter and the deaths of eight civilians. The inquiry cleared ICRC personnel of involvement. The attack must be distinguished from the subsequent hostage rescue.

Using the appearance of humanitarian assistance turned the expectation of a safe encounter into exposure to violence. Villagers’ testimony complicated the official account of a successful rescue, raising questions about civilian deaths and the protection of relief work. Prabowo’s command of the operation is documented; the identity and individual orders of every gunman are not established by that fact alone. The surviving record includes both the hostages’ ordeal and the civilians whose deaths were obscured by the rescue narrative. Sources: Blood on the cross Mark Davis · Pacific Journalism Review · 2000 https://ojs.aut.ac.nz/pacific-journalism-review/article/view/665; Trahi par l’armée indonésienne, le CICR demande des comptes Le Temps · 15 March 2000 https://www.letemps.ch/monde/trahi-larmee-indonesienne-cicr-demande-comptes; Hostage watched as two friends were killed The Independent · 17 May 1996 https://www.independent.co.uk/news/hostage-watched-as-two-friends-were-killed-1347695.html
text.pmy:
Pada Januari 1996, pasukan OPM pimpinan Kelly Kwalik menyandera anggota ekspedisi ilmiah di Mapenduma. Pekerja gereja serta Komite Internasional Palang Merah ikut berunding. Operasi Kopassus di bawah Prabowo Subianto berlangsung pada Mei. Sembilan sandera yang tersisa dibebaskan pada 15 Mei; dua sandera Indonesia meninggal pada tahap akhir. Krisis menarik perhatian internasional ke pegunungan, sementara pengalaman warga kampung jauh kurang diperhatikan.

Serangan tersendiri di Geselema pada 9 Mei menjadi sasaran penyelidikan berikutnya. Mark Davis merekam kesaksian warga tentang orang bersenjata yang tiba dengan helikopter putih yang mereka kenal dari kunjungan bantuan. Le Temps melaporkan bahwa penyelidikan yang ditugaskan ICRC mengonfirmasi penyamaran menggunakan helikopter yang dikenal serta kematian delapan warga sipil. Penyelidikan menyatakan petugas ICRC tidak terlibat. Serangan ini berbeda dari pembebasan sandera yang berlangsung kemudian.

Menggunakan penampilan bantuan kemanusiaan mengubah harapan pertemuan aman menjadi bahaya kekerasan. Kesaksian warga menantang gambaran resmi pembebasan yang berhasil dan mengangkat kematian sipil serta perlindungan kerja bantuan. Kepemimpinan Prabowo dalam operasi terdokumentasi; identitas dan perintah setiap penembak tidak otomatis terbukti dari fakta tersebut. Catatan yang tersisa mencakup penderitaan sandera sekaligus warga yang kematiannya tertutup kisah pembebasan. Sumber: Blood on the cross Mark Davis · Pacific Journalism Review · 2000 https://ojs.aut.ac.nz/pacific-journalism-review/article/view/665; Trahi par l’armée indonésienne, le CICR demande des comptes Le Temps · 15 March 2000 https://www.letemps.ch/monde/trahi-larmee-indonesienne-cicr-demande-comptes; Hostage watched as two friends were killed The Independent · 17 May 1996 https://www.independent.co.uk/news/hostage-watched-as-two-friends-were-killed-1347695.html

text.en:
After Suharto fell in May 1998, demands for independence were voiced more openly in Papua. On 2 July, the Morning Star flag flew from the water tower near Biak's harbour. Residents gathered, sang and made political demands. Filep Karma became a leading figure in the gathering. Security officers asked for the flag to be lowered, but participants maintained it.

At around five in the morning on 6 July, troops attacked from several directions and fired on the crowd. Human Rights Watch recorded testimony that people were shot while already lying on the ground. After the attack, residents were arrested, beaten and taken into detention. Wounded people faced restrictions on hospital access; some bodies were not returned to their families.

ELSHAM, working with church networks, documented eight people killed, three missing, dozens injured and detentions. Its report separately recorded 32 unidentified bodies found in Biak's waters. Families were left without certainty as bodies were withheld and missing relatives remained unaccounted for. Authorities attributed the bodies at sea to the tsunami in Papua New Guinea; local testimony about violence in Biak prompted demands for further investigation.

Biak showed that the political opening after Suharto was accompanied by continuing violence against Papuan independence demands. In its 1999 report, ELSHAM called for intimidation of families to end, disappearances to be investigated and perpetrators to be brought to justice. Families and survivors faced a struggle for recognition of what happened alongside the search for relatives they had lost. Sources: Biak: the flag-raising and military attack Human Rights Watch · 1998 https://www.hrw.org/legacy/reports/reports98/biak/biak.htm; Names Without Graves ELSHAM Papua & church investigators · 1999 https://www.biak-tribunal.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/Names-Without-Graves_Elsham-Papua-English.pdf; Bodies found at sea Human Rights Watch · 1998 https://www.hrw.org/legacy/reports/reports98/biak/bodies.htm
text.pmy:
Setelah Suharto jatuh pada Mei 1998, tuntutan kemerdekaan disampaikan lebih terbuka di Papua. Pada 2 Juli, Bintang Kejora berkibar di menara air dekat pelabuhan Biak. Warga berkumpul, menyanyi dan menyampaikan tuntutan politik. Filep Karma menjadi salah satu tokoh utama perkumpulan itu. Aparat meminta bendera diturunkan, tetapi warga mempertahankannya.

Sekitar pukul lima pagi pada 6 Juli, pasukan menyerang dari beberapa arah dan menembaki warga. Human Rights Watch mencatat kesaksian tentang orang yang ditembak ketika sudah terbaring di tanah. Setelah serangan, warga ditangkap, dipukuli dan dibawa untuk ditahan. Korban luka menghadapi pembatasan akses rumah sakit; sejumlah jenazah tidak diserahkan kembali kepada keluarga.

ELSHAM bersama jaringan gereja mendokumentasikan delapan orang tewas, tiga orang hilang, puluhan orang luka dan penahanan. Laporan itu juga mencatat 32 jenazah tak dikenal yang ditemukan di perairan Biak. Keluarga yang kehilangan kerabat menghadapi ketidakpastian karena tubuh tidak dikembalikan dan orang hilang tidak ditemukan. Aparat mengaitkan jenazah di laut dengan tsunami di Papua Nugini; kesaksian warga mengenai kekerasan di Biak mendorong tuntutan penyelidikan lebih jauh.

Biak memperlihatkan bahwa pembukaan ruang politik setelah Suharto tetap disertai kekerasan terhadap tuntutan kemerdekaan Papua. Dalam laporan 1999, ELSHAM meminta intimidasi terhadap keluarga dihentikan, penghilangan diungkap dan pelaku kekerasan diproses. Keluarga dan penyintas harus memperjuangkan pengakuan atas apa yang terjadi sekaligus mencari kepastian mengenai orang-orang yang mereka kehilangan. Sumber: Biak: the flag-raising and military attack Human Rights Watch · 1998 https://www.hrw.org/legacy/reports/reports98/biak/biak.htm; Names Without Graves ELSHAM Papua & church investigators · 1999 https://www.biak-tribunal.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/09/Names-Without-Graves_Elsham-Papua-English.pdf; Bodies found at sea Human Rights Watch · 1998 https://www.hrw.org/legacy/reports/reports98/biak/bodies.htm

text.en:
After an attack on a police post in Abepura on 7 December 2000, police and Brimob raided student dormitories and nearby settlements. Human Rights Watch documented that Ninmin dormitory students had refused an earlier request to join the attackers. They were nevertheless beaten and detained in the reprisals. The response treated students and residents as targets without establishing their involvement in the original attack.

The investigation recorded more than a hundred people subjected to torture and ill-treatment, with two deaths in custody and another killing during the raids. Beatings and degrading treatment extended beyond the moment of arrest. For students, a place of study and residence became a place of violence. Families and survivors then had to pursue an account of the deaths against institutions whose officers had carried out the operation.

The case reached the Human Rights Court, but the two senior police defendants were acquitted in 2005. Amnesty criticised the proceedings for failing to provide justice and compensation to victims. The trial’s outcome left a gap between the documented treatment of detainees and accountability for those responsible. Abepura became an important example of how bringing a case to a special court did not guarantee a remedy for Papuan survivors. Sources: The Abepura case Human Rights Watch · 2001 https://www.hrw.org/reports/2001/papua/PAPUA0701-05.htm; Justice denied for the victims of Abepura Amnesty International · 2005 https://www.amnesty.org/en/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/asa210182005en.pdf
text.pmy:
Setelah serangan pos polisi di Abepura pada 7 Desember 2000, polisi dan Brimob menyerbu asrama mahasiswa serta permukiman sekitar. Human Rights Watch mencatat mahasiswa Asrama Ninmin sebelumnya menolak ajakan bergabung dengan penyerang. Mereka tetap dipukuli dan ditahan dalam pembalasan. Tanggapan menjadikan mahasiswa serta warga sasaran tanpa membuktikan keterlibatan mereka dalam serangan awal.

Penyelidikan mencatat lebih dari seratus orang mengalami penyiksaan serta perlakuan buruk, dengan dua kematian dalam tahanan dan satu pembunuhan lain saat penyerbuan. Pemukulan serta penghinaan berlanjut setelah penangkapan. Bagi mahasiswa, tempat belajar dan tinggal berubah menjadi tempat kekerasan. Keluarga serta penyintas harus mencari penjelasan atas kematian dari lembaga yang petugasnya menjalankan operasi.

Perkara sampai ke Pengadilan HAM, tetapi dua terdakwa pejabat polisi dibebaskan pada 2005. Amnesty mengkritik proses yang tidak memberikan keadilan serta ganti rugi kepada korban. Hasil persidangan menyisakan jarak antara perlakuan terhadap tahanan yang terdokumentasi dan pertanggungjawaban pelaku. Abepura menjadi contoh penting bahwa membawa perkara ke pengadilan khusus belum menjamin pemulihan bagi penyintas Papua. Sumber: The Abepura case Human Rights Watch · 2001 https://www.hrw.org/reports/2001/papua/PAPUA0701-05.htm; Justice denied for the victims of Abepura Amnesty International · 2005 https://www.amnesty.org/en/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/asa210182005en.pdf

text.en:
Theys Hiyo Eluay, chairman of the Papuan Presidium Council, was killed after attending a Kopassus event on 10 November 2001. His leadership had become prominent during the public mobilisation and Congress that followed Suharto’s fall. The killing removed a leading representative of the independence demand at a moment when Jakarta was introducing special autonomy.

In April 2003, a military tribunal convicted seven Kopassus soldiers. Lieutenant Colonel Hartomo received a sentence of three and a half years. The convictions established responsibility among members of the unit, but the short sentences drew criticism. The court outcome belongs alongside the political loss: a trial of soldiers did not restore the public leadership that had been attacked.

For the movement, the murder made the limits of the Reformasi opening unmistakable. An independence leader could participate in public political life and still be killed by soldiers. It deepened the problem of trust surrounding the government’s new institutional offer. The history of autonomy therefore cannot be separated from the violence against the people whose demands it was meant to answer. Sources: Kopassus troops jailed over Papua leader’s murder ABC News · 21 April 2003 https://www.abc.net.au/news/2003-04-21/kopassus-troops-jailed-over-papua-leaders-murder/1840650
text.pmy:
Theys Hiyo Eluay, ketua Presidium Dewan Papua, dibunuh setelah menghadiri acara Kopassus pada 10 November 2001. Kepemimpinannya menonjol dalam pengorganisasian publik serta kongres setelah jatuhnya Suharto. Pembunuhan menyingkirkan wakil utama tuntutan kemerdekaan ketika Jakarta memberlakukan otonomi khusus.

Pada April 2003, pengadilan militer menghukum tujuh prajurit Kopassus. Letnan Kolonel Hartomo menerima hukuman tiga setengah tahun. Putusan menetapkan tanggung jawab anggota satuan, tetapi hukuman singkat mendapat kritik. Hasil pengadilan juga harus dibaca bersama kehilangan politik: persidangan prajurit tidak mengembalikan kepemimpinan publik yang diserang.

Bagi gerakan, pembunuhan memperjelas batas pembukaan Reformasi. Pemimpin kemerdekaan dapat berperan dalam kehidupan politik publik dan tetap dibunuh tentara. Peristiwa memperdalam persoalan kepercayaan terhadap tawaran kelembagaan pemerintah. Sejarah otonomi karena itu tidak terpisah dari kekerasan terhadap orang yang tuntutannya hendak dijawab. Sumber: Kopassus troops jailed over Papua leader’s murder ABC News · 21 April 2003 https://www.abc.net.au/news/2003-04-21/kopassus-troops-jailed-over-papua-leaders-murder/1840650

text.en:
After a raid on a military weapons store in Wamena on 4 April 2003, the army conducted sweeping operations across nearby communities. Investigations described operations reaching 25 villages. Residents faced violence and fled their homes, turning the response to an attack on a military facility into a crisis for families across the surrounding area.

Flight separated people from gardens, shelter and services. Deaths attributed to hunger after displacement show that the consequences continued beyond direct killings and injuries. Reaching safety from soldiers did not ensure access to food or medical care. The village became a place people could no longer safely inhabit, and return required more than the end of the initial raid.

Komnas HAM investigated Wamena together with Wasior as alleged gross violations and pressed for legal accountability. Years of disagreement over the investigation and prosecution prolonged uncertainty for survivors. The record links military reprisals with the destruction of conditions needed for ordinary life, making displacement and its deaths part of the case rather than an incidental aftermath. Sources: Wasior and Wamena: the cases awaiting justice BBC Indonesia · 2017 https://www.bbc.com/indonesia/indonesia-39031020; Komnas HAM rejects a solely political settlement VOA Indonesia · 2016 https://www.voaindonesia.com/a/komnas-ham-tolak-pendekatan-politik-kasus-wasior-wamena-/3305241.html
text.pmy:
Setelah serangan gudang senjata militer di Wamena pada 4 April 2003, tentara melakukan penyisiran di masyarakat sekitar. Penyelidikan menggambarkan operasi yang menjangkau 25 kampung. Warga menghadapi kekerasan serta meninggalkan rumah, sehingga tanggapan terhadap serangan fasilitas militer berubah menjadi krisis keluarga di wilayah sekitarnya.

Pelarian memisahkan warga dari kebun, tempat tinggal serta layanan. Kematian akibat kelaparan setelah pengungsian menunjukkan bahwa akibat berlanjut melampaui pembunuhan dan luka langsung. Selamat dari tentara belum memastikan pangan atau perawatan. Kampung menjadi tempat yang tidak aman untuk dihuni, dan kepulangan memerlukan lebih dari berakhirnya serangan awal.

Komnas HAM menyelidiki Wamena bersama Wasior sebagai dugaan pelanggaran berat serta mendesak pertanggungjawaban hukum. Perselisihan bertahun-tahun mengenai penyelidikan dan penuntutan memperpanjang ketidakpastian penyintas. Catatan menghubungkan pembalasan militer dengan rusaknya kondisi kehidupan sehari-hari. Pengungsian serta kematian yang mengikutinya merupakan bagian perkara, bukan akibat sampingan. Sumber: Wasior and Wamena: the cases awaiting justice BBC Indonesia · 2017 https://www.bbc.com/indonesia/indonesia-39031020; Komnas HAM rejects a solely political settlement VOA Indonesia · 2016 https://www.voaindonesia.com/a/komnas-ham-tolak-pendekatan-politik-kasus-wasior-wamena-/3305241.html

text.en:
The killing of road construction workers by TPNPB independence fighters in December 2018 was followed by Indonesian military operations in Nduga. The road project had become part of a conflict over the state’s presence in the highlands. Families living near the operations fled, including children who had no part in the attack. A UN communication relayed allegations of ground and aerial attacks and asked Indonesia to respond.

Reporting in June 2019 followed displaced children and families living away from their villages. Fear, interrupted schooling and difficulty obtaining food made the crisis extend beyond clashes between fighters. People who fled to forests or other settlements lost access to the gardens and relationships that sustained them at home. Relief workers and teachers tried to maintain support while safety and access remained uncertain.

Nduga made civilian displacement a central issue in the later highland conflict. A military operation presented as restoring security could leave communities unable to return or resume ordinary life. The UN correspondence records allegations requiring answers rather than a completed investigation, while reporting from displaced families supplies the daily experience behind them. Food, schooling and safe return became urgent demands alongside accountability for direct violence. Sources: Communication to Indonesia concerning Nduga UN Special Procedures · 2019 https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadPublicCommunicationFile?gId=24508; Frightened and displaced: Papua children haunted by conflict Al Jazeera · 5 June 2019 https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/6/5/frightened-and-displaced-papua-children-haunted-by-conflict
text.pmy:
Pembunuhan pekerja pembangunan jalan oleh pejuang kemerdekaan TPNPB pada Desember 2018 diikuti operasi militer Indonesia di Nduga.
